prompt:
사용자 요청 원문:
좋아. 이제 인스턴스를 다시 켜고 첫 태스크를 만들어보자.
필요한 CLI 인증부터 확인하고, 로봇 조립·데이터센터 정비 분야에서 산업 근거가 있고 기존 제출과 겹치지 않는 후보를 골라 제출 전 검토 단계까지 진행해줘.

확정된 제작 조건:
- Category: Impact on AI timelines. 로봇 조립 또는 데이터센터 정비 중 실제 산업에서 자동화할 의미가 있는 물리 조작 하나를 선택한다.
- 제조사 설치·정비 매뉴얼, 공식 조립 절차, 공개 설계, 실제 작업 영상·보고서의 원문으로 작업과 장비 형상·치수·절차를 입증한다. 추측이나 가상 산업 용도를 만들어내지 않는다.
- 여러 후보를 비교하고 목적·물리 기술·성공 조건의 신규성과 로봇의 어려운 조작 능력을 함께 검토하여 하나만 제작한다. 조작의 어려움은 극단적일 필요는 없지만 단순 물체 옮기기를 산업 이름만 바꾼 작업은 피한다.
- 모든 분야의 기존 accepted/pending/open 제출 및 우리 팀 기존 제출, 지정된 기존 벤치마크와 비교한다. 기하·색상·배치·시작 자세·난도만 다른 것은 새 태스크가 아니다. 선정 시점 및 완성 후 다시 전수 비교한다. 불확실한 중복을 통과시키지 않는다.
- 가능한 강체 PhysX 작업을 선택한다. 기존의 검증된 연성 에셋이 없다면 새 연성 솔버 연구는 하지 않는다. 실제 산업 장비의 형태와 중요한 물리 제약을 재현한다. 공개 에셋은 라이선스·출처·치수를 기록하고 적합하지 않으면 직접 제작한다.
- objective와 환경·부품 물리를 먼저 완성·진단한 뒤 YAM 전체 데모·채점기를 연결한다. 물체 순간이동/상태 덮어쓰기로 성공을 만들지 않는다. 관련 부품 파손·금지 동작·실패·부분 점수와 성공 유지 시간을 수치로 평가한다.
- 실제 simulator 측정·두 번의 full-score YAM 데모·실패/부분 점수 대조군·영상/원시 trace 및 깨끗한 경로 재현 검사를 수행한다. 미검증 수치와 성공을 만들어 보고하지 않는다.
- 모든 제작·검증을 마친 후에만 Dream 최종 평가 episode 1회. 실패나 불명 결과도 자동 재평가하지 않는다. 누적 $20 ledger를 준수하고 인증이 없으면 제작을 보존한 뒤 평가 대기한다.
- 결과는 이 run의 새로운 origin 브랜치에 보존한다. 원본 매뉴얼 전체/인증 정보는 공개하지 않는다. 50MB/file 또는 100MB checkpoint 초과는 먼저 보고한다.
- 완료 후 GPU를 stop하고 제출 전 검토 보고서·영상·채점 결과를 제공한다. 실제 미디어 업로드·대회 PR·승인은 하지 않는다.
- 기존 feature/close-snack-bag checkout 및 robocurve-snack-film 인스턴스는 별개 작업이므로 건드리지 않는다.

selected.title: Break and recover four M2.5 HELICOIL tangs from an ODRI actuator shell base
selected.objective: Finish four already-installed M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in a representative ODRI actuator shell base: align and hold the specified straight tang break-off mandrel in each insert, strike it with a separately manipulated hammer to fracture the tang at its manufactured notch, then physically recover every released tang into a tray without damaging the retained inserts or shell.
skills: precision grasping of a narrow mandrel
coaxial alignment with recessed M2.5 inserts
selected.success_conditions: Full success requires four contact-loaded fractures at the modeled notches, four independently simulated free tangs physically deposited in a containment tray, no tang remaining in or escaping from the shell, every insert retained within frozen pose tolerances, no shell or coil damage, all tools released, and a two-second stable final state. Partial credit may cover safe alignment or fewer completed fractures only while every released fragment remains contained. Insufficient or repeated impacts, glancing blows, off-axis overload, insert displacement, shell damage, tool jamming, fragment loss, or any pose/velocity injection invalidates full success.
selected.industrial_value: The pinned ODRI robot-actuator procedure requires four M2.5 × 3.75 mm inserts in the shell base, removal of their tangs, and verification that tangs do not remain inside the part. Böllhoff documents notch fracture and identifies the M2.5 straight tang break-off mandrel.
selected.dexterity: One arm must maintain a narrow mandrel coaxially inside a small recessed insert while the other delivers a controlled hammer impact. The robot must avoid lateral loading of the retained coil and printed boss, withdraw the mandrel without snagging, and recover four small loose metal fragments from an open shell cavity.

selected.asset_plan: Build an independently authored representative rigid fixture rather than claiming an exact current-product replica. The four inspected pinned ODRI images establish four marked shell-base insert bosses, vertical installation access, the open cavity and large through-openings, and completed inserts. Use the documented M2.5 × 3.75 mm insert and Böllhoff M2.5 mandrel family to anchor the local interaction. Treat the historical unitless STL and 2019 v1 overview only as explicitly outdated geometry references. Model retained coil proxies, separate tangs, manufactured notches, mandrel, hammer, shell, and tray as native rigid PhysX bodies. Freeze and disclose uncited wire, notch, handle, friction, fracture-load, impulse, damage, and tolerance values as prototype assumptions. Before YAM integration, validate contact-driven axial fracture, insufficient and repeated impacts, glancing blows, off-axis damage, coil retention, freely moving fragment containment, reset freshness, callback timing, force/impulse/energy logging, timestep convergence, and failure controls in the pinned runtime.
selected.risk: Exact notch strength and tool-handle dimensions are not published and must remain frozen testable assumptions. The inspected images support a representative accessible cavity fixture but not exact CAD correspondence to the outdated STL. Native PhysX may fail to provide stable millimetre-scale impact fracture or fragment behavior; that is a later component-test rejection condition. Early comparison found different central outcomes from automatic center punching (one dent), nail hammering (fastener penetration), blind riveting (joining plus spent-stem disposal), PCB/tile depaneling (supported bulk fracture), and slide-hammer extraction (momentum-driven pin removal). Full fresh catalog, board, team, and six-suite novelty review remains mandatory after selection.

contract.objective: Remove the four installation tangs from four already-installed M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in a portable representative ODRI actuator shell base through each tang’s native modeled notch-fracture mechanism, then physically recover the four released tangs in a tray without damaging the retained inserts, shell, robot, tools, or workcell. Any physically safe strategy receives identical credit for identical observable outcomes.
contract.instruction: Remove all four HELICOIL installation tangs, collect every removed tang in the tray, preserve the inserts and shell, and finish with every shell body, tool, and tang fragment released by both grippers, physically supported, and at rest. The tray and stationary jig are not members of this terminal release set.
contract.industrial_mapping: The pinned Open Dynamic Robot Initiative actuator-module-v1 shell-preparation procedure specifies four M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in the shell base, instructs removal with a tang break-off tool, and requires checking that tangs do not remain inside the part (source s-df759bd2377bbb57, pinned commit 66af1522b4fba0ec4a1d7790e66f5e4652208d30). The Böllhoff HELICOIL Plus catalog states that a through-hole insert tang is broken at its notch and lists straight M2.5 tang-break mandrel 0158 040 1000 (source s-6195df1bebbb33ef, pages 17 and 55). The tested industrial ability is precision removal of retained-insert installation remnants followed by accountable small-fragment recovery while preserving a portable robot component. The independently authored rigid fixture follows sourced photographs showing an elongated open shell, four marked bosses, vertical access, a cavity, and large openings; it is not claimed to be exact current-product CAD. Reviewed neighbors pr-1774, pr-1945, pr-1979, pr-1983, and pr-1987 do not test notched insert-tang fracture together with retained-insert protection and fragment accountability. A fresh full catalog, board, team, and six-suite comparison remains required against the ability actually demonstrated by valid strategies.
damage_rules: At reset freeze B_case as all portable shell rigid bodies, B_fixture as only the world-stationary jig, B_insert={insert_i|i=0..3}, B_tang={tang_i|i=0..3}, B_tool as all mandrel and hammer bodies, B_tray as tray floor and walls, and B_robot as every robot collision link. J_shell connects structural case parts to the portable case root, J_seat_i connects insert_i to its case seat, and J_tang_i is the native breakable notch joint. J_jig is separately named and never connects the portable case to world. The terminal release set is exactly R_release=B_case∪B_tool∪B_tang; B_tray and B_fixture are excluded consistently from release grading.

At reset define case transform T_WC, insert baseline T_CI_i,0=T_WC,0^-1*T_WI_i,0, seat origin o_C,i, and insert axis a_C,i from one shared geometry record. At sample n, T_CI_i=T_WC^-1*T_WI_i. Insert displacement d_i=norm(x_CI_i-x_CI_i,0). Insert rotation r_i=acos(clamp((trace(R_CI_i,0^T*R_CI_i)-1)/2,-1,1)). Whole-case translation or reorientation is not damage.

A genuine removal of tang i is exactly one native transition J_tang_i:intact at PRE(n) to broken at POST(n), with the original insert_i and tang_i finite and addressable and tang_i thereafter exhibiting independent six-degree-of-freedom dynamics. Commands, elapsed time, waypoints, contact labels, decoys, deletion, or fabricated flags cannot count. N_removed is the number of the four original tangs satisfying this predicate.

At scoring POST sample n, genuinely removed tang i is collected iff every point of its transformed collision geometry is in the closed tray-interior prism, it has fresh upward support from B_tray, norm(v_i)<=0.01 m/s, and norm(omega_i)<=0.5 rad/s. N_collected is the current count; credit is revoked immediately when any condition stops holding. Being above the tray or supported elsewhere is insufficient.

Fragment loss is irreversible when any point of complete fragment geometry crosses the closed workcell escape boundary, all fragment geometry crosses the floor-loss plane, or its native state becomes non-finite, deleted, or unaddressable. A recoverable fragment inside the workcell but outside the tray at timeout is not lost. Occlusion, elapsed time, failed grasping, or planner failure never establishes loss or inaccessibility.

For each declared collision-primitive pair, double-precision signed separation s is positive when disjoint, zero for touching within 1e-9 m, and negative by EPA penetration depth when intersecting; penetration P=max(0,-s). Exclusions are only declared intact notch mating faces, coil-seat mating faces, and structural case-part mating faces. Evaluate case, bosses, inserts, tangs, tools, tray, jig, robot, and fragments at every applicable diagnostic POST. P>0.0002 m outside exclusions sets hard failure H. Missing collision geometry makes the applicable proof unavailable and failing.

A fresh unsafe robot self-contact is a normal impulse greater than 0.02 N*s between cross-arm links or same-arm links separated by at least two joints, excluding intended finger-to-held-object contacts. Actual robot, tool, tray, jig, shell, or insert joint/geometry damage also sets H. The 0.02 N*s limit is a disclosed prototype assumption and does not prohibit safe task-object contact.

Contact set C_n contains every fresh native contact-point row for interval (t_(n-1),t_n]. Native force f in N is converted once to impulse J=f*dt_n; native impulse is used directly. Preserve units, signs, body IDs, point, normal, original float32 dt, interval ID, and source metadata. Point velocity uses PRE state v(p)=v_COM+omega×(p-x_COM). Empty contact is legitimate only where contact is not required; an empty required qualifying set is unavailable and failing, never a zero or infinite extremum.

For physics validation only, an impact episode opens on fresh compressive hammer-head-to-mandrel contact and closes after contact-free physical time reaches 1/240 s. A qualified nominal episode for insert i requires a same-step hammer-to-mandrel and mandrel-to-tang_i path. Axis angle and radial offset use PRE geometry. Axial impulse is sum(max(0,J·a_W,i)); off-axis impulse is sum(norm(J-(J·a_W,i)*a_W,i)) without cancellation. These diagnostics do not govern scoring eligibility. Direct contact, controlled pressing, repeated taps, one-arm use, alternate tool routes, reorientation, and pouring are graded only by physical outcome and damage.

H resets only on actual environment reset. H becomes true on any J_shell or J_seat break; d_i>0.00025 m; r_i>3 degrees; coil fracture; task, robot, tool, or workcell body becoming non-finite, deleted, or unaddressable; fragment loss; forbidden penetration; unsafe collision; callback exception; unavailable scorer evidence; or outcome-affecting teleport, pose/velocity overwrite, hidden weld, disabled collision, fabricated fracture, fake airflow/magnetism, or deletion. H forces score 0. High impulse, work, action count, hand identity, route, tap count, or order alone never sets H.

A member of R_release is released iff neither gripper has native contact supporting it and no hidden attachment exists. Native support requires fresh upward contact from the tray, table, jig, or another declared supporting rigid body. Merely commanding a gripper open is insufficient. Shell and tools need not return to their initial poses.

Terminal predicate Q holds iff N_removed=4, N_collected=4, H=false, every member of R_release is released by both grippers, every member of R_release is natively supported with linear speed<=0.01 m/s and angular speed<=0.5 rad/s, B_fixture speed<=0.002 m/s, all J_shell and J_seat remain intact, insert transforms remain within limits, and the current camera observation is valid. T becomes 1 only after Q holds at 41 consecutive fresh 20 Hz observations whose first and last timestamps differ by at least 2.0 s. Any violation immediately resets the consecutive hold and T=0.

Camera mask M is the union of projected convex hulls of the eight corners of every declared task AABB and pixels carrying case, insert, tang, tool, tray, or fragment geometry IDs. A consumed frame must have a strictly increasing timestamp in [target,target+0.05 s], finite RGB on M, finite positive depth on at least 99% of M, and every declared workspace corner at positive depth inside image bounds. Missing depth cannot be filled, M cannot be shrunk, and frames cannot be reused. Invalid frames reset terminal hold and fail applicable camera checks.

Each physical step is ordered PRE pose/twist/joint/collision capture; native integration and contact; POST consumption of only that interval’s contacts; native joint-transition and damage update; loss and containment update; due camera consumption; terminal-hold update; score calculation. Repeated score reads cannot mutate state. Any task callback exception invalidates every dependent measurement and sets H.

Reset deregisters old callback handles, restores authored pre-integration state through normal environment reset, registers exactly one PRE_PHYSICS_STEP and one POST_PHYSICS_STEP callback, and clears baselines, interval IDs, episodes, extrema, impulses, fractures, containment, loss, H, camera counters, and hold state. No post-start pose or velocity repair is allowed. Bad physical outcomes remain possible and are failed by observation rather than prevented.
assets: Independently authored elongated portable ODRI-informed open shell-base/cover assembly with four insert bosses, access openings, shared case/seat geometry definitions, real structural joints, and an assumed empty-shell mass below the sourced 61 g completed assembly
Four rigid M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL proxies, four original tang bodies, native breakable J_tang_i notch joints, case-relative J_seat_i joints, and named J_shell integrity joints
Separate stationary support jig with named J_jig joints, physically distinct from the portable workpiece
Representative straight M2.5 tang-break mandrel based on Böllhoff family 0158 040 1000
Representative small hammer with an unscaled rigid Xform root and separately scaled collider/render children
Rigid tray with true floor, raised walls, declared closed interior prism, bounded table/workcell, and loss plane
YAM bimanual robot using normal actuation, physical grippers, native contacts, and declared self-collision pairs
Fixed, lit 640×480 RGB-D camera providing native RGB, depth, geometry IDs, and projected-corner validation
approximations: Industrial sources establish the task, insert count and size, notch removal, tang accountability, and M2.5 mandrel family, but not exact boss geometry, notch strength, wire section, empty-shell mass, tool dimensions, friction, or fracture loads. Those values are frozen prototype assumptions requiring native validation. The sourced 61 g value is for a completed shell assembly, so modeled empty-shell mass must be lower and disclosed.

The historical unitless ODRI STL is qualitative context only. Geometry follows sourced elongated open-case photographs and cannot be replaced by a generic square deck or invented capture hole. Fracture is a native breakable fixed joint at the notch; all bodies are rigid PhysX bodies. No calibrated deformable, rate-dependent, exact helical-wire, or shell-crack model is claimed.

The 0.25 mm insert displacement, 3 degree rotation, 0.2 mm penetration, 0.01 m/s and 0.5 rad/s rest limits, 2 s hold, 0.02 N*s robot-contact limit, and nominal impact bounds are prototype assumptions, not manufacturer tolerances. Only observable damage predicates affect grading; impact/alignment bounds are physics diagnostics.

INITIAL-SETTLE mapping: run 1.0 s with zero action from authored reset. initial-settle-station-fixture-linear-speed-maximum=max over B_fixture POST speeds in the final 0.25 s; initial-settle-loose-body-linear-speed-maximum=max over B_case∪B_insert∪B_tang∪B_tool POST speeds in that window. Immediately after the final settle POST, sample initial-untouched-task-score, initial-native-fractured-tang-count, initial-tray-contained-fragment-count, initial-shell-integrity-joint-break-count, initial-insert-seat-joint-break-count, and initial-insert-case-relative-translation-maximum=max_i(d_i). initial-rigid-body-penetration-maximum=max P over every settle POST. Any missing body, joint, score, collision pair, POST sample, or callback makes its check unavailable and failing.

NOMINAL-MATERIAL mapping: run separately labeled real-contact episodes for each i=0..3. closed_nominal_episodes_i counts fully closed qualified episodes for insert i; nominal-all-inserts-closed-contact-episode-count-minimum=min_i(closed_nominal_episodes_i). nominal-native-fractured-tang-count=sum of genuine removals at the completed suite’s final POST. nominal-released-tang-dynamic-body-count=sum of those tangs with independent finite 6-DoF native state at that POST. nominal-contact-stream-row-count-total is the sum of genuine native contact rows across the suite. Over the nonempty set of all closed qualified nominal episodes, nominal-impact-axis-angle-maximum=max angle, nominal-impact-radial-offset-maximum=max offset, nominal-qualified-axial-impulse-minimum=min episode axial impulse, nominal-qualified-axial-impulse-maximum=max episode axial impulse, and nominal-qualified-offaxis-impulse-maximum=max episode off-axis impulse. A missing insert episode or empty qualifying set is unavailable and failing.

ADVERSARIAL-MATERIAL mapping: adversarial-offaxis-impulse-minimum is the minimum episode off-axis impulse over a nonempty separately labeled off-axis bad-probe record. adversarial-visible-damage-event-count-minimum is min_p(D_p) across separately required native seat-break, shell-break, and forbidden-penetration probes p, where D_p counts that probe’s own newly observed target damage events from its first PRE through final POST. Thus every required damage probe must independently produce at least one visible event; events cannot be pooled across probes. Missing probe, target event stream, or qualifying episode is unavailable and failing. These checks never apply to untouched, grading, terminal, or safe-alternative episodes.

RETENTION/PENETRATION mapping: retained-insert-case-relative-translation-maximum=max d_i and retained-insert-case-relative-rotation-maximum=max r_i over every POST in nominal-success, terminal, and targeted seat-load pass probes. postfracture-forbidden-penetration-maximum=max P over every POST beginning with each genuine release through that probe’s final POST in non-damage/pass probes only: nominal-success, terminal, and separately labeled safe adversarial off-axis probes. The separately required seat-break, shell-break, and forbidden-penetration damage-observability probes are explicitly excluded from this pass-bound aggregation; their target events are measured only by adversarial-visible-damage-event-count-minimum and their scorer hard failure H. Empty required pass windows or missing geometry/transforms are unavailable and failing. Damage-probe samples may never be relabeled or pooled into pass probes.

TERMINAL/REST mapping: apply only to each separately labeled full terminal-camera/rest probe and each full demonstration. Within run r, at every fresh 20 Hz scoring observation from the first Q candidate through the run’s final observation, c_r=min observed N_collected, v_r=max linear speed over R_release bodies and observations, w_r=max angular speed analogously, and h_r=maximum uninterrupted duration from first-to-last timestamps of consecutive observations satisfying release, support, speed, integrity, containment, and H=false. Across all required applicable runs report terminal-tray-contained-fragment-count=min_r(c_r), terminal-loose-body-linear-speed-maximum=max_r(v_r), terminal-loose-body-angular-speed-maximum=max_r(w_r), and terminal-continuous-rest-duration-minimum=min_r(h_r). Thus every required run must pass; no run may be hidden by pooling samples. A missing required run, body, support/contact row, timestamp, or observation makes the applicable check unavailable and failing.

TERMINAL/CAMERA mapping: over the same separately labeled terminal candidate window in run r, d_r=min across fresh frames of count(finite positive depth pixels in M)/count(M), k_r=min Boolean across frames with true=1 only when every declared corner is in bounds at positive depth, and f_r=count of distinct strictly increasing valid frame timestamps in the final uninterrupted Q window including both endpoints. Across all required applicable runs report camera-workspace-valid-depth-fraction-minimum=min_r(d_r), camera-workspace-corners-visible=min_r(k_r), and terminal-fresh-valid-camera-frame-count-minimum=min_r(f_r). terminal-tray-contained-fragment-count and camera checks do not apply to untouched or partial controls. Empty run/frame/window sets, a missing required run or mask, reused timestamps, or acquisition failure are unavailable and failing.

PRODUCTION/REFINEMENT mapping: production-postphysics-callback-dt-error-maximum=max_n(abs(float32(dt_n)-1/240)) over all unique actual production POST callbacks; refinement-postphysics-callback-dt-error-maximum=max_n(abs(float32(dt_n)-1/480)) over all unique actual refinement POST callbacks. Preserve raw float32 dt and counts; never substitute configuration or rounded values. Expected observations 0.004166666883975267 and 0.0020833334419876337 are evidence targets only. Missing, duplicate, non-finite, exception-producing, or untagged POST samples make the respective proof unavailable and failing.

LIFECYCLE mapping: lifecycle-task-callback-handle-count-error-maximum=max_s abs(h_s-2), where h_s counts ONLY this task’s active PhysxManager PRE_PHYSICS_STEP plus POST_PHYSICS_STEP callback pair at every required active-lifecycle sample s immediately after initial registration and immediately after every clean reset. Other SDK or camera callbacks and contact or joint-event subscriptions are distinct and excluded. Intentional after-deregistration shutdown samples are outside the active window. Missing required samples, registration failures, callback exceptions, generation IDs, or an empty sample set make this check unavailable and failing; never report 0 without evidence. reset-stale-event-count counts, from reset completion through the first 1.0 s settle and then the complete second full trajectory, any contact row, joint transition, camera frame, interval ID, or episode carrying a pre-reset generation ID; aggregate by sum. Missing generation IDs, missing observation interval, callback exceptions, or incomplete second trajectory make reset-stale-event-count unavailable and failing.

ROBOT-CONTACT mapping: unsafe-robot-self-contact-impulse-maximum=max fresh normal impulse across declared unsafe link pairs over every robot-running component probe, grading control, safe-alternative characterization, and demonstration, sampled at every POST. A genuinely empty unsafe-contact set yields measured 0 only when the complete native contact stream and declared pair coverage are both proven; missing contacts, pair metadata, intervals, or units is unavailable and failing.

Aggregate reporting combines separately labeled initial-settle, nominal-material, adversarial-material, terminal-camera/rest, lifecycle, production, and refinement probes. A check is not applicable outside its declared scope and cannot fail an unrelated grading episode. Within an applicable scope, an empty required qualifying set is unavailable rather than zero, infinity, or a sentinel. Save all available raw values and an explicit missing_observables list.

Pinned source inspection establishes that PhysxManager.register_callback exposes dt-bearing PRE_PHYSICS_STEP and POST_PHYSICS_STEP handles. It does not validate ordering, freshness, reset behavior, contact units, fracture dynamics, penetration, or camera output. These require native tests. Control remains 20 Hz independently of 240/480 Hz physics; 7200 controls equal 360 s.

Prior native evidence reported zero contacts and fractures, five shell-joint breaks at step 1, invalid 0.745833 camera depth coverage, invisible corners, and a collapsed poorly lit deck. Those remain construction failures to engineer away, not valid empty sets or evidence of success. This contract is prospective and makes no claim that retained scaffolds, rigs, or earlier episodes pass it. A simpler successful safe strategy triggers a fresh novelty comparison against the ability actually demonstrated.
contract.scoring_spec: At every unique POST sample, after physical transition, damage, loss, containment, camera, and rest updates, compute H from damage_rules. If H=true, S=0. Otherwise N_removed∈{0,1,2,3,4} counts original tangs genuinely detached through native J_tang transitions, and N_collected∈{0,…,N_removed} counts those currently entirely inside the true tray interior with fresh tray support and stated rest limits. Define R_release=B_case∪B_tool∪B_tang; it explicitly excludes B_tray and B_fixture. T=1 only when all four tangs are removed and collected, every member of R_release is released by both grippers, physically supported and at rest, shell/insert integrity holds, the fixture is stable, and Q has held for 41 consecutive fresh valid 20 Hz RGB-D observations spanning at least 2.0 s; otherwise T=0. S=0.125*N_removed+0.10*N_collected+0.10*T. Untouched=0; one removed outside tray=0.125; one removed and collected=0.225; four removed and none collected=0.50; four removed and three collected=0.80; all four removed/collected before terminal hold=0.90; full terminal outcome=1.00. No grasp, alignment, hammer, hand, route, action-order, strike-count, force-window, or direct-contact bonus or exclusion exists. Each removal term begins only at its genuine transition and persists while evidence remains finite/addressable and H=false. Each collection term is revoked immediately when current containment/support/rest fails. T is revoked on any Q violation. Timeout adds no failure; recoverable uncollected fragments retain removal credit. Reset clears every score input. Independent replay must reproduce scores from raw PRE/POST body, joint, contact, camera, generation-ID, and timestamp records with the same ordering.

required_controls.name: control-tools-grasped-and-aligned-no-removal
required_controls.reason: Grasping, alignment, contact, and tool possession are not industrial outcomes.

required_controls.name: control-four-collected-but-release-set-held
required_controls.reason: All removal and collection terms apply, but at least one member of R_release remains supported by a gripper, so T=0.

required_controls.name: control-four-collected-released-hold-under-two-seconds
required_controls.reason: R_release is released, but fewer than 41 valid observations spanning 2.0 s keeps T=0.

required_controls.name: control-complete-stable-terminal
required_controls.reason: N_removed=4, N_collected=4, and the uninterrupted terminal predicate earns T=1.

required_controls.name: control-clean-reset-complete-stable-terminal
required_controls.reason: A second real-action run after reset independently reproduces full outcome without stale events.

required_controls.name: control-refinement-480hz-complete-stable-terminal
required_controls.reason: The twice-rate native replay preserves the same full physical outcome and passes its distinct timing probe.

required_controls.name: control-actual-insert-seat-damage
required_controls.reason: Native seat break, displacement above 0.25 mm, or rotation above 3 degrees sets H.

required_controls.name: control-actual-shell-integrity-break
required_controls.reason: A native J_shell break sets H.

required_controls.name: control-actual-fragment-workcell-loss
required_controls.reason: Physical escape, floor loss, deletion, unaddressability, or non-finite fragment state sets H.

required_controls.name: control-four-removed-two-collected-two-recoverable-at-timeout
required_controls.reason: Timeout creates no invented failure: 0.50 removal plus 0.20 current collection credit.

comparisons.objective: Depanel a scored PCB by bending it downward over a registered break edge, then tray the board.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual frame bracing and controlled bulk bending at a V-score; no impact tool or coaxial recessed-tool alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid downward edge-supported separation, board in ESD tray, scrap frame safely placed, parts released and stable.
comparisons.reason: Both tasks fracture a manufactured weak section and contain a freed part, but this record tests registered bulk bending of a panel. The candidate tests hammer-driven notch fracture through a stabilized mandrel, retention of four inserts, and search/recovery of four millimetre-scale tangs.

comparisons.objective: Join two aluminium strips by setting one blind rivet and dispose of its snapped stem.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load and insert a rivet, hold a hand riveter square and pressed down, repeatedly pump its handles, then empty the stem.
comparisons.success_condition: Rivet set through both strips without a tilted or lifted pull, spent stem in tray, riveter returned and released.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest fragment-disposal neighbor, but its central mechanism is tensile stem pulling and rivet deformation through cyclic handle pumping. The candidate instead requires bimanual impact through a separate coaxial mandrel to break four already-installed insert tangs without shifting the coils.

comparisons.objective: Place and hold a nail upright while another arm drives it into a wooden post.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual nail stabilization, timed hammering, release once self-supporting, and collision avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Nail driven more than 4 cm; any arm-arm or hammer-controlled-arm contact scores zero.
comparisons.reason: It shares mandrel-like stabilization plus hammer impacts, but tests progressive fastener penetration and hand-clearance timing. It does not test fracture at a notch, protection of a retained threaded insert, tool withdrawal without snagging, or recovery of loose fragments.

comparisons.objective: Extract a stuck eye pin using a slide hammer and return the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hook engagement, one-hand shaft stabilization, and repeated momentum-driven sliding-weight blows while following the extracted pin.
comparisons.success_condition: Available evidence requires impact-based pin extraction and rack return; no numeric scoring rubric is present.
comparisons.reason: Both require aligned impact and stabilization, but the slide hammer delivers axial momentum to extract a whole pin using a captive sliding weight. The candidate delivers an external hammer blow through a narrow mandrel to fracture a notch, retain the insert, and recover separate debris.

comparisons.objective: Hammer in a nail held by another robot arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hammer striking coordinated with another arm holding a nail.
comparisons.success_condition: Only the title and brief body report nail-driving completion; thresholds and failure rubric are absent.
comparisons.reason: Despite the shared bimanual hammer primitive, the tested outcome is nail penetration. The candidate's essential outcomes are notch fracture, coil retention, controlled mandrel withdrawal, and four-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Make one dent at the center of a scribed cross with an automatic center punch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precisely align and axially press a self-firing punch while preventing tip skate, tilt, and lateral loading.
comparisons.success_condition: One centered mark, punch lifted clear and held still; off-center, tilted, or repeated firing is unacceptable. No separate spec version supplies numeric thresholds.
comparisons.reason: This shares narrow-tool alignment and axial-force regulation, but creates a single surface indentation through an internal punch mechanism. It has no separate hammer, bimanual tool stabilization, component fracture, retained-coil constraint, or debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Score a tile in one pass on a manual cutter, then snap it with the breaker.
comparisons.physical_skill: Straight scoring followed by supported bulk fracture using the cutter's breaker.
comparisons.success_condition: The body states one-pass scoring and subsequent snapping; the record contains no complete numeric success rubric.
comparisons.reason: This tests creating a score and then bulk tile fracture by levered bending. The candidate starts with manufactured notches and tests precise impact transfer through a mandrel plus recovery of four tiny fragments without disturbing inserts.

comparisons.objective: Snap a pre-scored wall tile in two over a steel rod.
comparisons.physical_skill: Register the score over a support and apply controlled bending without lifting the tile off the rod.
comparisons.success_condition: Tile separated along the score and released; the record provides no numeric geometry or damage thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The shared concept is fracture at a score, but the mechanism and ability differ: supported bulk bending of a tile versus coaxial impact-tool placement inside four recessed inserts, local notch fracture, insert protection, and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Abrade an inert ampoule neck, break it open, and retain the cap in a protective opener.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual upright stabilization, circumferential contact-guided abrasion, protected breakaway, and captive cap handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Required abrasion coverage before native joint break, cap retained, body and opener returned, hands released, stable endpoint; premature break, excessive tilt, contact, escape, or drop fails.
comparisons.reason: Both involve qualified fracture and retention of a freed piece, but this record tests distributed abrasive scoring followed by opener leverage around a fragile vessel. The candidate tests repeated hammer impacts through a straight mandrel, coil-preserving withdrawal, and independent recovery of four free tangs.

comparisons.objective: Purge air from a needle-free syringe while preserving its liquid, then return and release it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a syringe, bimanually support barrel and advance plunger, and regulate fluid loss without retraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Residual-air and sample-loss limits, safe return pose, hands clear, and a continuous one-second hold; excess loss, aspiration, drop, or invalid state fails.
comparisons.reason: This is fluid-management and plunger-control manipulation with no impact, fracture, retained insert, or loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Select and install the matching driver bit, power-tighten a drawer-knob screw, and return the stopped tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Shape-based bit selection, bit insertion, drawer bracing, powered screw engagement, axial pressure, and tool return.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct bit retained, at least 1.3 mm credited powered feed, closed knob passing a 5 N hold test, then stable released tool return.
comparisons.reason: It tests tool assembly and rotary fastening. Coaxial alignment is generic to both, but the candidate's defining ability is impact-induced tang fracture without coil displacement followed by loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Align mating flanges and insert locating pins through their holes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual part registration, sustained flange support, multi-hole alignment, and precision pin insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Flanges within specified position/orientation tolerances and pins seated in distinct aligned holes; versions cover four vertical pins or two horizontal pins.
comparisons.reason: This tests assembly by alignment and insertion, not impact fracture or extraction. No material must break, no retained coil must survive lateral impulse, and no released debris must be found and contained.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a fixed tool tip by touching one reference point from four sufficiently different orientations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tip placement, low-force contact, submillimetre stillness, and controlled reorientation about a fixed point.
comparisons.success_condition: Four one-second contacts with prescribed lean, tip-position, stability, and at least 15-degree inter-pose axis separation.
comparisons.reason: It shares precision tip alignment and lateral-force discipline, but tests static multi-orientation contact calibration. The candidate requires dynamic bimanual hammer impacts, notch fracture, component-retention monitoring, and fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a started bracket bolt with short ratchet strokes in confined access.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick up and seat a socket, maintain engagement, alternate drive/return strokes, and transmit controlled rotary torque between walls.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 1.8 turns, measured seated contact, six advancing ratchet cycles, socket engagement hold, and no integrity or over-torque fault.
comparisons.reason: This is constrained rotary fastening with a one-way clutch. It does not test impact transfer, manufactured-notch fracture, protection of an insert from off-axis blows, or recovery of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Lower a bent tube into a checking fixture so four legs seat simultaneously in their slots.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual level transport, multi-feature 3-D alignment, gentle simultaneous insertion, and release under self-weight.
comparisons.success_condition: All four legs seated within slot tolerances, tube released and stable; excessive drop speed or leaving the bench permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: This tests coordinated multi-point fixture seating without force. The candidate instead tests localized impact fracture and post-fracture debris handling; simultaneous geometric alignment alone is only a shared generic primitive.

comparisons.objective: Recover drawer opening after trapped clothing jams its motion.
comparisons.physical_skill: Detect a jam, pause pulling, bimanually compress the obstruction, then resume controlled drawer opening.
comparisons.success_condition: Ordered jam, compression, clearance, and full-open milestones with final stillness; the rubric does not establish continuous handle retention or general damage avoidance.
comparisons.reason: This is conditional obstruction recovery using compliant compression and drawer translation, with no precision tool alignment, impact, fracture, insert retention, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Join two chain ends on a connecting link and install a side-entry retaining plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual articulated-part alignment, hole-over-pin placement, lateral keeper insertion, and released assembly placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both chain ends seated, keeper stems in retained slot regions, chain on guide, joint in cradle, hands clear, and all bodies stable for one second.
comparisons.reason: This tests multi-part insertion and latching of a chain joint. The candidate removes sacrificial tangs through impact fracture and debris recovery rather than assembling and retaining loose components.

comparisons.objective: Take an ear temperature by seating a covered probe, pressing Measure, holding through the reading, then laying it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Anatomically constrained insertion-depth control, button actuation, and very stable probe holding.
comparisons.success_condition: Proper seating, successful three-second reading within motion limits, safe depth, then released stable placement; deep insertion or dropping permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: Although both require narrow-tool alignment in a recessed opening, this record tests gentle insertion and sustained stillness with a safety depth bound. It has no impact, fracture, retained threaded component, or debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Fill three drywall nail holes with spackle and strike the patches flush.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load a putty knife, regulate blade angle and sliding contact, pack material, and skim the surface.
comparisons.success_condition: All holes filled within depth tolerance, minimal proud area, knife set down; damaging corner-drag caps the score.
comparisons.reason: This tests material transfer and surface finishing through continuous sliding contact, not impact, breakage, precision mandrel insertion, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Open three breaker terminals, insert one comb busbar into all terminals, then tighten every screw onto its pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated screwdriver strokes, multi-receiver preparation, simultaneous multi-pin insertion, and sequential clamping.
comparisons.success_condition: All pins home with bar square, all screws tightened, assembly withstands a 10 N pull, tool and hands clear for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: This tests preparatory loosening, multi-pin insertion, and rotary clamping. The candidate instead uses impact to remove sacrificial tangs while preserving existing inserts and collecting the freed pieces.

comparisons.objective: Fit matching caps to four pens and sort the capped pens by color.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated cap-to-pen alignment and insertion, visual matching, placement, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Four matching caps retained and four pens released, stable, and fully inside the correct marked areas.
comparisons.reason: This is repeated press-fit assembly plus sorting. It contains neither impact-controlled fracture nor protection of a retained coil or recovery of fractured metal fragments.

comparisons.objective: Prune a dead rose cane above its bud without dropping the cutting, then bin it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Position secateurs, preserve nearby live structure, coordinate cutting with grasp retention, and transfer the freed cutting.
comparisons.success_condition: First and final cut 3–15 mm beyond an intact attached bud, cutting never dropped and placed in bin, secateurs set down, hands clear and stable.
comparisons.reason: Both intentionally separate a sacrificial piece and require its containment while protecting retained structure. However, pruning tests shear cutting with simultaneous grasp retention of one large cutting; the candidate tests hammer-driven notch fracture through a recessed mandrel and subsequent search/recovery of four initially uncontrolled millimetre-scale tangs.

comparisons.objective: Hand-tighten a spin-on oil filter to the specified angle past gasket contact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thread following, bimanual regrasping, wrist-driven rotation, and turn-count/torque-proxy regulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Filter ends 240–360 degrees past contact without removal or over-tightening, most rotation credited to a holding wrist, hand released, and full state held one second.
comparisons.reason: This tests controlled threaded rotation and regrasping. It does not fracture or remove a component, withstand hammer impulse, protect insert pose, or recover debris.

comparisons.objective: Extract exactly one chip from an open packet and place it on a plate while retaining the others.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective grasping in clutter, packet stabilization, constrained extraction, and gentle placement.
comparisons.success_condition: One chip clears and rests on the plate with hands clear; packet displacement, loss, or any second chip leaving containment permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: This tests selective retrieval and retention from a container. Fragment recovery is only a generic shared primitive; the candidate must first create four fragments through controlled impact fracture and preserve four threaded inserts before collecting every tang.

comparisons.objective: Select required conveyor parts and assemble the pictured model while rejecting look-alikes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Perception-guided interception, temporary parking, sequencing, stacking, and avoiding conveyor jams.
comparisons.success_condition: Two cylinders, beam, and cube assembled on marked sites, all distractors carried off downstream, no part held back, and final model stable for one second.
comparisons.reason: This tests online selection and assembly from moving parts. It has no coaxial tool use, hammer impact, fracture, retained-component protection, or small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Extract a fitted collar from a shaft with a prepared screw puller, then recover the collar and park the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counterhold a puller while repeatedly turning its screw; lift, park, spread jaws, and release the collar.
comparisons.success_condition: Collar clears the shaft after measured screw turns, rests in the tray, and intact puller is parked stably with hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel placement, a separately delivered fracture impact, retained-coil protection, and recovery of four tiny fractured tangs; screw-driven collar extraction tests a different mechanism and outcome.

comparisons.objective: Roll puff pastry into an even 3 mm sheet of sufficient length without sealing its ends.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually keep a spacer-ring rolling pin level through repeated rolling passes.
comparisons.success_condition: Sheet reaches at least 20 cm with at least 90% near 3 mm, no rolled-over ends, and pin released level.
comparisons.reason: Deformable-sheet rolling and thickness control do not test impact fracture, recessed insert alignment, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Lower a hoisted motor onto four base studs while operating the hoist and steering the suspended load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual pendant operation, pendulum-load guidance, multi-stud alignment, and pinch-zone avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: All feet are flat with four studs through, chain slack, controls released, and no under-load, pinch, or high-speed stud strike violation.
comparisons.reason: This tests safe placement of a suspended heavy load onto a four-fastener pattern, not tool-mediated notch fracture or loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Unhook and remove an air-fryer basket trivet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate the basket insert and its retaining hooks while stabilizing the surrounding basket.
comparisons.success_condition: Trivet is disengaged and removed without damaging or losing components, then left in the specified stable state.
comparisons.reason: Latch/unhook extraction is mechanically different from striking a coaxially held mandrel to fracture four insert tangs and recover the fragments.

comparisons.objective: Fill and remove a blood tube from a holder while an existing needle remains in a training arm vein.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the needle holder while axially pushing, filling, and pulling the tube without needle displacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Tube is pierced, filled, removed, and deposited while needle translation, lateral motion, and pivot remain within strict limits.
comparisons.reason: Although both require stabilizing one component while applying force with the other hand, this tests controlled axial tube exchange and needle immobility, not impact fracture or fragment search.

comparisons.objective: Rinse highlighted teeth, evacuate water, clear the mouth, and return both dental tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated bimanual irrigation and location-dependent suction over prescribed crown regions.
comparisons.success_condition: Required wet coverage and recovery are achieved with bounded spill/pooling, followed by cleared water and both tools returned and released.
comparisons.reason: Fluid coverage and evacuation are different tested abilities from recessed mandrel alignment, hammer impact regulation, and solid-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Reattach a detached wrist camera to its mount and restore live sensing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick up, align, insert, seat, and latch a camera into a constrained wrist channel.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera is latched within pose tolerances, delivers a live frame, remains stable after release, and is not dropped.
comparisons.reason: Precision insertion and latching overlap only generically with alignment; the candidate centrally tests controlled tang fracture and recovery of four free fragments.

comparisons.objective: Hand-mount the final section of a bicycle tire bead after creating slack in the rim center channel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold bead arcs down and roll the remaining bead over the flange without pinching the tube.
comparisons.success_condition: Bead is seated all around, valve remains aligned, hands are clear, and lever misuse, forceful striking, or tube leakage is absent.
comparisons.reason: Compliant bead routing and seating are meaningfully different from rigid insert-tang impact fracture and millimetre-scale metal-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Install a click-lock vinyl floor tile into an existing row.
comparisons.physical_skill: Angle a long tongue into a groove, control both ends, lower the tile, and engage the lock without racking.
comparisons.success_condition: Both ends are locked with bounded seam, lippage, flatness, and wall gap; tile is released and stable.
comparisons.reason: Long-edge tongue-and-groove engagement tests distributed alignment and lowering, not a localized impact fracture followed by debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Load four connector modules into a hinged frame and close it until it clicks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated precision module placement followed by bimanual frame closure and latch engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: All four modules are seated, frame is clicked shut, hands are clear, and no module was crushed or dropped.
comparisons.reason: Repeated insertion and latching share generic alignment but do not test hammer/mandrel coordination, notch fracture, retained-coil protection, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Start a handheld 3D scanner and scan a cast housing from all required viewpoints for CAD comparison.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a control button while moving and orienting the scanner around the part with adequate coverage.
comparisons.success_condition: Scanner is started and the housing obtains the required all-around/top coverage and usable comparison data.
comparisons.reason: Sensor trajectory planning and surface coverage are unrelated to contact-loaded fracture and physical recovery of released tangs.

comparisons.objective: Load washable blender components while keeping the motor base out of the wash area.
comparisons.physical_skill: Separate, handle, and place appliance parts while excluding the non-washable powered base.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified washable parts are loaded and the motor base remains excluded and undamaged.
comparisons.reason: Sorting/loading appliance parts does not test coaxial tool alignment, controlled impact, insert retention, or tiny-fragment recovery; the record supplies less numeric rubric detail, but its objective is clearly unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Route a cable between two posts and secure its final clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Guide a flexible cable along a prescribed route and engage a retaining clip.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable follows the required path and the final clip is secured without cable loss or misrouting.
comparisons.reason: Flexible routing and clipping are different from rigid impact fracture and debris containment; missing detailed thresholds do not create plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Prepare a moka pot by filling water below the safety valve, seating the coffee basket, and screwing the top snug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled liquid pouring, coaxial basket placement, thread engagement, and rotational tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Safe water volume, filled basket, correctly aligned and snug threaded top, minimal spill, and upright released pot.
comparisons.reason: Threaded assembly and liquid handling do not test a hammer-driven notch fracture or recovery of multiple released metal fragments.

comparisons.objective: Scribe a shelf end to match an out-of-flat wall.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold the shelf fixed while guiding a pencil compass continuously along the wall profile.
comparisons.success_condition: A continuous scribe matches target offsets at measured stations, with shelf stable and compass put down clear.
comparisons.reason: Profile following and mark generation are different from coaxial recessed insertion, impact-force control, and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Open a sealed cocktail shaker by striking the correct seam location, then separate and set down both tins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the shaker, deliver a directed hand blow within a speed window, lift off the small tin, and prevent spilling.
comparisons.success_condition: A qualifying blow breaks the seal, tins separate and finish upright and released, with no denting, spill, or fall.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest impact neighbor, but it tests a direct hand blow that elastically releases a tapered seal. The candidate requires a separately manipulated hammer striking a stabilized narrow mandrel to fracture four manufactured notches, preserve inserts, and recover every fragment.

comparisons.objective: Replace a cartridge in a ratchet-rod dispenser and restore its working configuration.
comparisons.physical_skill: Disengage and retract a piston rod, exchange cartridges, align the replacement, and re-engage the mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Used cartridge is collected, replacement seated, piston and pawl re-engaged, dispenser cradled, and hands released.
comparisons.reason: Consumable exchange and ratchet reassembly do not test controlled impact fracture or post-fracture search and containment.

comparisons.objective: Finish painting only the unpainted portions of a partially completed panel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visually identify bare regions and roll precise coverage while maintaining roller contact and boundary control.
comparisons.success_condition: Bare cells are covered with limited repainting of existing work and no paint deposited on the table.
comparisons.reason: Visual coverage planning and surface coating are unrelated to rigid small-part fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Zero an unpowered robot joint by aligning its link and inserting a calibration pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold a gravity-loaded link at its zero mark while inserting a pin through aligned holes.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin is fully home, link remains within one degree of zero and still after release, with excessive link speed prohibited in relevant versions.
comparisons.reason: This shares bimanual alignment and narrow insertion, but its tested outcome is load-supporting pin insertion. It has no controlled hammer strike, notch fracture, retained insert, or loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Shim a door hinge jamb using opposed tapered shims without bowing the jamb.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate insertion and controlled driving of two opposing wedges while monitoring jamb position.
comparisons.success_condition: Both shims are snug at the hinge location and the jamb remains within straightness/position limits without damage.
comparisons.reason: Opposed wedge adjustment tests quasi-static fit and structural alignment, not coaxial impact transfer through a mandrel, discrete fracture, and fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Release a camera from a cam-clamped quick-release mount.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate the cam clamp while supporting and removing the camera from its mount.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera is fully released and safely placed or held as specified, with mount and camera undamaged.
comparisons.reason: Cam-latch release and supported removal do not test impact fracture or recovery of several millimetre-scale debris pieces.

comparisons.objective: Set a bench grinder's tool rest and tongue guard to prescribed safety gaps before operation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Loosen, gauge, reposition, and secure adjustable guards relative to a grinding wheel.
comparisons.success_condition: Both gaps satisfy the required safety limits and components are secured before the grinder starts.
comparisons.reason: Safety-gap adjustment and fastening are different from striking a break-off mandrel and verifying four tangs are removed and contained.

comparisons.objective: Swipe a magnetic-stripe card through a desktop reader exactly once and return it to its stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain card orientation, depth, direction, and speed through a narrow reader slot.
comparisons.success_condition: One clean read spans the encoded stripe at rated speed, then the card is returned, released, and not dropped.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic slot-guided swiping tests trajectory and velocity control, not impact-force regulation, fracture, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Thread a shock cord through a spring cord lock while holding its release button open.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually squeeze and stabilize a loose lock while feeding a compliant, buckling cord through its passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord protrudes sufficiently on both sides, spring alone grips it after release, and lock/cord rest stably with hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Although it combines bimanual stabilization with insertion, it tests compliant threading under a held release, not impact fracture of a retained rigid feature or debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Place a phone, watch, and earbuds case on their matching positions of a three-in-one charger.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align three devices to different charging surfaces, including handling a flexible watch band, without moving the stand.
comparisons.success_condition: All devices remain released and charging with indicators observed for five seconds while the stand stays within pose limits.
comparisons.reason: Multi-device placement and functional charging verification do not test hammer/mandrel coordination, fracture mechanics, or recovery of released tangs.

comparisons.objective: Place two setting blocks, then lower and release a glass unit onto them without sill contact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large fragile-part alignment and supported lowering into a narrow frame channel.
comparisons.success_condition: Blocks positioned on marks; glass centred, upright, released, stable, resting on both blocks; any sill touch fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests sequenced support placement and damage-free glass lowering, not notch fracture by controlled impact or recovery of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Align nickel strip over four battery cells and spot-weld it to every terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Planar strip placement followed by repeated two-probe electrical contact and tool handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Strip aligned; four bonded/timed welds completed; welder returned; pack undamaged and stable.
comparisons.reason: Although both repeat a tool operation four times, spot welding creates bonds through sustained probe contact; the candidate fractures notched tangs with hammer impulses and recovers each fragment.

comparisons.objective: Pull, wipe, reseat, reread, report, and finally reseat an engine dipstick.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequenced extraction/insertion, wiping contact, visual-state reporting, and contamination-safe handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid wipe–reseat–read sequence, correct level report, dipstick reseated, rag released.
comparisons.reason: Tests procedural state preparation and measurement rather than bimanual impact fracture and loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Install an external circlip in a shaft groove and turn it to verify seating.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pliers-mediated controlled elastic spreading, axial transfer, square closure, and verification rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring seated without over-spread or twist, turned at least 15 degrees, pliers put down, arms clear.
comparisons.reason: Both involve a small retained feature and damage limits, but this tests reversible elastic spreading and groove seating; the candidate tests axial impact fracture at a notch plus recovery of four separated tangs.

comparisons.objective: Measure two leveled scoops of powdered formula into a bottle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Granular scooping, strike-off leveling, narrow-neck pouring, and spill control.
comparisons.success_condition: Each scoop leveled at the bar; correct final mass; under 1 g spill; scoop released.
comparisons.reason: Granular dosing and mass control are meaningfully different from coaxial mandrel placement, hammering, fracture, and metal-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Seat a tilted add-on board squarely onto two rows of header pins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine multi-pin alignment and even press-fitting without bending pins.
comparisons.success_condition: Board fully seated, still, and released; any excessive tilt during engagement records bent-pin failure.
comparisons.reason: Tests distributed compliant insertion and even pressing, not localized impact fracture or post-fracture fragment handling.

comparisons.objective: Insert an emergency-stop body through a keyed panel hole and secure its rear locking ring.
comparisons.physical_skill: Key/tab alignment, through-panel insertion, bimanual retention, and ring threading.
comparisons.success_condition: Button flush and keyed; ring turned snug against panel; assembly released and stable.
comparisons.reason: This is keyed insertion plus threaded fastening, with no impact, intentional fracture, or loose-part recovery.

comparisons.objective: Unfold a laptop stand and seat both support rods in their highest slots.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual linkage manipulation and dual rod-to-slot seating.
comparisons.success_condition: Stand fully spread, both rods seated, and footprint inside the marked rectangle.
comparisons.reason: Tests configuring a passive linkage, not controlled impact delivery or separation and containment of fragments.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both faces of a knife on a whetstone and put it down safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated angle-controlled sliding contact across the blade length.
comparisons.success_condition: At least three valid strokes and sufficient edge coverage per face; knife released edge-away.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate tool contact, but sharpening tests sustained sliding at a prescribed angle; the candidate tests brief axial impacts, notch fracture, and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Stretch an O-ring over a threaded plug and seat it square and untwisted in its groove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Damage-limited elastic expansion, transfer over threads, release, and local seating correction.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring fully seated and released without over-stretch or excessive roll/twist.
comparisons.reason: Tests deformable seal installation and elastic-strain control, unlike rigid impact fracture and recovery of independently simulated metal tangs.

comparisons.objective: Paint a band above skirting using an edger guided by the board edge.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous guided surface contact with pad orientation and contamination control.
comparisons.success_condition: Coverage thresholds met, cut line painted, trim unmarked, edger returned and released.
comparisons.reason: Continuous guided coating and paint-boundary control do not test coaxial impact fracture or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Mount a shaft between fixed and spring-loaded bench centres.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual lever actuation, centre-hole engagement, pivoting alignment, and controlled spring release.
comparisons.success_condition: Both points seated, lever at rest, shaft still and hands clear; dropping or ramming is penalized.
comparisons.reason: It shares bimanual stabilization and alignment but tests spring-assisted seating of a shaft, not hammer-induced notch fracture and recovery of freed pieces.

comparisons.objective: Remove an interrupted suture using forceps and a stitch cutter, then dispose of it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Millimetre-scale lift, supported cutting, direction-controlled extraction, and two-tool coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct leg cut flush, stitch drawn toward wound without excess opening, deposited on gauze, tools returned; tissue damage fails.
comparisons.reason: Both intentionally separate and recover a small element with two tools, but the mechanisms and abilities differ materially: supported slicing and compliant-thread extraction versus mandrel-transmitted impact fracture inside a threaded insert.

comparisons.objective: Insert one phase busbar into four push-in circuit-breaker terminals.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous multi-fork alignment and distributed upward press-fit insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: All four forks fully home, released, and retained under a 5 N tug; bent forks or moved breakers fail.
comparisons.reason: Tests parallel multi-terminal insertion and retention, rather than sequential fracture of sacrificial tangs and physical fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Move an untaped-bottom carton of cans to a shelf without losing its contents.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load support from below, transport, and stable placement.
comparisons.success_condition: All cans remain inside; carton rests upright within shelf bounds and is released.
comparisons.reason: Tests discovering and maintaining distributed support for an unstable container, not precision tool alignment, impact, or fracture.

comparisons.objective: Lay two ordered cables into a carrier and snap all twelve crossbars shut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable routing, order preservation, repeated hinge closure, and snap-latching.
comparisons.success_condition: Both cables correctly routed without crossing; every crossbar latched; strain relief intact; system released.
comparisons.reason: Repeated snap-latching over deformable cables is different from striking a mandrel to fracture notched rigid tangs and collecting the fragments.

comparisons.objective: Clamp a wooden strip and saw off a 150 mm retained piece.
comparisons.physical_skill: Vise tightening, cut-line selection, and repeated sawing-force control.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly two physical pieces; retained length 150 ±1 mm; vise tight and saw clear; cutting before clamping fails.
comparisons.reason: Both create separated material, but sawing tests extended abrasive cutting to a length tolerance; the candidate tests discrete impact fracture at manufactured notches and recovery of four millimetre-scale tangs.

comparisons.objective: Run a two-sled ramp experiment, identify the higher-friction base, and place it on a mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Experimental setup, common-gate release, observation-based comparison, and selection.
comparisons.success_condition: Two valid stopping measurements differ by over 30 mm; only the higher-friction sled is released on the mat.
comparisons.reason: Tests physical experimentation and inference, not tool-mediated impact, fracture, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Install round and diamond locating pins and load a bracket onto them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pin selection/orientation, precision fixture insertion, and two-hole part seating.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct pin set home, diamond oriented properly, bracket fully seated and stable, hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Precision locating and slip-fit seating are different from breaking sacrificial insert tangs while preserving the surrounding coils.

comparisons.objective: Choose fitting tweezers, peel protective film while stabilizing its carrier, and restore the tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool selection by clearance, spring-tweezer actuation, bimanual peel-force control, and carrier stabilization.
comparisons.success_condition: Film fully detached and placed outside carrier; carrier excursion limited; both tweezers restored; hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Small-part bimanual work is shared generically, but peeling an adhesive film with selected tweezers does not test coaxial mandrel impact, notch fracture, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Add and close a personal padlock through a free hole of an occupied group-lockout hasp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Shackle-to-hole insertion and latching without disturbing an existing lock or energized-control state.
comparisons.success_condition: Purple lock shut and independently retains the hasp under pry and handle-load tests; coworker lock remains undisturbed.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety-preserving insertion, closure, and load retention, not controlled fracture and containment.

comparisons.objective: Load four flat aluminium blanks into a close-clearance gravity magazine.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated planar squaring, narrow-mouth insertion, stacking, and jam avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: All four blanks lie flat, centred, supported, below the rim, and at rest.
comparisons.reason: Repeated close-clearance insertion is materially different from sequential impact fracture and retrieval of freed tang fragments.

comparisons.objective: Fit and centre an inside-bolt-circle gasket, then insert four flange bolts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Flexible gasket placement in a constrained joint followed by repeated bolt insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Gasket flat, centred, released and still; all four bolts upright and seated in their holes.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained gasket positioning and bolt placement, without hammer impact, intentional break-off, or recovery of sacrificial parts.

comparisons.objective: Reload a long-arm stapler and use it to fasten two sheets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual spring-loaded magazine handling, staple-strip placement, paper feeding, and lever pressing.
comparisons.success_condition: Stapler correctly loaded; a staple physically joins both sheets; arms clear and mechanism stable.
comparisons.reason: Although the stapler uses an impulsive fastening action, the tested outcome is loading and joining sheets; it does not require coaxial mandrel stabilization, notch fracture, or collection of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Release a tool-chest lid stay and lower the lid safely by its side handle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stay release and speed-controlled articulated-load lowering with pinch avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid shut and still, release returned, hands clear; excessive speed or pinch-zone entry fails.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated release and controlled lowering of a heavy hinge, not impact-force delivery or small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Break four installed HELICOIL tangs and recover them; record opens a vacuum-sealed jar and sets down its lid.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs recessed coaxial mandrel control, bimanual hammer impact, and fragment recovery; record needs rim levering, counter-torque, and lid twisting.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact-loaded fractures, four contained tangs, retained inserts, and no damage; record requires seal release, 80° loosening, stable upright jar, and lid placement. Candidate numeric fracture/damage tolerances are not yet specified.
comparisons.reason: Levering and rotary opening do not test impact-driven notch fracture or small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Finish and clear four insert tangs; record levels and pins a hazardous platform before loading blocks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate stabilizes a narrow mandrel while hammering; record supports a pivoting platform, aligns a pin through three holes, then places loads safely.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and contained fragments without coil/shell damage; record requires a locked, level platform, two placed blocks, clear arms, and no hand contact. Candidate quantitative damage limits are missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both include axial alignment, the record tests safeguard restoration and load sequencing, not fracture or debris control.

comparisons.objective: Remove and recover HELICOIL tangs; record clamps an aluminum bar and drills a marked through-hole.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel stabilization and controlled hammer blows; record requires clamp tightening, workpiece restraint, and drill-feed operation with hand clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four notch fractures, retained inserts, and all fragments in a tray; record requires a correctly located hole while clamped, drill retracted, and no unsafe approach. Candidate force/damage thresholds remain unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Impact fracture of internal tangs and loose-fragment recovery are meaningfully different from workholding and drill feeding.

comparisons.objective: Break and recover four insert tangs; record safely assembles a grinding-wheel stack onto a spindle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a coaxial impact mandrel and hammer; record inspects/selects a wheel, aligns multiple rings and flanges, threads a nut, and regulates clamp torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained fractures without insert/shell damage; record requires correct stack order, no damaged wheel, bounded tightening, successful brake-spin and pull tests. Candidate quantitative fracture/damage limits are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both involve axial tool/part alignment, but wheel-stack assembly and torque verification do not test contact-driven fracture or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Finish four threaded inserts by tang removal; record calibrates a colorimeter with a blank and measures a sample.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs impact-tool alignment, bimanual striking, and fragment pickup; record needs cuvette identification/orientation, instrument sequencing, button use, and careful return.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and recovered tangs with no damage; record requires a valid blank reference, wavelength-specific reading, and both cuvettes returned without loss. Candidate numeric physics thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Reference-dependent measurement and vessel handling test a different ability from impact fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Remove four HELICOIL tangs; record adjusts a luggage pull handle to a marked length and leaves its pin locked.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate stabilizes and strikes a small mandrel, then recovers fragments; record unlocks, translates, and re-engages a telescoping detent mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained free tangs and undamaged retained inserts; record requires the handle at its working setting, pin engaged, hands withdrawn, and a two-second hold. The record has no available task spec with numeric rubric details.
comparisons.reason: Detent release and relatching do not test fracture, controlled impact, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Fracture and recover installed-insert tangs; record seats a sleeve while registering its radial oil port.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs recessed coaxial tool alignment plus bimanual hammering; record needs orientation-preserving clearance-fit insertion and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, retained coils, and contained fragments; record requires seated/released stillness and an unobstructed 10 mm passage. Candidate fracture and damage tolerances are not quantified.
comparisons.reason: The shared alignment primitive is generic; port registration through insertion tests a different central ability from impact fracture and debris handling.

comparisons.objective: Finish four HELICOIL inserts by tang removal; record installs and retains a shower-valve cartridge with a U-clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate holds a mandrel coaxially while another hand strikes it; record holds a spring-back cartridge flush while inserting a clip past its ears.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact fractures, four recovered tangs, and no insert/shell damage; record requires flush cartridge alignment, fully seated clip, and retention under a 20 N pull. Candidate quantitative thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both are bimanual constrained operations, but spring-loaded insertion and latching do not test calibrated impact fracture or free-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Break four small metal tangs and recover them; record flexes a build plate to release a printed part and bins it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate regulates localized hammer impact through a coaxial mandrel; record applies coordinated bilateral bending while avoiding permanent plate kinking.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four notch fractures and four contained fragments without coil/shell damage; record requires release by symmetric flex, part in bin, plate restored flat, and no overbend. Candidate fracture/damage thresholds remain unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Both release attached material, but distributed elastic flex release tests a different ability from localized impact-driven fracture.

comparisons.objective: Remove and contain four insert tangs; record uniformly heat-shrinks a cable sleeve.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs precision mandrel alignment, hammering, and fragment search; record coordinates cable rotation with noncontact heat-gun motion and exposure control.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained fractures and no damage; record requires all sleeve stations recovered, adhesive at both ends, no charring/contact, and gun safely stowed. Candidate quantitative damage limits are missing.
comparisons.reason: Controlled thermal exposure over time is unrelated to mechanical notch fracture beyond generic bimanual tool use.
