comparisons.objective: Finish installed inserts by breaking and recovering tangs; record measures subfloor flatness and classifies PASS/FAIL.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs coaxial impact manipulation and tiny-fragment recovery; record places a straightedge, probes the deepest gap with a wedge, and reports a measurement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, all tangs contained, and no retained-part damage; record requires a deepest-gap reading within 0.3 mm and the correct tag. Candidate fracture thresholds are not quantified.
comparisons.reason: Measurement and classification test reference placement and probing, not fracture mechanics or debris control.

comparisons.objective: Break and recover four HELICOIL tangs; record immerses a wafer for a timed interval and returns it to heater pins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate coordinates mandrel stabilization and hammer impact; record maintains plier grip and vertical immersion while separately operating a timer.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained fragments and undamaged inserts/shell; record requires one 28–32 s immersion, correct countdown sequencing, dry hands/handles, and stable wafer return. Candidate numeric force limits are absent.
comparisons.reason: Timed liquid handling and timer coordination test a meaningfully different ability from impact fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Remove four insert tangs; record opens a bottle by sequentially lowering a safety loop and pressing a rocker.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs coaxial mandrel control, bimanual striking, and fragment pickup; record stabilizes a free bottle while operating two passive latch elements in sequence.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, contained tangs, and no damage; record requires a lid angle over 60°, upright support, bounded wrist reaction, and contact-only manipulation. Candidate quantitative physics limits are missing.
comparisons.reason: Sequential latch release is not impact fracture, and the record has no loose-fragment recovery outcome.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks four HELICOIL tangs and recovers them; record flush-cuts a PCB lead and deposits its offcut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual controlled separation and debris handling. Candidate stabilizes a coaxial mandrel for hammer impact, then searches for loose tangs; record positions and closes nippers while the other hand directly restrains the offcut.
comparisons.success_condition: Both demand successful separation plus contained debris. Candidate additionally requires four contact-loaded notch fractures and retained inserts without shell/coil damage; record requires a flush cut, no unheld flight beyond 10 cm, and offcut released in a cup. Candidate fracture, damage, and retention tolerances are not numeric.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record, but it tests shear cutting with proactive offcut capture; the candidate centrally tests impulse-controlled notch fracture through a recessed mandrel, withdrawal without coil displacement, and post-release fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Finish four threaded inserts by tang removal; record loosens a nut with an adjustable wrench.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate aligns and strikes a mandrel; record adjusts jaw play, loads the fixed jaw in the safe direction, pulls through torque, and removes the wrench.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained tangs and no insert/shell damage; record requires at least 60° loosening without rounding or wrong-jaw loading and the wrench set down. Candidate damage thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Torque transfer through a snug wrench and avoidance of rounding do not test impact fracture or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Break and recover insert tangs; record routes a curved board edge using a starting pin and bearing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs small-scale coaxial impact work; record braces and pivots a board onto a bearing, then controls directional feed while maintaining cutter clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and recovered fragments without damage; record requires sufficient routed length, correct pin-assisted entry/feed direction, safe hand clearance, and board clear of the cutter. Candidate numeric damage limits are absent.
comparisons.reason: Machine-feed path control around a curved workpiece is meaningfully different from notch fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Remove and recover four HELICOIL tangs; record snaps a lid around a full hot-drink cup rim.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses a precision mandrel and hammer, then manipulates tiny fragments; record supports a compliant cup while progressively pressing a lid around its circumference.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, contained tangs, retained inserts, and no damage; record requires complete rim engagement without tipping, squeezing, spilling, or unsafe release. Candidate fracture/damage tolerances are not numeric.
comparisons.reason: Progressive snap-fit closure on a crushable filled cup does not test impact-driven fracture or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Finish threaded inserts by breaking and recovering tangs; record safely sorts bottles in a crowded vertical rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed tool alignment, bimanual hammering, and tiny-part recovery; record requires collision-aware extraction, classification, and placement among constrained bottles.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained fractures with inserts and shell intact; record requires correct bottle destinations without drops, collisions, or unsafe rack disturbance. Candidate numeric thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Crowded pick-and-place and sorting do not test controlled fracture or debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Remove four HELICOIL tangs and contain them; record performs an air check through a handhole.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate stabilizes and strikes a narrow mandrel; record manipulates inspection/checking equipment through restricted access and verifies sealing or leakage behavior.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact fractures, four recovered fragments, and no coil/shell damage; record's available evidence centers on completing the handhole air check, with some exact rubric details not explicit in the record summary. Candidate numeric physics limits are also absent.
comparisons.reason: The objectives and central outcomes—fracture/removal versus pressure or leak checking—are clearly different despite restricted-access tool use.

comparisons.objective: Break and recover four insert tangs; record opens an obstructed locker and removes a leaning case upright.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs millimetre coaxial impact manipulation; record manages a coupled door/load interaction while stabilizing and extracting a bulky case.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained fragments and undamaged retained inserts; record requires the locker opened and case removed upright without dropping or unsafe displacement. Candidate quantitative damage limits are missing.
comparisons.reason: Obstruction management and bulky-object extraction test a different physical ability from impact fracture and small-fragment handling.

comparisons.objective: Finish installed inserts by tang removal; record gauges and sorts seven machined blocks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs bimanual hammer/mandrel control and fragment recovery; record sequentially seats parts in GO and NO-GO gaps and sorts them based on physical fit.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, all fragments contained, and no damage; record requires valid ordered gauge checks and all seven blocks in correct trays, heavily penalizing escapes. Candidate numeric damage thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Physical metrology and classification are not the same tested ability as contact-loaded fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Break and recover four HELICOIL tangs; record opens a can with a hand-held rotary opener.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate stabilizes a coaxial mandrel while striking it; record keeps opener handles clamped while repeatedly regrasping and turning a key around the rim.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four notch fractures and four contained tangs without damage; record requires a complete circumferential cut, upright can, opener removed, and hands clear. Candidate force/damage thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Sustained clamp-and-rotate cutting tests regrasped rotary actuation, not impact fracture or loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Remove and recover insert tangs; record removes a drawer by holding two opposite-sense release levers while pulling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate needs precision mandrel stabilization and hammering; record simultaneously actuates opposed latches, pulls a large drawer free, carries it, and sets it down.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and contained fragments with no damage; record requires the drawer fully off both slides, flat and still on the table, and both grippers clear. Candidate quantitative tolerances are missing.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous latch actuation and bulky extraction do not test impact fracture or small debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Finish four threaded inserts by tang removal; record locates a hidden wall screw with a magnetic stud finder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate performs coaxial impact work and fragment recovery; record scans a surface while maintaining flat contact and senses magnetic capture before release.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact fractures, contained tangs, and undamaged inserts/shell; record requires the finder hanging stably with a magnet within 10 mm of a hidden screw. Candidate numeric fracture limits are absent.
comparisons.reason: Search by magnetic interaction and stable hanging test a different ability from controlled mechanical fracture.

comparisons.objective: Break and recover four insert tangs; record releases a disc from a spring hub and inserts it into a console slot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate aligns a narrow mandrel, regulates hammer impact, and retrieves tiny fragments; record coordinates hub depression with edge grasp, reorients a thin disc, and performs close-clearance slot insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, four tangs in a tray, retained inserts, and no damage; record requires hub release and a centered upright insertion deep enough for drive capture, without dropping the disc. Candidate fracture/damage thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Release-plus-thin-object insertion is a meaningfully different tested ability from impact-driven notch fracture and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Mount and orient a boring bar at the correct overhang, then clamp it with two set screws.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coaxial shaft insertion, rotational indexing, depth setting, and sequential hex-key tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Bar correctly oriented at 45–48 mm stick-out, both screws tight, key removed, hands clear, and assembly stable.
comparisons.reason: This tests precision mounting and threaded clamping, not impact fracture of notched tangs or recovery of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Insert a circuit board fully into an antistatic bag and place the bag in a crate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual bag stabilization and broad, thin-part insertion through a compliant-object stand-in.
comparisons.success_condition: Board fully enclosed near the bag end; bag placed, released, and stable in the crate without either item falling.
comparisons.reason: Although both use bimanual stabilization and insertion, this tests planar packaging rather than coaxial mandrel placement, controlled impact fracture, and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Scrub an IV connector hub for 15 seconds before attaching a flush syringe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed wiping around a small medical fitting followed by aligned syringe attachment.
comparisons.success_condition: Required hub surfaces receive the prescribed scrub duration before a correctly attached syringe; contamination or incorrect sequencing fails.
comparisons.reason: The defining abilities are timed decontamination and connector attachment, with no impact fracture or loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Produce a sound L-shaped TIG weld using a torch and filler rod.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous bimanual path following, arc-gap control, heat regulation, and coordinated filler dabbing.
comparisons.success_condition: Joint segments meet bead-quality limits without contamination or burn-through; tools are returned and released.
comparisons.reason: Both require bimanual tool coordination, but welding tests sustained thermal process control along a seam, not discrete hammer impacts and tang recovery.

comparisons.objective: Replace a toilet roll on a spring spindle and refit both spindle ends into sockets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spring compression, one-ended support, constrained steering, socket seating, and roll/tube handling.
comparisons.success_condition: New roll is on the spindle, both ends are seated, old tube is in the tray, hands are clear, and the assembly is stable.
comparisons.reason: This tests spring-loaded socket fitting and exchange of a roll, not fracture at manufactured notches or millimetre-scale metal-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Cut open a taped carton seam without reaching the product below, then retract the blade.
comparisons.physical_skill: Guarded blade-depth control and straight cutting along a long seam.
comparisons.success_condition: The seam is slit over the required length, product remains undamaged, and blade is safely drawn back in.
comparisons.reason: The central ability is controlled continuous cutting with clearance to hidden contents, unlike coaxial impact transfer and post-fracture containment.

comparisons.objective: Perform an insulin pen safety shot and dial a 12-unit dose using the dose window.
comparisons.physical_skill: Needle-up orientation, button actuation, fine rotary dialing, and visual/state verification.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid 2-unit safety shot precedes an accurately indicated 12-unit dose without unsafe needle handling.
comparisons.reason: This tests ordered medical-device operation and dial-state reading, not notch fracture, hammer regulation, or fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Bread every face of a chicken tender while minimizing unnecessary gripping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coverage-aware turning, pressing granular coating onto irregular surfaces, and gentle food handling.
comparisons.success_condition: All faces have adequate breading with limited gripping and without loss or unsafe handling.
comparisons.reason: The task concerns surface coverage and gentle reorientation of food, with no precision tool alignment or impact-mediated separation.

comparisons.objective: Deliver one eye drop into a manikin’s right eye while holding the lower lid down and keeping the bottle tip off the face.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual eyelid displacement, bottle positioning, and single-drop dispensing without contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one drop reaches the target eye while the lid is drawn down and the tip avoids the face; excess drops or contact fail.
comparisons.reason: This tests noncontact liquid dosing and soft-anatomy positioning, not controlled fracture and recovery of solid fragments.

comparisons.objective: Count hex nuts using a desk tally counter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated singulation or tracking of small identical objects coordinated with counter actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: The final tally must equal the bin’s nut count without omissions or double counts; the recovered board record provides limited numeric rubric detail.
comparisons.reason: Small-object handling is generic commonality only; counting does not test mandrel alignment, bimanual hammer impact, fracture, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Release a spring plunger and open a panel held shut by it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plunger retraction against a spring while coordinating panel motion and avoiding re-latching.
comparisons.success_condition: The latch is disengaged and the panel reaches its required open state without dropping or damaging components.
comparisons.reason: This is spring-latch release and articulated-panel opening, not material fracture or recovery of detached pieces.

comparisons.objective: Attach a welding ground clamp in the required order relative to the welding setup.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clamp opening, conductive-jaw placement, cable management, and safety-critical sequencing.
comparisons.success_condition: The clamp is secured at the specified grounding location in the prescribed order, with unsafe or reversed sequencing rejected.
comparisons.reason: The tested outcome is safe electrical setup and clamp placement, not impact-force regulation or removal and containment of tangs.

comparisons.objective: Seat a swivelling tie-rod ball stud squarely in a knuckle’s tapered hole.
comparisons.physical_skill: Control of an articulated swinging linkage, stud-hole alignment, angular correction, and tapered seating.
comparisons.success_condition: The stud is inserted squarely and seated to the specified depth/alignment without jamming, dropping, or false placement.
comparisons.reason: It shares precision alignment and insertion, but its defining ability is controlling an articulated stud into a taper; no impact fracture or free-fragment recovery occurs.

comparisons.objective: Wrap and ratchet a tie-down strap taut around a crate, latch the handle, and withstand a deck jolt.
