comparisons.physical_skill: Operate two passive tools, maintain controlled wafer handling, and clear multiple debris surrogates.
comparisons.success_condition: Body requires debris removal and controlled returns; drops, wafer-face contact, or robot collisions invalidate. Numeric pose/clearance thresholds are not provided in a spec.
comparisons.reason: Fragment/debris removal is a secondary similarity, but this tests non-contact blowing from a held wafer; the candidate tests manufacturing-notch fracture by impact and physical pickup of every resulting tang.

comparisons.objective: Adjust two forearm crutches so their spring buttons fully engage the same marked hole.
comparisons.physical_skill: Press a spring button, slide a telescoping leg through intermediate holes, and align for re-engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both buttons centred within 1.5 mm and protruding at least 3 mm; crutches released and stable, with any drop failing.
comparisons.reason: This is telescoping adjustment and spring-button latching, not mandrel-guided impact fracture or recovery of loose fragments.

comparisons.objective: Push two foam protectors fully onto the bare corners of a supported picture frame.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a compliant L-shaped pocket along two edges while bracing the loose frame.
comparisons.success_condition: Both protectors seated within 4 mm, square/level within 6°, gripping the frame, released and stable; frame or existing-protector disturbance fails.
comparisons.reason: Both require alignment and protection against collateral movement, but this tests compliant press-fitting rather than axial impact fracture and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Transfer a newborn manikin from a bassinet to a changing pad while supporting its head.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual whole-body support across a passive neck joint during lifting and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Neck never exceeds 20° and body never exceeds 30° tilt; manikin ends aligned, released, and stable for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: This tests coordinated support of an articulated load, not precision tooling, controlled hammer impulse, material separation, or small-part recovery.

comparisons.objective: Square a racked gantry beam by moving both rail carriages onto their stops together.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply coordinated forces at both ends to overcome frictional binding without lifting the carriages.
comparisons.success_condition: Both stop gaps at most 0.05 mm, carriages seated, beam stable and grippers clear for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual force coordination is shared only generically; gantry squaring tests synchronized translation against stops, not impact fracture and containment.

comparisons.objective: Pour a simulated molten charge into the dry rather than wet mould.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually lift and tip a crucible shank while selecting the safe mould and controlling spill.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 90% enters dry mould with at most three spilled beads; crucible returned upright and released for 1 s. Any charge in wet mould or direct crucible grasp fails.
comparisons.reason: Its free beads and containment concern arise from pouring, not from producing and recovering fragments through controlled notch fracture.

comparisons.objective: Insert both ends of a two-pin lamp tube into sockets and rotate it to lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual dual-end alignment, simultaneous insertion, coordinated quarter-turn, and detent engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both ends centred within 3 mm, pins seated, both plungers engaged, tube released and stable for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: This is a close dexterity neighbour because it tests bimanual alignment and latching, but its central outcome is dual-end insertion and rotation, not impact-driven break-off and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Remove a retaining bar and open the top drawer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize a mechanical obstruction, slide a loose bar from two sleeves, then pull the drawer.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer opened at least 18 cm; bar removal earns partial credit, while damage or cabinet motion fails.
comparisons.reason: Sequential restraint removal is not equivalent to fracturing a manufactured tang while retaining the surrounding insert and collecting the released piece.

comparisons.objective: Read a diagnostic blink code, replace the indicated module, and verify it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Temporal visual diagnosis followed by keyed module extraction and insertion with detent engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Failed module removed, spare inserted within depth/alignment limits, healthy modules retained, DIAG held for green verification, released and stable 1 s.
comparisons.reason: This is excluded connector/module replacement and verification. It does not test hammer impact, fracture mechanics, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Pause both arms during a human stop signal, then resume and finish boxing cubes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visually triggered interruption and resumption of concurrent manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Combined gripper motion at most 3 cm while signal is raised, then all four cubes boxed; body gives no separate spec.
comparisons.reason: The central ability is human-signal compliance, unrelated to precision mandrel use, impact fracture, insert preservation, or loose-part containment.

comparisons.objective: Place the last cake slice on plate number 1 rather than the nearest plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Read a symbolic label and perform basic pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Cake rests within 6.5 cm of plate 1 centre and at the proper height; otherwise zero.
comparisons.reason: This is semantic target selection plus pick-and-place and lacks the candidate's contact-rich tooling, fracture, damage controls, and fragment accounting.

comparisons.objective: Brace an umbrella while pushing its runner until it latches open, then lift it by the handle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual spring-loaded sliding and latch engagement followed by controlled release and lift.
comparisons.success_condition: Runner reaches latch, hands clear of runner, umbrella lifted by handle with tip raised, stable for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Spring-loaded bimanual actuation is a generic shared primitive; the tested mechanism and outcome are latching an articulated umbrella, not impact fracture and physical recovery of four tangs.

comparisons.objective: Remove a push-and-turn medicine-bottle cap without overturning the vial.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the vial while applying sustained axial pressure and rotary motion to disengage a cap.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap fully off; vial never knocked over; loose cap earns partial credit.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests coaxial mandrel placement, a separately delivered hammer impulse, notch fracture, and recovery of four fragments. Cap unlocking is sustained press-and-turn removal with no impact, fracture, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Move a heavy carton onto a raised platform while keeping it upright.
comparisons.physical_skill: Use the step edge as a pivot, lifting the leading edge and pushing the load past its tipping point.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton released flat and level on the platform; intermediate credit for stable step-bearing states; excessive tilt invalidates.
comparisons.reason: Edge-pivoting a bulk load tests controlled quasi-static tipping and pushing, not tool-mediated impact fracture, coaxial small-part alignment, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Create two required gaps between three parcels on a continuously moving conveyor.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed interception, lifting or repositioning, and release of moving parcels while preserving belt occupancy.
comparisons.success_condition: All parcels pass the scanner on the belt with measured 5 cm gaps; off-belt, stacked, or missing parcels invalidate.
comparisons.reason: Moving-line singulation tests timing and parcel placement. It does not test impact delivery, fracture at a manufactured notch, retained-insert protection, or loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Hang two parts on separate moving overhead-conveyor hooks before a deadline.
comparisons.physical_skill: Track moving hooks and thread large eyes over them, then release without delaying the conveyor.
comparisons.success_condition: Each part hangs freely on its own hook for the specified interval at the mark; interference or conveyor delay prevents full credit.
comparisons.reason: This is moving-target eye-on-hook placement. The candidate's stationary coaxial mandrel alignment, bimanual hammer strike, fracture regulation, and post-fracture fragment recovery are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a 2x2 battery pack by placing a holder in a jig, seating four cells, and fitting the second holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated close-clearance insertion with polarity control and final multi-cell alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Both holder halves and all four cells correctly seated, stable, released, and arms withdrawn; fallen parts invalidate.
comparisons.reason: Although both require precise alignment with four small sites, battery assembly tests placement and press-fitting without impact, intentional fracture, insert-retention constraints, or recovery of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Place a tall canister upright behind a shelf fence despite insufficient upright passage height.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tilt through constrained headroom, pass the base over a fence, and reorient upright.
comparisons.success_condition: Released canister stands behind the fence within position and tilt limits for three seconds.
comparisons.reason: Constrained reorientation through a shelf opening is unrelated to notch fracture with two tools and millimetre-scale fragment retrieval.

comparisons.objective: Knock a spent espresso puck from a held portafilter into a knock box, then return the portafilter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Swing the held container into a bar so abrupt deceleration breaks a weak bond and ejects its contents into containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Puck released into the box, portafilter returned and released; digging, dropping, or knocking outside the box invalidates.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest impact neighbor, but its tested mechanism is inertial ejection by striking the container itself. The candidate instead stabilizes a separate coaxial mandrel while another hand strikes it to fracture a manufactured metal tang, protects a retained coil from lateral load, then searches for and deposits four tiny free fragments. Those are meaningfully different abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Vent only the warm cryostat, wait, remove its sample, and place the sample in a tray without disturbing the cold unit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Status discrimination, ordered button/lid/sample manipulation, and timed procedural restraint.
comparisons.success_condition: Warm sample released in the tray after the required wait; touching the cold unit or moving the warm lid early invalidates.
comparisons.reason: This tests procedural sequencing and hazard avoidance, not impact mechanics, fracture, coaxial tool use, or fragment recovery. No spec versions are available, but the complete body supplies the central objective and scoring distinctions.

comparisons.objective: Balance a loaded service arm by sliding its counterweight, then insert a locking pin and withdraw.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support a free pivot, tune gravitational moment, align pin holes, and insert a retaining pin.
comparisons.success_condition: Arm remains level with the counterweight retained after both hands withdraw.
comparisons.reason: Counterweight balancing and pin insertion are quasi-static equilibrium and alignment tasks. The record omits detailed numeric scoring thresholds, but its mechanism is clearly different from hammer-driven notch fracture and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Lower a glovebox past two sprung stops, replace a keyed cabin filter, and latch the glovebox back up.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual squeezing/latching plus extraction and deep keyed-slot insertion through constrained access.
comparisons.success_condition: Old filter safely removed, new filter seated within position/orientation tolerances, glovebox restored on both stops, all released; broken stops or dropped filters invalidate.
comparisons.reason: This tests simultaneous compliant-stop release and long keyed insertion. It has no intentional impact fracture, struck mandrel, retained threaded insert, or loose-fragment search and containment.

comparisons.objective: Move five fragile upright tiles into a box in as few trips as possible.
comparisons.physical_skill: Batch grasping and transport of multiple fragile plates while preventing slip and tip-over.
comparisons.success_condition: All tiles upright in the box without any fall or tip; score depends on trip count.
comparisons.reason: Batch transport and risk/efficiency tradeoffs do not test tool alignment, controlled hammering, fracture, or recovery of generated fragments.

comparisons.objective: Clamp a printed part upright in a vise at a marked height.
comparisons.physical_skill: One hand holds part pose while the other rotates the vise control to generate clamping force.
comparisons.success_condition: Part is tightly clamped upright with its mark aligned to the jaw tops.
comparisons.reason: Both are bimanual tool/fixture operations, but vise closure tests sustained rotary tightening while holding a workpiece. The candidate tests impulse transfer through a coaxial mandrel, fracture without coil displacement, and fragment retrieval.

comparisons.objective: Cap and shake a cocktail shaker on its side without spilling, then return it upright.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually retain a loose cap while cyclically accelerating and reorienting a container.
comparisons.success_condition: Required tip and reversal counts achieved, contents retained, shaker upright and stable.
comparisons.reason: This tests sustained bimanual closure retention during cyclic motion and spill prevention, not a discrete tool impact, notch fracture, retained-insert protection, or fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Invert a cake pan and plate together, release the cake, and remove the pan.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-handed opposed clamping and coordinated 180-degree rotation of a wide stacked assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Cake rests upside down on the plate on the stand, pan removed, all stable.
comparisons.reason: Coordinated stack inversion and demolding are mechanically different from stabilizing a narrow mandrel for a hammer strike and recovering fractured tangs.

comparisons.objective: Push a packet completely through a spring flap into a drop box.
comparisons.physical_skill: Choose a grasp and insertion strategy that advances the packet beyond a hand-blocking panel and lets the flap close.
comparisons.success_condition: Packet entirely inside and at rest with the flap shut.
comparisons.reason: This is constrained insertion through a compliant flap. It has no impact-induced fracture, bimanual tool interaction, retained-component damage constraint, or small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Reorient a baby bottle mouth-down and hang it over a drying-rack peg.
comparisons.physical_skill: In-hand quarter-turn reorientation and blind hollow-object-over-peg placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle hangs released and stable with the peg sufficiently inserted.
comparisons.reason: Blind peg placement shares generic alignment but not the candidate's contact-loaded fracture, hammer/mandrel coordination, coil protection, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Loosen two media-bottle caps before placing their basket in an autoclave.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize a safety prerequisite, rotate both caps, then push the basket into the chamber.
comparisons.success_condition: Both caps loosened before full insertion; inserting a sealed bottle latches failure.
comparisons.reason: This is procedural safety with screw-cap rotation and basket placement. The complete record has no spec versions, but its objective and staged scoring clearly differ from impact fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Fit an end bracket onto a loose DIN rail, push it flush to terminal blocks, and tighten its screw.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the rail, hook and seat a bracket on both lips, then use a screwdriver to clamp it.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket seated, flush within 0.5 mm, tightened to the target, stable; excess rail motion caps credit.
comparisons.reason: This tests snap/seat geometry and screwdriver tightening. Shared bimanual stabilization is generic; there is no hammer impulse, intentional breakage, retained coil, or generated-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Convert a motor terminal arrangement from delta to the correct star connection for a 400 V supply.
comparisons.physical_skill: Infer the electrical configuration, remove and reseat small conductive links on specified stud pairs.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct star bridges installed and unused link stored; unsafe or incomplete configurations score zero.
comparisons.reason: This tests configuration reasoning and small-link placement rather than force-regulated fracture and recovery. No spec versions are available, but the body explicitly describes the objective, invalid outcomes, and numeric pose checks.

comparisons.objective: Verify names and sample IDs, then route matching and mismatching specimen containers to different trays.
comparisons.physical_skill: Read and compare labels, grasp containers, and place them upright in the correct destinations.
comparisons.success_condition: Both containers correctly routed, supported, stable, and released; a mismatch in PROCESS invalidates.
comparisons.reason: Label verification and semantic routing are unrelated to tool-mediated impact and fracture. The record lacks spec versions and some full rubric geometry, but its central tested ability is unambiguously different.

comparisons.objective: Flatten a springy open-ended carton for recycling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain a steep down-and-over force direction while the carton shears through its crease arc.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton fully flattened, stable on the table, and released; partial folds or rebound score zero.
comparisons.reason: Carton collapse tests distributed quasi-static force along articulated creases, not precision impact through a mandrel, manufactured-notch fracture, or recovery of detached pieces.

comparisons.objective: Join two boards evenly over three dowels.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually align three dowels with three sockets and press both seam corners evenly to avoid wedging.
comparisons.success_condition: Boards fully seated, flush, flat, stable, and released within submillimetre gap limits.
comparisons.reason: Multi-point alignment and even insertion are different from hammer-driven tang fracture. Generic bimanual alignment does not establish overlap, and this task produces no loose fragments or retained-insert damage hazard.

comparisons.objective: Align a DIN rail over two tapped holes, insert two loose screws, and tighten them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold rail alignment, place screws through slots, engage threads, and operate a hex screwdriver.
comparisons.success_condition: Both screws started and tightened while the rail remains flat and aligned; one-second stable final state.
comparisons.reason: This is fastener insertion and rotary tightening. It does not test impulsive fracture, lateral-load regulation on an installed coil, or recovery and containment of broken tangs.

comparisons.objective: Thread a blister card's closed slot over an obstructed scan-hook tip beside existing stock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a thin card, find a shielded wire tip, thread the slot past the upturn, and avoid disturbing adjacent cards.
comparisons.success_condition: New card hangs released beyond the upturn and existing cards remain on the hook.
comparisons.reason: Fine threading near obstacles shares only generic alignment. The candidate additionally requires separate-tool hammering, physical notch fracture, insert retention, and retrieval of four millimetre-scale fragments.

comparisons.objective: Pull a segmented cable to a 30 cm mark, hand it over as needed, and leave it straight.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual handoff, controlled pulling to length, and management of a flexible chain without kinks or over-pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Released cable lies straight within length tolerance; excessive pull, lift, lateral deviation, or fixture movement invalidates.
comparisons.reason: This tests deformable-cable measurement and handoff, not rigid-body tool impact, fracture, retained insert protection, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Reseat one half-inserted network plug; candidate fractures and recovers four installed HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plug pushing among neighboring cords versus coaxial mandrel holding, controlled hammering, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug depth ≥22 mm without disturbing neighbors versus four contact-driven notch fractures, retained coils, and four contained tangs.
comparisons.reason: Insertion is excluded from the candidate and does not test impact fracture or free-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Lift a cord, pass a cart beneath it, and restore the cord; candidate finishes threaded inserts by tang removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable-cord clearance while pushing a cart versus bimanual mandrel stabilization and hammer impact.
comparisons.success_condition: Cart crosses without cord contact and cord is restored versus four safe fractures and physical containment of every tang.
comparisons.reason: Only generic bimanual coordination is shared.

comparisons.objective: Align and slide a carriage onto a rail through a detent; candidate breaks and retrieves insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Close-fit linear insertion and sustained pushing versus coaxial tool placement, impulse regulation, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Carriage seats past the plunger at the stop versus four notch fractures with no coil or shell damage.
comparisons.reason: The detent click is an assembly latch, not controlled destructive separation.

comparisons.objective: Hold an enabling lever while moving a part through a cell; candidate performs HELICOIL finishing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous hold-to-run coordination and part transport versus narrow-tool alignment, hammering, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Lever remains held during motion, then part and lever are safely released versus four fractures and contained tangs.
comparisons.reason: The record lacks a full numeric spec, but its stated safety objective and outcome are clearly unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Hook a wire to fish tape and pull it through bent conduit; candidate removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable hooking and long-path pulling versus rigid coaxial mandrel placement, impact control, and tiny-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Wire end emerges ≥5 cm while the hook remains joined versus four tangs fracture and enter containment without damage.
comparisons.reason: Shared tool use and alignment are generic; the tested mechanisms differ.

comparisons.objective: Sort crumbs into a bin while rescuing a toy ladybird to a pot; candidate performs insert finishing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Object classification and pick-and-place versus bimanual impact tooling and millimetre-scale metal-fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Two crumbs binned and ladybird saved versus four contact-loaded fractures with coil retention and tang containment.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful manipulation outcome overlaps.

comparisons.objective: Fasten a screw through a plate into a nut; candidate fractures and removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual coaxial insertion, thread engagement, and sustained rotation versus mandrel stabilization, hammer impulse, and debris recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Screw caught, turned ≥1.5 rotations, and snug versus four tangs separated at notches without insert displacement.
comparisons.reason: Both concern threaded hardware, but one creates a bolted joint while the other destructively removes manufacturing tangs.

comparisons.objective: Transfer and plug a sterile device cord while preserving sterile zones; candidate finishes threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cable handoff, zone avoidance, and plug insertion versus impact tool alignment and fragment containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Connector ≥15 mm in jack, cord in slot, and no contamination versus four fractures with retained coils and no escaped tangs.
comparisons.reason: Sterility-constrained insertion does not test fracture or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Open a processor socket, key and seat a CPU, then close its shield and lever; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sub-millimetre keyed placement and interlocked latch sequencing versus coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammering, and fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: CPU seated flat within tight pose tolerances and socket locked versus four physical notch fractures and contained fragments.
comparisons.reason: Both require damage avoidance in robot assembly, but their central mechanisms and terminal states differ.

comparisons.objective: Tension and snap a chalk line to leave a straight mark; candidate breaks insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual line tension and vertical pluck-release versus rigid mandrel holding and hammer-delivered fracture impulse.
comparisons.success_condition: One straight print within mark/bow tolerances versus four separated tangs, intact inserts, and physical recovery.
comparisons.reason: Both include a transient impact, but the tested abilities and material outcomes are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Draw a measured liquid dose from a vial into a syringe; candidate performs HELICOIL tang removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Needle placement, syringe stabilization, and plunger metering versus tool coaxiality, controlled hammering, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: 9–11 ml liquid with ≤1 ml air and syringe safely racked versus four safe fractures and all tangs contained.
comparisons.reason: Only generic bimanual stabilization is shared.

comparisons.objective: Uncap and spike an IV bag, then prime its chamber; candidate finishes threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a bag, pull a cap, drive a spike, and squeeze a chamber versus stabilize a mandrel, strike it, and recover fragments.
comparisons.success_condition: Spike locked and chamber one-third to two-thirds full versus four notch fractures with no shell or coil damage.
comparisons.reason: Insertion and priming are not impact-fracture manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Feed flexible filament into a tight printer inlet; candidate removes four HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual flexible-filament straightening and insertion versus rigid narrow-tool alignment, hammering, and loose-fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Filament ≥2 cm deep without kink or spool loss versus four fractures with insert retention and tang containment.
comparisons.reason: Tight alignment is shared, but flexible feeding and controlled fracture test different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Select only the soup utensil appropriate for a person with dementia; candidate performs insert finishing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic selection and cutlery placement versus impact tool use and small-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Spoon on mat and both forks removed versus four tangs fractured and physically contained without damage.
comparisons.reason: No full spec versions are available, but the complete body supplies an unrelated scoring rule.

comparisons.objective: Extract a sample carrier from under a retaining lip while keeping samples upright; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated two-arm sliding and level load transfer versus coaxial tool holding, controlled impacts, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Carrier clears the lip, stays below tilt limits, and rests released on its stand versus four intact-coil fractures and contained tangs.
comparisons.reason: The record has no separate spec version, but its body gives sufficient mechanism and measured success evidence.

comparisons.objective: Load a brush with pollen and stroke two female cucumber flowers; candidate finishes threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Light tool-tip path control across delicate targets versus mandrel coaxiality, hammer impulse regulation, and metal-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Both female stigmas receive strokes after a male-anther stroke versus four safe tang fractures and containment.
comparisons.reason: Shared precision tool use is generic; neither mechanism nor outcome overlaps.

comparisons.objective: Carry a laptop level onto a dock and engage both latches; candidate breaks and retrieves insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual support of a wide load, connector alignment, and symmetric latch seating versus stabilizing a narrow mandrel during impact.
comparisons.success_condition: Laptop level, connector seated, both latches clicked, and no drop versus four fractures, retained coils, and recovered fragments.
comparisons.reason: Docking tests load support and latching, not controlled fracture.

comparisons.objective: Lower a gas-spring overbed table to a marked height; candidate performs HELICOIL tang removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a release paddle while applying regulated downward force versus mandrel alignment, hammering, and fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Height within tolerance, column locked, low tilt, and ≤30 N on shins versus four safe fractures and tang containment.
comparisons.reason: Both use bimanual force coordination, but the controlled mechanisms and outcomes differ.

comparisons.objective: Seat four studs in layout-jig slots against a fence; candidate finishes four threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate large boards into guided slots versus stabilize a millimetre-scale mandrel, deliver impact, and recover tiny fragments.
comparisons.success_condition: Four studs upright, square, seated, and within 2 mm of fence versus four notch fractures with coils retained and tangs contained.
comparisons.reason: Matching object count and repeated alignment do not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Safely isolate dual electrical feeds, replace a cassette, close the guard, and restore power; candidate removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safety-state verification, isolator operation, cassette exchange, and sequencing versus impact fracture tooling and fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Bus proven below 1 V, cassette replaced, guard closed, supplies restored hands-clear versus four safe fractures and containment.
comparisons.reason: The record lacks separate spec versions, but its detailed body establishes a different safety-maintenance ability.

comparisons.objective: Measure and operate a cutter to cut DIN rail to 250 mm; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rail positioning plus lever or clamp/button operation versus coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammer striking, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: First cut within 1 mm with <0.5 mm rail motion versus four contact-driven notch fractures and retained inserts.
comparisons.reason: Both invoke material separation, but the rail task chiefly tests measuring and machine operation; its simulation does not physically cut, while the candidate requires real contact-driven fracture and free fragments.

comparisons.objective: Insert both headrest posts and lock the headrest at its lowest notch; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-post alignment plus simultaneous release-button holding and lowering versus mandrel stabilization, hammer impact, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Both posts seated, lowest pawl engaged, released and stable versus four fractured tangs, intact coils, and physical containment.
comparisons.reason: Latch-controlled insertion is materially different from destructive tang break-off.

comparisons.objective: Orient and nest a gas-burner head around an igniter, then seat its cap; candidate removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual rotational alignment and sequential nested placement versus narrow-tool coaxiality, impact regulation, and tiny-fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Head and cap seated within pose tolerances without dropping versus four safe notch fractures and contained tangs.
comparisons.reason: Both need damage-aware precision, but the tested mechanisms and outcomes differ.

comparisons.objective: Intercept and stop a rolling glass bottle before an edge; candidate performs HELICOIL tang removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dynamic prediction and compliant interception versus deliberate bimanual tool alignment, hammering, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle remains on the surface and still for one second versus four fractures, no component damage, and all tangs in a tray for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful central ability overlaps.

comparisons.objective: Open a clamp meter, enclose one selected motor lead, take a reading, and return the meter; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual trigger operation and threading a sprung jaw between adjacent conductors versus mandrel stabilization, controlled hammering, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Jaw shut around only T2 for three seconds, then meter returned safely versus four notch fractures with intact inserts and contained tangs.
comparisons.reason: Selective enclosure with a sprung tool is not impact fracture or debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Release two spring latches simultaneously, lift a lid, and place it beside a case.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sustained latch retraction and coordinated lid lifting; no impact fracture or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid released, lifted, placed flat and still; partial credit for one/both latches. No damage-force limits are specified.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests coaxial mandrel alignment, controlled hammer fracture at a notch, coil preservation, and recovery of four free fragments—not simultaneous unlatching and cover removal.

comparisons.objective: Plug in a cord, route it through a notch, and close a floor-box cover without pinching it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cable handling, plug insertion, routing, and lid placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug seated at least 15 mm, cord through notch, cover flat and released; pinching or incomplete closure fails.
comparisons.reason: Its central ability is deformable-cable routing during enclosure closure, whereas the candidate requires impact-driven tang fracture and small-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Refuse an expired reagent kit by putting it in a pulled-stock tray and calling a supervisor.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic safety judgment followed by box placement and button pressing.
comparisons.success_condition: Kit in tray and call button actuated; putting the kit in the analyser forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This tests rule-following and disposition of expired stock, not precision tooling, impact regulation, fracture, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Build two stacked trilithons from six slender blocks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential precision placement and gentle release of marginally stable blocks.
comparisons.success_condition: A free-standing two-level structure reaches 18 cm and remains released; the record body supplies staged geometry but no separate task spec.
comparisons.reason: Stable construction from loose blocks is meaningfully different from coaxial tool use and contact-loaded notch fracture with retained-coil and debris constraints.

comparisons.objective: Select photo-matching parts from a conveyor and assemble a model while staging early arrivals.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual discrimination, timed conveyor picking, staging, and sequential assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Target model built without jamming the conveyor or retaining distractors; exact geometric scoring thresholds are absent from the available body.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is perception and scheduling under continuous transport, not force-controlled impact fracture or recovery of manufactured tangs.

comparisons.objective: Remove three remove-before-flight items from an aircraft and stow all of them in a kit bag.
comparisons.physical_skill: Identify, extract, and contain several fitted safety items.
comparisons.success_condition: Each entire item must be removed and bagged; loose removed items receive no credit. Detailed fit, force, damage, and stability thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both require removal and containment, this record extracts reusable whole covers/pins. It does not test mandrel alignment, notch fracture, hammer coordination, or preservation of a surrounding insert.

comparisons.objective: Fit a carriage onto an open-ended undercut rail and push it through a spring detent to the stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Millimetre-clearance slide-fit alignment, insertion, resisted pushing, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Carriage captured under rail lips, within 3 mm lateral and 3 degrees level, past the plunger, within 3 mm of the stop, released and still for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: This tests constrained translational assembly through a detent, not impact-induced separation and physical collection of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Open a folding fan by holding one guard stick while sweeping the other around its pivot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization and controlled arcuate motion against a stiff hinge.
comparisons.success_condition: Fan spread at least 135 degrees, supported on its stand, with arms returned for full score.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization is generic; the fan task tests pivot articulation, while the candidate tests coaxial impact tooling, fracture, and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Register a windowed plate behind an inspection screen despite grasp-induced visual occlusion.
comparisons.physical_skill: View planning, memory or regrasp, and precise released planar registration.
comparisons.success_condition: Released, supported, stable registration within 3 mm for full credit or 12 mm for partial; detailed damage constraints are not given in the body.
comparisons.reason: It tests perception-conditioned placement under occlusion, with no impact, manufactured-notch fracture, retained insert, or fragment-containment outcome.

comparisons.objective: Insert the correctly polarized final magnet into a rotor while preventing its loose neighbor from jumping out.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hold-while-inserting under modeled magnetic forces and pole-order selection.
comparisons.success_condition: Red-topped magnet flush within stated pose tolerances, adjacent magnet never rises over 6 mm, and arms return for full score.
comparisons.reason: Both demand bimanual stabilization, but this record tests force-coupled insertion and polarity; the candidate tests hammer-driven material separation and recovery of four fragments without coil damage.

comparisons.objective: Open two bracket gates, seat a long blind headrail, and close both gates.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-part transport, two-end alignment, seating, and latching.
comparisons.success_condition: Both ends seated on bracket floors and against the back within tight pose tolerances, then both gates shut.
comparisons.reason: This is retained long-part installation with gate sequencing, not precision impact tooling, notch fracture, or loose-fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Seat a glass condenser on a ground-glass cone and snap a joint clip over it while supported.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hold-while-fastening, coaxial glassware alignment, and gentle handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Condenser seated within 5 mm/6 degrees and clipped without prior drop or excessive tip; arms returned for full score.
comparisons.reason: Despite shared coaxial alignment and stabilization, its central outcome is joining and latching intact glassware. The candidate requires calibrated impact fracture, insert retention, and containment of separated tangs.

comparisons.objective: Torque a lug bolt with a click wrench and stop immediately at its one-shot break-over cue.
comparisons.physical_skill: Steady torque application and rapid cessation on tactile/tool motion feedback.
comparisons.success_condition: Click occurs with peak torque in the 90–110% band, no reversal or over-torque, then tool released and still for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate tool-applied load, but this task avoids crossing a torque limit and leaves the joint intact; the candidate must deliberately exceed a notch-fracture threshold through axial hammer impact and recover the debris.

comparisons.objective: Operate a sprung soda lever with a cup, stop at a target fill level, and set the cup down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained contact, alignment under a nozzle, and timing based on fill state.
comparisons.success_condition: Level ends 0.5–2 cm below rim with cup upright and still; overflow, spill, or excessive tip forces zero.
comparisons.reason: This is continuous contact and fill-level control, not impulsive fracture, coaxial mandrel stabilization, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Peel a cucumber's middle surface while leaving both ends intact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual reorientation and repeated surface-following strokes with 1–10 N contact force.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 44 of 48 patches peeled with no gouges; end cuts, blade contact with a gripper, or falling off the board force zero.
comparisons.reason: Although both test force regulation and damage avoidance, peeling is distributed tangential material removal over a surface; the candidate is discrete axial notch fracture followed by loose-part containment.

comparisons.objective: Close only the cabinet doors that begin open without toggling closed doors open.
comparisons.physical_skill: State recognition and selective push-latch actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: All initially open doors latched; actuating any initially closed door forces zero. Exact travel/force thresholds are absent from the body.
comparisons.reason: Selective toggle actuation is unrelated to tool alignment, impact dynamics, fracture, retained-component protection, and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Wind back a screw-type brake piston with a two-pin tool, then seat two pads.
comparisons.physical_skill: Engage face slots while maintaining axial pressure and ratcheting rotation, followed by tight-clearance pad insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Piston face at or below 63 mm and both pads seated within 1–1.5 mm and 3 degrees, released and stable for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: This tests pressure-plus-rotation of a threaded mechanism and subsequent insertion. It neither fractures a sacrificial feature nor creates and contains free fragments.

comparisons.objective: Place a cable plug in a holder while keeping the entire cable clear of a hot-plate zone.
comparisons.physical_skill: Whole-body deformable routing and hazard avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug seated and released, cable on the table and at least 5 cm from the disc; any cable/plug overlap with the disc at any time forces zero.
comparisons.reason: The central ability is safe cable routing around a keep-out region, not rigid precision impact, notch fracture, or small-fragment retrieval.

comparisons.objective: Trace hidden crossed cables, identify two correct plugs, and place each in its matching holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Interactive perception through tugging, deformable cable reasoning, and selective plug placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct two plugs released in their holders; moving distractor plugs over 5 cm, cross-matching, or pulling a cable from its box forces zero.
comparisons.reason: It tests hidden connectivity inference and cable manipulation, with no controlled fracture or retained-insert protection.

comparisons.objective: Pick up and freely roll a die so a marked face turns from up to down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pickup, ballistic/free release, and settling control.
comparisons.success_condition: Marked-face turnover occurs while free and the die rests for 1 s; exact numeric pickup/release tolerances are referenced but absent from the record body.
comparisons.reason: The die task tests intentional free-body turnover, not tool-mediated impact at a manufactured notch or recovery of resulting fragments.

comparisons.objective: Extract a retaining pin while supporting the height of a loaded carriage.

comparisons.success_condition: Pin extracted without dropping the carriage; exact height, pin-travel, force, and hold thresholds are absent from the available body.

comparisons.objective: Use two separate sticks as improvised tongs to lift an unreachable cup from a fire pit onto a stone.

comparisons.success_condition: Cup upright within 10 degrees and centred on the stone, still for 2 s; partial credit when merely outside the pit.

comparisons.objective: Load five glazed pots into a kiln with clearance from pots, posts, and walls.

comparisons.objective: Lower a ratchet-held load to an intermediate tooth, verify the hold, then lower it to a rest.

comparisons.success_condition: Intermediate native tooth hold must support the load after both grippers withdraw, followed by controlled lowering to the rest; numeric pose/force thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: This tests reversible support transfer through a ratchet and pawl, not irreversible notch fracture or fragment cleanup.

comparisons.objective: Choose weights whose total makes a scale read exactly 300 g.

comparisons.objective: Secure a chest with a restraint bolt before loading and closing its drawer.

comparisons.success_condition: Restraint must be fitted before loading; unsecured loading that tips the chest fails. No detailed spec or numeric rubric is available.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety-critical operation ordering and furniture restraint insertion, not coaxial mandrel stabilization, impact fracture, or recovery of small fragments.

comparisons.objective: Bimanually shake a loaded sieve so soil passes through while pebbles remain.
comparisons.physical_skill: Level two-handle lifting and sustained controlled shaking of granular contents.
comparisons.success_condition: Pass specified quantities of 72 crumbs into the tub, retain every pebble, and return the sieve to its battens. No separate spec is available.
comparisons.reason: Tests dynamic sifting and material separation, not localized notch fracture with a mandrel and hammer or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: After a printer cools, replace its used print plate with a clean plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Signal-conditioned bimanual level carrying and plate placement around locating pins.
comparisons.success_condition: Wait for green, keep the loose print aboard, place the used plate flat on its rest, fit the clean plate flat on the bed, release, and stabilize for one second.
comparisons.reason: Tests delayed plate exchange and level transport; it has no impact tool use, fracture, retained insert, or loose tang recovery.

comparisons.objective: Pull out a spring-return tape and make one accurate mark at 300 mm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold a sprung slider while positioning and dabbing a pen.
comparisons.success_condition: Make one measured mark within 4 mm of 300 mm with the tape extended past it, then lift the pen and hold the state for one second.
comparisons.reason: Although both tasks stabilize a narrow tool bimanually, this tests measurement and marking against spring return, not impact fracture and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Insert a spindle through an electrode-roll core, carry the roll, and deposit both spindle ends on rests.
comparisons.physical_skill: Through-bore insertion, two-end load support, and coordinated rigid-load transport.
comparisons.success_condition: Exclude direct roll handling, seat both spindle ends on their rests, release, and maintain a stable one-second hold. No full numeric spec is available.
comparisons.reason: Tests using an inserted spindle as a load-bearing carrier; the candidate uses a mandrel to transmit an impact and must fracture and recover four tangs.

comparisons.objective: Turn three cartons on moving carriers so their labels face a fixed scanner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed reorientation of moving objects without toppling or retaining contact.
comparisons.success_condition: At each gate crossing, the carton must be upright, centered on its carrier, released, never table-touched, and label-aligned within 20 degrees.
comparisons.reason: Tests moving-line interception and timed orientation, with no insertion, force-controlled fracture, or fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Select and fit a wrench, loosen a captive latch nut, and open the released arm.

comparisons.success_condition: Release the captive clamp without rounding the nut, open the arm, and demonstrate a 20-second hands-free hold; the preserved rubric does not independently score wrench return.
comparisons.reason: This is the nearest tool-mediated fastener task, but it tests rotary loosening and latch release rather than axial mandrel alignment, hammer impact, notch fracture, and loose-part recovery.

comparisons.objective: Release a catch, raise and rotate a swing handle, then open an enclosure lid.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential catch actuation, handle manipulation, and lid opening.
comparisons.success_condition: Open the target lid beyond 60 degrees and leave it untouched for 20 seconds. No detailed numeric spec is available.
comparisons.reason: Tests a multi-stage enclosure latch mechanism, not impact-driven consumable-feature removal or millimetre-scale debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Refit a spring-plunger insect screen into upper and lower window channels.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual large-frame alignment, spring compression, swing-in insertion, and controlled lowering.
comparisons.success_condition: Seat both edges in their channels, keep plungers bearing, avoid drops or frame penetration, release, and remain stable for one second.
comparisons.reason: Shares alignment and force regulation only generically; it tests compliant large-part channel insertion rather than tool-mediated fracture and recovery of four fragments.

comparisons.objective: Progressively seat a flexible power cord along a curved channel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential deformable routing and distributed pressing along a bend.
comparisons.success_condition: All eight channel sections must contain the cord below the lip for one second without moving the fixtures or pulling the cord from its box.
comparisons.reason: Tests global deformable-object routing and seating, not rigid coaxial tooling, discrete impact fracture, or loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Hang a cable in two cradles with a specified free sag.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual deformable placement and global slack regulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Both ends must hang outside their hooks, sag must be 4–6 cm, fixtures must remain fixed, and the released cable must rest for one second.
comparisons.reason: Tests cable shape and slack control; the candidate tests localized impact mechanics, insert retention, and recovery of fractured metal tangs.

comparisons.objective: Place a lid in a case pocket and press until two snap latches engage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual case bracing, close planar alignment, and controlled latch seating.
comparisons.success_condition: Both latches clicked, lid centered and aligned in the pocket, case not displaced or tipped, grippers withdrawn, and state still for one second.
comparisons.reason: Both involve force while protecting a retained assembly, but snap-fit engagement is the opposite mechanical outcome from fracturing sacrificial tangs and collecting the released pieces.

comparisons.objective: Identify the higher-friction sled using a mass-controlled experiment and place it on a mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load equalization, launcher operation, observation, comparison, and object sorting.
comparisons.success_condition: Launch both sleds at equal total mass without hitting the end wall, infer the shorter-sliding sled, and place only it on the red mat.
comparisons.reason: Tests experimental control and physical-property inference, not dexterous tooling, fracture, or debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Transfer a wafer carrier through an interlocked two-gate airlock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered gate operation and handoff while keeping a carrier in its lane.
comparisons.success_condition: Move the carrier to the left stop, never open both gates simultaneously, keep it on the lane, and finish with both gates shut. No detailed spec is available.
comparisons.reason: Tests interlock-safe sequencing and transfer, with no precision impact, retained insert, or small-fragment manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Unload five blocks from a motorized carousel while another robot keeps loading it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed interception, pick-and-place, and collision avoidance in a shared robot workspace.
comparisons.success_condition: Score by the fraction of five blocks in the crate; any contact between the arms zeros and stops the run.
comparisons.reason: Tests throughput and shared-workspace timing rather than coaxial tooling, fracture-force control, or containment of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Seat chocks on both sides of a rolling cradle before removing its load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization setup followed by restrained load extraction and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both chocks must remain seated while the load moves, and the load must reach the storage pad; low removal without restraint fails. No detailed spec is available.
comparisons.reason: Tests prerequisite stabilization of mobile equipment before load removal, not a supported tool strike or fracture-and-recovery sequence.

comparisons.objective: Put a drain pan under an engine outlet before removing its drain plug and store the plug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered pan placement, axial plug extraction, and small-part placement.
comparisons.success_condition: The pan must remain under the outlet whenever the plug is out; full score also requires the plug in the parts dish.
comparisons.reason: It shares ordered removal and containment of a small part, but tests direct plug extraction and spill prevention, not coaxial impact fracture while preserving an insert and recovering four newly freed tangs.

comparisons.objective: Declutch a powerless valve actuator and turn its handwheel closed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual lever holding, rotary regrasping, and detection of clutch engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Engage the clutch, close within 5 degrees of the stop, and hold for three seconds; turning while uncoupled scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Tests mode engagement followed by sustained rotation, not impact transmission, sacrificial-feature fracture, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Crack an egg on a bowl rim, pull its shell apart, deposit contents, and tray both shell halves.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual impact initiation, controlled separation, and sorting of contents and fractured shell.
comparisons.success_condition: Crack then open the egg, place yolk and at least five white drops in the bowl, place both shell halves only in the tray, retract, and hold still.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest fracture-and-recovery record, but it tests deformable food opening by direct bimanual pulling and content separation; the candidate tests tool-mediated notch fracture inside retained precision inserts using stabilized mandrel impacts.

comparisons.objective: Solve a sliding-number puzzle by moving rigid tiles through an empty cell.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential planar tile manipulation within a constrained tray.
comparisons.success_condition: Tiles must reach the solved arrangement within millimetre tolerances, remain seated and correctly oriented, and be released. No staged rubric is available.
comparisons.reason: Tests rearrangement planning and planar sliding, with no tool use, force threshold, fracture, or debris collection.

comparisons.objective: Match a generator's speed and close its breaker at the correct synchroscope phase.
comparisons.physical_skill: Instrument reading, button control, temporal regulation, and precise action timing.
comparisons.success_condition: First match pointer speed, then make the single effective CLOSE press within the allowed phase window; premature or unmatched closure scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Tests procedural knowledge and timing on a control panel, not contact-rich dexterous manipulation or fracture mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Exchange an AI-server cooling module while ignoring a malicious sticker targeting a protected drive.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring retainer, swap and park a module, and avoid manipulating a protected component.
comparisons.success_condition: Complete the C1 exchange and withdrawal; any sampled D1 disconnection permanently zeros the score. Detailed geometric thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests instruction hierarchy and protected-component avoidance during module exchange, not impact fracture, insert retention, or loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Move a fragile egg off a trivet before placing a pot there.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gentle obstruction removal followed by stable heavier-object placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Keep the egg supported, avoid pot–egg contact above 0.20 N or any fall, and release a stable pot on the cleared trivet.
comparisons.reason: Shares damage avoidance and force sensitivity only generically; it tests prerequisite obstacle relocation rather than intentional controlled fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Move two museum tankards one at a time by their bodies onto padded marked spots.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rule-constrained grasp selection and sequential fragile-object transport.
comparisons.success_condition: Use body grasps, never lift by handle or rim, never have both objects off the table together, and place both on their spots. Exact placement thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests conservation handling rules and grasp semantics, not coaxial tools, impact control, or recovery of fractured parts.

comparisons.objective: Determine which visually identical bottles are empty by lifting, then recycle only those.
comparisons.physical_skill: Active weight sensing, classification, and careful sorting.
comparisons.success_condition: Both empty bottles must stand in the bin; any full bottle in the bin, tipped bottle, or fallen bottle zeros the result.
comparisons.reason: Tests hidden-property inference through lifting and selective sorting, not impact-driven material separation or precision fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Rotate manifold fittings to establish a leak-free coolant route.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plan connectivity and turn several large indexed swivels by contact; no impact, fracture, or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Outlet connected with no open end; hands clear for 1 s. No damage rubric is specified.
comparisons.reason: Tests routing and rotary configuration, not coaxial mandrel placement, controlled tang fracture, and recovery of four released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Transfer a loaded tray from temporary support to a receiving shelf before withdrawing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support and transport a tray while retaining two tins; no small-tool alignment or impact.
comparisons.success_condition: Body reports tray transfer, contents retained, and hand withdrawal, but provides no numeric scoring rubric or specs.
comparisons.reason: Load transfer and retention are meaningfully different from contact-loaded insert finishing and loose tang collection.

comparisons.objective: Aim a loaded inspection arm to +15 degrees and lock its clamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: One arm supports a load while the other tightens an indexed clamp; bimanual stabilization is shared, but there is no striking, fracture, or fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Arm must retain elevation for 2 s after both grippers withdraw; numeric angle tolerance is not given in the record.
comparisons.reason: Its tested ability is support-while-locking a joint, whereas the candidate tests coaxial impact delivery, notch fracture, coil protection, and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Sort only cast red, blue, and blank ballots into their matching trays.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic selection and token pick-and-place while excluding an uncast ballot.
comparisons.success_condition: All three cast tokens in correct trays; any placement of the outside ballot in a tray invalidates success.
comparisons.reason: Tests provenance-aware sorting, not precision tool alignment, impact regulation, fracture, or retained-insert protection.

comparisons.objective: Stand a wide flat box on edge in a narrow slot using a riser.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual compression lift, ledge placement, tipping, and large-object reorientation.
comparisons.success_condition: Box upright within 20 degrees, positioned in the slot and still for 2 s; denting beyond 5 mm triggers replacement on reset.
comparisons.reason: Large-object lifting and tipping do not test impact fracture or millimetre-scale fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Open the clean-ice bin and serve clean ice with a scoop without contamination.
comparisons.physical_skill: Source discrimination, lid handling, scooping, and delivery.
comparisons.success_condition: At least one clean cube delivered without contamination; the record gives no numeric containment or damage thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Serving from the correct source is different from breaking retained insert tangs and recovering every fracture product.

comparisons.objective: Support an optical bar before withdrawing its carriage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered bimanual load transfer with continuous support and actual carriage clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Full transfer and carriage withdrawal are reported, but the record omits the complete numeric scoring rubric.
comparisons.reason: Tests support substitution and safe withdrawal, not impact-tool use, notch fracture, or loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Raise probes, index a wafer, then restore probe contact without scratching.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hold-aside and stage motion with cumulative contact-damage avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct wafer index and restored probes with zero latched scrape; exact pose and travel thresholds are absent from the record.
comparisons.reason: Both penalize damaging lateral contact, but the central ability here is damage-free indexed motion under raised probes, not controlled impact fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Hold a spring-loaded leaf aside while pouring water onto soil, then restore the scene.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual obstruction holding, controlled pouring, and spill/contamination avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Current specs require at least 90 ml on soil, at most 10 ml on leaves, jug and leaf restored, arms returned, and 1 s stability.
comparisons.reason: Tests liquid delivery around a compliant obstruction; shared bimanual coordination does not cover coaxial striking, fracture, or tiny rigid-fragment search.

comparisons.objective: Open a caught cabinet, remove a multimeter, place it on the bench, and re-latch the door.
comparisons.physical_skill: Handle-following along a hinge arc, object retrieval, placement, and catch engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Four ordered stages, arms returned, parts still for 1 s; falls or cabinet tilt over 20 degrees invalidate.
comparisons.reason: Cabinet access and tool retrieval differ from insert finishing by controlled impact and mandatory recovery of fracture debris.

comparisons.objective: Shear a racked face frame until its diagonals are equal while keeping it in bounds.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual opposed-force shaping with low-force regulation and no lifting or joint overtravel.
comparisons.success_condition: Diagonal difference at most 2 mm, released and still for 1 s; lifting, leaving the outline, or 15 mm overtravel latches failure.
comparisons.reason: This tests quasi-static frame squaring, not localized impact fracture, coaxial mandrel control, or fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Place a drill guide in the only structurally permitted joist-boring zone.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rule-based spatial selection and stable guide placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Binary correct-zone placement with release; the record describes tested exclusions but omits the full scorer's numeric pose tolerance.
comparisons.reason: Tests interpreting safe drilling-location rules, not performing an impact-driven finishing operation.

comparisons.objective: Lift a rabbit surrogate into a carrier while continuously supporting its back.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated two-point support and level transport of an articulated load.
comparisons.success_condition: Rabbit deposited in carrier; spine bend over 25 degrees or a fall of at least 3 cm irreversibly scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Tests distributed support of an articulated body rather than tool-on-feature alignment, fracture control, and small-part recovery.

comparisons.objective: Orient a pressure-relief cushion correctly and fit it flat into a wheelchair.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize functional orientation, execute two quarter turns with regrasping, and lower into side clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct orientation within 20 degrees, flat and positioned in the seat; wrong orientation scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Reorientation and constrained placement are unrelated to impact fracture and complete debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Seat both ends of a quick-release wheel axle and close the lever in the safe direction.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual axle/dropout alignment, insertion, and over-centre latch operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Both axle ends fully seated and lever closed along/rearward of fork; premature closure or closure while unseated invalidates success.
comparisons.reason: Although it includes precision insertion and latching, it tests assembly seating rather than controlled notch fracture and recovery of released tangs.

comparisons.objective: Raise a piano lid, set its prop into the cup, and lower the lid safely onto it.
comparisons.physical_skill: One arm continuously supports a load while the other aligns and inserts a hinged prop.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid rests unsupported by grippers on the seated prop; a detected lid fall irreversibly scores zero. Exact final tolerances are not supplied.
comparisons.reason: Support-and-prop insertion is a different tested mechanism from bimanual hammering, fracture-load regulation, and debris recovery.
