comparisons.objective: Transfer five glass slides into individual staining-rack grooves while keeping them upright and undamaged.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-object grasping and low-clearance slot insertion; no bimanual tool-on-tool striking or intentional fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: Five slides upright, centered, seated, alone, at rest, and released for 1 s; excessive tipping or table departure invalidates a slide. No impact or fragment-recovery criteria exist.
comparisons.reason: Although both require precise alignment with narrow openings, this tests fragile slide placement rather than stabilizing a mandrel during impact, breaking notches, and containing released pieces.

comparisons.objective: Eject a used pipette tip, force-seat a fresh tip, and return the pipette to its stand without touching either tip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool handling, passive-ejector actuation, axial seating force, and redocking; no hammering or deliberate component fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: Rewards disposal, fresh-tip seating, and pipette redocking; touching tips, unintended release, dropping, or tipping invalidates the run. Exact numeric seating and final-stability thresholds are absent from the record.
comparisons.reason: Shared axial alignment and force regulation are generic primitives; the tested outcome is contamination-safe tip replacement, not notch fracture and exhaustive fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Rotate both faucet handles to fully open.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous bimanual grasping and 120-degree in-hand rotation of square knobs; no tool alignment, impact, fracture, or recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Each handle scores when within 15 degrees of open and still seated. Release, damage, stability-duration, and force thresholds are not specified.
comparisons.reason: Tests coordinated rotary control of two retained knobs, meaningfully different from impact-driven tang removal and containment.

comparisons.objective: Power on a bench supply, set its voltage knob to 9 V, and leave other controls and the unit unchanged.
comparisons.physical_skill: Button pressing, knob grasping, precise wrist rotation, and arm retraction; no striking or fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Supply on, voltage within 0.2 V, knob released, other controls within 3 degrees, supply within pose tolerances, arms returned, and 1 s stillness; tipping/falling invalidates.
comparisons.reason: The precision feedback task changes a control setting rather than causing a validated fracture while protecting a retained insert and recovering debris.

comparisons.objective: Release a captive multistage bayonet sleeve through a spring-loaded internal track and rotational reversal, then place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained push/rotate/reverse manipulation and removal against spring/contact geometry; no hammer-and-mandrel impact or small-fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Released stationary sleeve earns partial credit; full success requires it in the parts tray with 20 s hands-off. Exact alignment, damage, and force limits are not stated.
comparisons.reason: Both culminate in recovered hardware, but this tests reversible bayonet-track extraction of one sleeve, not fracture of four notched tangs while retaining surrounding coils.

comparisons.objective: Move a heavy chest onto a rug without dragging it across a wood floor.
comparisons.physical_skill: Symmetric bimanual handle grasping, lifting, carrying, and controlled set-down; no precision tooling or impact.
comparisons.success_condition: Lift, carry, and place on rug; accumulated sliding of 2 cm or more while floor-contacting permanently zeros the score. Final release/stability tolerances are not detailed.
comparisons.reason: Tests load sharing and floor-safe transport, unrelated to coaxial impact fracture and millimetre-scale debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Aim a registered inspection camera at a target while preserving its pivot datum.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coupled adjustment of two passive controls with datum-preserving force application; no striking, fracture, or loose-part containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Settled camera axis must intersect the target, pivot must remain registered throughout, and both hands must be clear. Numeric aim, datum, clearance, and settling thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests kinematic aiming under registration constraints rather than destructive notch completion and recovery of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Seat a swing-top bottle stopper and push its lever through an over-centre toggle while steadying the bottle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual bracing, hinged-part sequencing, and force through a resistance peak; no hammer-mediated fracture or fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Lever past centre with stopper within 5 degrees of seat; bottle upright under 10 degrees, grippers at least 3 cm clear for 2 s; any 30-degree tip zeros the run.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate transient force while the other hand stabilizes something, but the bottle task tests over-centre latching of retained parts, not impact fracture and debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Pull four cans to a shelf edge while keeping them upright and on the shelf.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated planar translation and placement stopping; no narrow-tool alignment, bimanual striking, or recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Each can must be upright within 10 degrees, under 1 cm/s, directly on the board, and within the stated edge band. No release-distance or hold-duration threshold is specified.
comparisons.reason: Tests shelf-facing placement precision, not controlled fracture or containment of loose metal fragments.

comparisons.objective: Feed a cable plug through a panel grommet, hand it between arms, and pull the cable until its marked band reaches the panel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable-chain routing, aperture insertion, cross-panel hand-off, and pulling over an obstacle; no impact tool use.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable must traverse only the bore, plug must clear the far face and duct wall, and band must be within 2 cm for 1 s; fixture damage, grommet displacement, or cable pullout zeros the score.
comparisons.reason: Shared aperture alignment is generic; this tests routing and hand-over of an articulated cable, unlike notch fracture and independent fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Register an aluminum block flat and square against both faces of a corner stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hand-off, planar pose correction, and two-face contact registration; no impact, intentional breakage, or small-object recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Full score requires at most 1 mm gaps, at most 2 degrees angular error, flatness within stated limits, and 1 s stillness.
comparisons.reason: Tests fixture registration of an intact workpiece rather than stabilizing a mandrel, delivering a controlled blow, and accounting for every released tang.

comparisons.objective: Align a bayonet cap with keyed slots, push against a spring, and quarter-turn it into a locked state.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed coaxial insertion plus sustained axial force and rotation; no separate striking tool or fracture/recovery stage.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap axis within 3 mm, upright within 10 degrees, lugs rotated over 80 degrees and retained at height, both grippers 3 cm clear, and still for 1 s; excessive box movement invalidates.
comparisons.reason: This is a close neighbor in alignment and contact-constrained insertion, but it tests assembly/latching of an intact cap rather than impact fracture, coil protection, and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Stand one slat on a mark and slide two crossing slats down so their slots interlock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual support of an unstable member and repeated slot alignment/insertion; no hammer impact or deliberate breakage.
comparisons.success_condition: Both crossings interlocked within 6 mm positional and 4 mm height tolerances, all slats upright, base aligned within 2 cm/5 degrees, and still for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual stabilization and alignment do not erase the different tested outcome: constructing two half-lap joints versus fracturing and recovering four tangs without disturbing inserts.

comparisons.objective: Use a pin tool to depress and release two recessed spring plungers, then return the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precision grasping, recessed coaxial tool placement, controlled axial pressing, and redocking; no hammering or fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Each plunger must travel at least 8 mm, be held briefly, and return after release; tool returned and both grippers open. Hold duration, damage, alignment, and final-stability thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: This is a close neighbor for narrow-tool alignment in recessed wells, but it tests reversible spring travel rather than impact-loaded notch fracture and containment of detached pieces.

comparisons.objective: Arrange five cartons on two pads so no stack exceeds three times its base dimension.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object placement, stacking-order reasoning, orientation choice, and hand-off; no tooling or impact.
comparisons.success_condition: Each correctly seated/centered carton scores; any stack exceeding its base-derived height limit zeros the overall score. Numeric seating/centering and stability thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests geometric stability planning and stacking, unrelated to fracture mechanics, insert retention, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Brace a spot welder, pull its USB-C plug straight out by the plug body, set the plug down, and place the welder in a holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual bracing and low-clearance axial extraction followed by object insertion; no impact or intentional component fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug removed by a gripper and placed down, welder lifted and seated within 5 mm/upright within 10 degrees, arms returned, and welder still for 1 s; drops or battery displacement zero the run.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization and force direction are shared, but this tests nondestructive connector extraction and storage, not striking a mandrel to break notches and collecting all debris.

comparisons.objective: Sort two cloths into toilet and kitchen buckets according to a color code.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic classification and coarse pick-and-place; no precision insertion, impact, force regulation, or fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Cloths must rest with centers inside their assigned bucket walls; wrong red-cloth placement forces zero. Release-distance and stability thresholds are not quantified.
comparisons.reason: Tests rule-based sorting, with no meaningful overlap in the candidate’s fracture-and-recovery ability.

comparisons.objective: Place a relief block safely ahead of a mock saw blade, then register a board against it and a miter gauge.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-arm dependent fixture setup and hazard-zone-aware placement; no striking, breakage, or debris recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: The record states the relief block must be at least 2 cm ahead of the blade and the board must touch it for a 60 mm offcut; complete pose, release, stability, and zero-rule thresholds are not provided.
comparisons.reason: Tests safe setup geometry and ordered placement, not contact-loaded fracture or small-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Read a six-note card and strike the correct bars in time using one mallet in each hand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual rhythmic striking, timing, target selection, and mallet rebound; it does not stabilize a coaxial mandrel or recover fractured material.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct six-note sequence at half-second intervals with alternating arm groups; wrong or late notes are irreversible. Exact timing windows, impact thresholds, release, damage, and final-state criteria are missing.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record for controlled impacts, but it tests timed dual-mallet percussion; the candidate tests asymmetric stabilization/hammering, physical notch fracture, insert protection, and exhaustive fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a castle nut to the next slot and insert a cotter pin through the aligned slot and stud hole without backing off.
comparisons.physical_skill: Torque-direction reasoning, nut rotation, precision pin grasping, coaxial insertion through multiple apertures, and release; no hammer impact or fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut must be advanced clockwise to alignment and pin passed through; more than 5 degrees anticlockwise permanently zeros the score. Final pin tolerances, release distance, and stability duration are not stated.
comparisons.reason: A close neighbor for small-part alignment and insertion, but it secures an assembly by adding a pin rather than removing notched tangs through impact and recovering debris.

comparisons.objective: Repose two friction-jointed helping-hands fixtures so two wire ends cross over a marked location.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulating coupled passive joints by their clip bodies and coordinating two retained wire ends; no striking or loose-part recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Wire ends must cross over the yellow mark and both fixtures must remain after release. Numeric crossing, contact, release, and stability tolerances are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests coupled pose adjustment and maintained alignment, not fracture mechanics or containment.

comparisons.objective: Load a plate on each dumbbell sleeve and secure each with a collar.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual plate-hole alignment, sliding insertion, collar placement, and push-home finishing; no impact fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: Plates within 1 cm of flanges and collars no more than 6 mm outside them; any plate left on a sleeve without a locked collar zeros the end score. Final release/stability tolerances are not specified.
comparisons.reason: Shared coaxial insertion and safety constraints are insufficient for overlap; this tests assembly and retention of large parts, not tang fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Fill a bath while enforcing cold-first activation and hot-first shutdown.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered bimanual lever rotation and state monitoring; no tool alignment, impact, fracture, or fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Hot water running without cold at either transition permanently zeros the run; partial stages cover cold on, both on, and fill level. Exact final fill and lever tolerances are not given in the record.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety-critical action ordering on controls, unrelated to the candidate’s physical fracture-and-containment outcome.

comparisons.objective: Rearrange kitchen-rack items so frequently used objects occupy the middle shelf and a rare item does not.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic frequency reasoning and multi-level pick-and-place; no impact tooling or precision fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: Items must be on specified shelves, base within 8 mm, tilt under 15 degrees, and still; stacking or leaving items beside the rack earns nothing. Release is not checked.
comparisons.reason: Tests accessibility-aware storage planning rather than bimanual impact control, insert preservation, and recovery of all detached tangs.

comparisons.objective: Fit a foam sleeve over a spoon handle, then release the assembled spoon.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hold-and-thread with sustained sliding alignment and millimetre clearance; no impact fracture or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 8 cm of coaxial handle coverage, assembly still on the table, and grippers at least 10 cm clear.
comparisons.reason: The tested outcome is frictional sleeve threading, not notch fracture by a stabilized impact tool or containment of released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Clip a sprung plate guard onto a plate without displacing the plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Brace a light plate while pressing a beveled spring jaw over its rim.
comparisons.success_condition: Guard seated at least 9 mm, plate flat and displaced less than 1.2 cm throughout, objects still, and grippers clear.
comparisons.reason: Although both regulate lateral force near a retained component, this tests spring-clamp seating and bracing rather than impact-induced fracture and loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Put food and scented toiletries into a bear canister and lock its lid.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object packing followed by lid placement and quarter-turn locking.
comparisons.success_condition: All four required items inside before the lid is turned to the locked orientation.
comparisons.reason: This tests semantic item selection, packing, and lid rotation; it has no precision impact, sacrificial-feature fracture, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Safely remove battery-pack busbars after service-plug isolation and live-dead-live verification.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safety-sequenced plug extraction, meter probing, nut driving, and conductive-part handling.
comparisons.success_condition: The body states the service plug and verification must precede nut removal and that parts must not bridge terminals; numeric scoring and tolerances are absent.
comparisons.reason: The central ability is electrical isolation and sequenced disassembly, not mechanical notch fracture by hammer and mandrel. Missing numeric rubric details do not create plausible overlap.

comparisons.objective: Secure a spring-loaded tote lid using a loose elastic strap and two hooks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual elastic routing, hook engagement, and restraint against an upward load.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid gap below 3 mm for 20 seconds after release, with overload, snap-back, and penetration vetoes.
comparisons.reason: This tests tensioned flexible restraint and hook placement, not controlled impact fracture or recovery of small released pieces.

comparisons.objective: Measure a steak in its thickest meat area while avoiding bone and fat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp and insert a probe at a safe location, hold it still, then return it to its holder.
comparisons.success_condition: Probe held in the thick strip loin for 1.5 seconds; readings near bone, fat, or outside the target permanently fail.
comparisons.reason: The narrow-tool alignment primitive is generic, but the tested ability is safe probing and location choice, without impact, breakage, or fragment handling.

comparisons.objective: Fasten an instrument case using separate spring hooks, tensioning levers, and safety catches.
comparisons.physical_skill: Choose keepers, engage hooks, tension levers, and set independent secondary catches.
comparisons.success_condition: Closed case remains fastened for 20 seconds without contact while cases and instruments stay upright; detailed numeric geometry is not present in the record.
comparisons.reason: It tests multi-stage latch fastening under tension rather than fracture of sacrificial tangs and containment of resulting fragments.

comparisons.objective: Place a 911 call through a locked phone's emergency interface without attempting a passcode.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precise glass touches and swipe/tap sequencing with correction of interface input.
comparisons.success_condition: Clean emergency-route 911 call sustained for 3 seconds with nothing touching the glass; any passcode attempt vetoes the trial.
comparisons.reason: This is touchscreen interaction and safety reasoning, physically unrelated to bimanual hammering, contact-loaded fracture, and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Hold a wafer with pliers while sweeping a blow gun across its face to remove particles.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual delicate holding and noncontact tool sweeping over a fragile surface.
comparisons.success_condition: Complete the handling sequence, remove all twelve modeled particles, and return wafer and gun to supports; the record gives no numeric force or clearance thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Both use two coordinated tools, but wafer cleaning tests controlled sweeping and particle removal, not impact delivery, notch fracture, or physical collection of generated fragments.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve a charger from behind a box by manipulating its cord and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable-cord pulling along a constrained gap, tension awareness, and object retrieval without moving an obstacle.
comparisons.success_condition: Charger released in the tray while the box stays within 2 cm and 10 degrees and neither object leaves the table.
comparisons.reason: Fragment containment in a tray is only a generic final placement similarity; this task centrally tests cable-mediated occluded retrieval and wedge avoidance, not fracture creation.

comparisons.objective: Sort six good biscuit packs from a moving belt into cases while rejecting two cracked packs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fast bimanual perception, selection, and repeated pick-and-place from a moving conveyor.
comparisons.success_condition: Six good packs occupy case cells before the red line while cracked packs pass; the record supplies no finer numeric scoring rubric.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is throughput-limited dynamic sorting, with no precision tooling, impact fracture, or small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Clear a block from a sliding-door track and fully open the door without derailment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Diagnose an obstruction, remove it, and coordinate sequential reaches to slide a constrained panel.
comparisons.success_condition: Door reaches within 2 cm of the end stop, remains within track alignment limits, block stays on the table, and both are still for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: This tests obstruction removal and prismatic door motion; removing a preexisting block is not equivalent to creating and recovering fracture fragments.

comparisons.objective: Issue ABO-compatible red-cell units to three patient trays.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rule-based item selection and bimanual handover/placement.
comparisons.success_condition: O goes to O and A patients, B to the B patient, and AB remains stored; the record does not provide numeric pose or stability thresholds.
comparisons.reason: The central challenge is compatibility reasoning and allocation rather than contact mechanics, tooling, fracture, or debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Place coins totaling exactly 70p into a change dish.
comparisons.physical_skill: Read values, perform arithmetic, and pick and place selected small rigid objects.
comparisons.success_condition: Coins resting in the dish total exactly 70p; overpayment earns 0.25 and underpayment earns zero.
comparisons.reason: Small-object handling and tray placement are generic shared primitives, but this tests arithmetic selection, not impact fracture and mandatory recovery of newly released tangs.

comparisons.objective: Position, unfold, level, and switch on a foldable desk lamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual manipulation of a free base and three passive hinges plus toggle actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Base inside its frame, shade at least 20 cm high and within 15 degrees of level, with lamp on.
comparisons.reason: This tests articulated-object configuration and final pose, with no fracture, impulse regulation, retained insert protection, or debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Insert a retaining fork laterally into a shaft groove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a loose fixture while aligning and feeding both fork tines through a narrow groove.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tines pass the shaft center; the record mentions measured partial lift credit but omits its numeric thresholds.
comparisons.reason: It shares precision alignment around a retained mechanical feature, but its outcome is insertion of a fastener, whereas the candidate removes sacrificial tangs through contact-driven fracture and recovers them.

comparisons.objective: Clip a wafer to an e-beam sample plate and load it face-down through a safely operated load lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select clips, center a wafer, repeatedly regrasp and turn a screwdriver, flip a coupled assembly, and operate a door lock.
comparisons.success_condition: Each screw turns 300–420 degrees, wafer remains intact and face-down, loading occurs on green, and the door is open under 120 seconds before being shut and locked.
comparisons.reason: Despite precise tool use and force-sensitive damage avoidance, it tests threaded fastening and load-lock sequencing rather than impact fracture and collection of released pieces.

comparisons.objective: Hand off and insert a cable-bound duplex fibre connector into a keyed adapter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Inter-arm transfer, cable-constrained retention, and coupled dual peg-in-hole insertion with submillimetre clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Connector is inserted, released, arms retreat, and the state remains stable for 20 seconds.
comparisons.reason: This is explicitly a connector insertion task and tests tight-fit mating; the candidate instead fractures and removes existing insert tangs and is not an insertion/release task.

comparisons.objective: Place an unscrewed reagent cap interior-up on a rest without contaminating protected surfaces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Delicate reorientation and release with continuous contact avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap rests interior-up without any contact to its interior or opening rim; forbidden contact is persistently latched.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is protected-surface handling and orientation, not forceful impact, sacrificial fracture, or free-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Pack a cold-chain shipper with a buffer separating medication from a refrigerant brick.
comparisons.physical_skill: Order-sensitive placement and flat stacking of three rigid components in a confined cavity.
comparisons.success_condition: Brick, buffer, and carton are flat in that order, under 4 degrees tilt, with zero brick-carton contact, arms withdrawn, and state held 3 seconds.
comparisons.reason: This tests safe packing order and contact separation; it lacks precision tooling, controlled fracture, retained-component protection under impact, and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Place three color-coded ECG lead clips at the correct manikin electrode locations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate deformable leads, reason about mirrored body locations, and place/release clips.
comparisons.success_condition: Each clip lies in its assigned cup, no clip is wrong, fixtures remain fixed, leads stay attached, and all clips rest released for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Cable handling and semantic placement are meaningfully different from mandrel alignment, hammer impact, notch fracture, and containment of four free tangs.

comparisons.objective: Mount a module on a DIN rail by hooking, pivoting, and snapping its spring latch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a rigid module to a rail, establish a hook pivot, then press a sprung latch past the lower lip.
comparisons.success_condition: Module is hooked, square within 3 degrees, closely seated at both lips, latch returned behind the rail, and still for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Both demand controlled contact near retained hardware, but DIN mounting tests snap-fit assembly and latching, not intentional fracture plus fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Insert a cable-bound USB-C plug into a handheld spot welder and set the assembled device down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual device stabilization and submillimetre connector alignment under cable stiffness.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug body is within 1.5 mm of the device face, within 0.5 mm of port center, under 8 degrees tilt, then both objects are released and arms return home.
comparisons.reason: It shares coaxial precision and bimanual stabilization but centrally tests tight connector insertion, not impact-force control, breakage at a notch, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Move four vials only while a permit lamp is green, renewing permission after lapses.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed pick-and-place coordinated with indicator monitoring and button actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: All vials reach the carrier, every lift begins under green, and each vial is set down within 3 seconds of a lapse.
comparisons.reason: The defining ability is compliance with a changing temporal permit, not mechanical impact, fracture, insert retention, or debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Extend an adjustable training handle and positively engage its detent pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Withdraw and hold a pin clear while changing length, then align and reengage the detent.
comparisons.success_condition: Handle reaches the selected extension and the pin positively engages; early pin return is rejected, but numeric pose and engagement thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: This tests coordinated pin withdrawal and re-latching in an adjustable mechanism, not sacrificial-feature fracture or recovery of released fragments. Missing numeric details do not make the objectives plausibly duplicative.

comparisons.objective: Latch a mechanical gas shutoff under a visible methane warning; candidate fractures four installed insert tangs and recovers them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Single control latching and hazard avoidance versus coaxial mandrel placement, bimanual hammer impact, and tiny-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Shutoff latched with no ignition versus four notch fractures, four contained tangs, retained undamaged inserts, released tools, and stable finish.
comparisons.reason: The tested outcomes and central mechanisms differ; neither controlled fracture nor fragment recovery is present.

comparisons.objective: Place a baby bottle upright in a warm-water bath while avoiding microwave use and submersion; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe object selection and upright placement versus stabilized coaxial tooling, regulated impact fracture, withdrawal, and fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Released bottle safely supported with microwave unused versus four physical fractures and recovered tangs without coil or shell damage.
comparisons.reason: Shared grasping and placement are generic; the record does not test impact, retained-insert protection, or fracture debris.

comparisons.objective: Join two loose-cord barrel connectors and lay the joined pair down; candidate breaks and removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual coaxial connector mating within stated pose tolerances versus mandrel stabilization during hammer impact and post-fracture recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug fully inserted, connectors released on bench, arms returned, and nothing lost versus four tang fractures and containment with inserts unchanged.
comparisons.reason: Both require fine coaxial alignment, but mating two parts tests insertion/seating, while the candidate tests contact-driven notch fracture and recovery of free fragments.

comparisons.objective: Select and seat a PH2 hex bit in a stabilized screwdriver; candidate fractures and recovers four HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed hex alignment and tight axial insertion versus coaxial mandrel placement followed by separately delivered impact and fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct bit seated to depth and orientation, tool stable, arms withdrawn versus four fractured tangs contained with no insert displacement or damage.
comparisons.reason: Fine alignment and stabilization overlap generically, but the defining tested ability—keyed seating—is materially different from controlled fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Pull open a spring-loaded flange gap, insert and center a blind plate, then let the joint grip it; candidate finishes threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained bimanual force against a spring while feeding a plate versus stabilizing a narrow mandrel during discrete hammer impacts and collecting fragments.
comparisons.success_condition: Plate centered and captured by the returned flange; numeric tolerances and explicit failure gates are absent from the record body. Candidate requires four valid fractures, containment, and no damage.
comparisons.reason: The record tests compliant gap holding and insertion, not impact fracture or recovery of separated material.

comparisons.objective: Lift two free plates and align their edges in the air with a positive seam; candidate removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Symmetric bimanual pose coordination of large free plates versus asymmetric tool stabilization, hammering, withdrawal, and millimetre fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified gap, level, yaw, tilt, and midpoint geometry versus four notch fractures, retained insert poses, and all fragments in a tray.
comparisons.reason: Both are bimanual, but the tested abilities and terminal physical states are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Remove a hot-pot lid by opening it away from the operator and set it down; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Direction-sensitive lid tipping and carrying versus coaxial small-tool control, regulated impact, and tiny-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Far side opens first, lid clears and is placed on the counter; candidate requires four contact-loaded fractures with no damage or escaped tang.
comparisons.reason: The record tests safe removal trajectory, not fracture mechanics or retained-component protection.

comparisons.objective: Cook and serve two patties using two spatulas while tracking sear times and contamination rules; candidate removes four tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual scooping, stopping, flipping, timing, and serving versus mandrel alignment, hammer impulse regulation, and fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Both sides cooked 20–40 seconds and served without contamination, burns, drops, or forbidden contact versus four fractures and complete containment without damage.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful overlap beyond generic two-tool manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Identify and place the water beaker on a hotplate while keeping acetone away; candidate finishes inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hazard-aware object selection and upright transport versus precision impact tooling and loose-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Water upright and released on the hotplate, acetone outside a 7.5 cm exclusion zone, no tipping or loss versus four safe fractures and contained tangs.
comparisons.reason: The central ability is semantic hazard selection and transport, not mechanical fracture.

comparisons.objective: Meter a hydraulic valve to lower a fragile cabinet gently onto rails; candidate breaks insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous valve modulation and load-speed control versus discrete hammer impulse control while maintaining mandrel coaxiality.
comparisons.success_condition: Cabinet transfers to stable rail support with acceptable landing speed and no glass contact; exact failure thresholds beyond the reported landing are absent. Candidate requires four fractures, containment, and no insert or shell damage.

comparisons.reason: Tests stateful search and sliding-lid manipulation, not coaxial tool placement, hammer impact, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Extract a robot-assembly spacer using a pusher.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a pusher with an assembly component and apply controlled force to drive the spacer out.
comparisons.success_condition: Spacer extraction must satisfy detailed contact checks; the body gives no numeric extraction or damage thresholds.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest tool-assisted neighbor, but its central outcome is pushing an intact spacer out. The candidate instead fractures four sacrificial tangs at notches, retains every coil, and collects every fragment.

comparisons.objective: Remove and store two transport keys before unloading a captive carrier.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual restraint removal, storage, and prerequisite-sensitive carrier handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Both keys are stored before carrier movement; premature movement and unsupported recovery poses fail.
comparisons.reason: Tests ordered restraint removal and unloading, without impact fracture, hammer–mandrel coordination, or loose-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Release a loaded spring platform while supporting and safely unloading it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual restraint removal, support, and regulation of stored spring energy.
comparisons.success_condition: The platform must be supported during release and unloaded without sudden upward motion; numeric limits are not stated in the record.
comparisons.reason: Tests controlled stored-energy release, whereas the candidate deliberately delivers impact energy to fracture notched tangs while preserving surrounding inserts.

comparisons.objective: Extend a training handle to its second hole and re-engage its detent.
comparisons.physical_skill: Retract a locking pin, translate the handle, align a hole, and relatch.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct locking sequence and re-engagement before release; no numeric tolerances are supplied.
comparisons.reason: Tests pin sequencing and detent engagement, not impact-driven fracture or recovery of detached pieces.

comparisons.objective: Raise and align a pump baseplate using two wedges without excessive tilt.
comparisons.physical_skill: Matched bimanual wedge driving and load/tilt control.
comparisons.success_condition: Raise 15 mm onto both flat seats while never exceeding 2 degrees of tilt.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual force regulation, but this task tests synchronized continuous wedge motion under load, not mandrel stabilization, hammer impact, fracture, and fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Load, center, and focus a microscope slide without contacting the objective.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual holder operation, slide insertion, knob-driven XY centering, and fine focus adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Specimen within 1.5 mm of the axis and slide at the specified focus spacing, never within 0.5 mm of the objective.
comparisons.reason: Tests multi-stage precision positioning and collision avoidance, with no fracture, percussion tool use, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Sort fruit by whether its kind appears on a training-set reference mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual/semantic classification and pick-and-place sorting.
comparisons.success_condition: Known kinds go in the bowl and novel kinds on the plate; detailed placement thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests category comparison and sorting rather than mechanical tool use or contact-driven fracture.

comparisons.objective: Map a two-wire harness with flying probes and record the electrical verdict.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual probe alignment, spring-tip compression, measurement sequencing, and interpretation.
comparisons.success_condition: Four valid two-probe acquisitions lead to the correct PASS, CROSSED, or OPEN tag; disconnected probes cannot establish an open wire.
comparisons.reason: Shares small-target bimanual alignment, but tests electrical probing and interpretation rather than impact, destructive notch separation, and fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Singulate four parcels onto a sorter lane with prescribed gaps and orientations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Carton pick-and-place, cross-arm staging, orientation, and spatial arrangement.
comparisons.success_condition: All parcels lie flat and single-file, long axes along the lane, with at least 10 cm clear gaps and no stacking or side-by-side placement.
comparisons.reason: Tests arrangement and handoff of large packages, not precision impact tooling or recovery of millimetre-scale debris.

comparisons.objective: Separate nested rigid trays and park both upright in designated bays.
comparisons.physical_skill: Forceful denesting followed by controlled placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Stable separation earns partial credit; correct bay placement held for two seconds earns full credit.
comparisons.reason: Tests overcoming nesting friction and placing intact trays, with no deliberate fracture, retained insert tolerance, or fragment accounting.

comparisons.objective: Move a long board through a narrow doorway between partitioned workspaces.
comparisons.physical_skill: End-first pivoting, bimanual handoff, regrasping, and final orientation.
comparisons.success_condition: The complete board ends flat on the target mat and parallel to the partition.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained-object transfer and handoff geometry rather than impact-force regulation and small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Place only dog-safe snacks in a bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safety knowledge plus object classification and pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Safe foods are placed in the dog's bowl while toxic foods are excluded; numeric placement details are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests semantic safety classification, not mechanical finishing of threaded inserts.

comparisons.objective: Slide a strong magnet off a steel plate without allowing it to snap back.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual plate stabilization, tangential force control, and separation against attraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Magnet is released on the table at least 5 cm from the plate without snapping back.
comparisons.reason: Both demand lateral-force control and fixture stabilization, but the outcome is nondestructive magnetic separation, not axial impact fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Insert black and red multimeter leads into the correct voltage-measurement jacks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Color-based selection and close-clearance coaxial plug insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Black lead in COM and red lead in V/ohm, with the 10 A jack unused.
comparisons.reason: Shares precise coaxial alignment, but tests insertion and correct jack selection; it has no striking, fracture, retained-component protection, or debris collection.

comparisons.objective: Remove unloaded line eyes from a pin rail while leaving load-bearing lines attached.
comparisons.physical_skill: Identify line tension, lift eyes from pins, and sort released lines into crates.
comparisons.success_condition: Free lines go into crates and taut load-bearing lines remain; no numeric thresholds or fuller rubric are provided.
comparisons.reason: Despite the title's word 'strike,' the described action is lifting line eyes from pins. It tests load-state discrimination and removal, not hammer striking or material fracture.

comparisons.objective: Secure a bird cage before opening a nearby cat cage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hazard inference, key locking, and sliding-door operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Bird cage must be shut and locked before the cat door is opened; the record provides no numeric rubric or stability details.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety-aware action ordering and lock/door manipulation, wholly different from insert finishing and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Combine two vending spirals into one wide selection and load it from the front pitch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spiral reconfiguration and product loading.
comparisons.success_condition: The record supplies no detailed scoring rubric, tolerances, or failure conditions beyond the stated configuration and loading outcome.
comparisons.reason: Available evidence still establishes a different central ability—reconfiguring and loading vending spirals—with no impact fracture or debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Replace a missing drain-pipe section and close both joints with correctly sized slip couplings.
comparisons.physical_skill: Size discrimination, sequencing, coaxial insertion, bimanual staging, and coupling translation.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct section and couplings form both joints, parts remain on the bench, and the released final assembly stays still for one second.
comparisons.reason: Shares coaxial alignment and sequencing, but tests assembly of intact pipe joints rather than percussion fracture and exhaustive recovery of detached tangs.

comparisons.objective: Place a fresh pad over a soaked-through dressing and hold it in place.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pad placement and sustained holding over an existing dressing.
comparisons.success_condition: The record does not state placement tolerances, hold duration, damage rules, or a detailed scoring rubric.
comparisons.reason: The stated objective is additive dressing placement and holding, clearly different from tool-mediated metal fracture and fragment containment despite sparse rubric evidence.

comparisons.objective: Load and center a wafer on a spin-coater chuck using tweezers and an aligner while controlling the lid.

comparisons.success_condition: Wafer centered within 0.5 mm on the 24 mm chuck, lid closed, with no gripper or fingertip contact on the wafer top.
comparisons.reason: Shares demanding bimanual tool alignment and careful withdrawal, but tests contamination-safe placement of an intact wafer, not controlled impact fracture and collection of four released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Place vineyard row anchors at prescribed positions.
comparisons.physical_skill: Outdoor anchor placement and row alignment, not recessed mandrel alignment, impact fracture, or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Anchors aligned and offset by post height; no insert-retention, notch-fracture, or tang-containment test.
comparisons.reason: Tests large-scale placement rather than finishing threaded inserts. The record supplies no specs or detailed damage thresholds, but its stated objective and outcome are clearly different.

comparisons.objective: Rotate a Geneva drive through two indexes and demonstrate dwell.
comparisons.physical_skill: Contact-driven rotary indexing and release, not bimanual hammering of a stabilized precision mandrel.
comparisons.success_condition: Two advances with stationary dwell before both hands release; no fracture, retained coil, or loose-fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Install the correct end and mid clamps at six solar-panel rail positions.

comparisons.success_condition: Correct clamp type seated level at each position; no hammer strike, insert retention, or containment requirement.

comparisons.objective: Open a magnetic 3D-printer door while stabilizing the light printer.

comparisons.success_condition: Door stays fully open, printer remains still, and print/head are untouched.

comparisons.objective: Straighten a training doll’s sprung legs and close a footboard to measure length.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained limb restraint plus board closure, not tool-on-tool impact or brittle notch separation.
comparisons.success_condition: Legs held flat, footboard left at the reading, then released; no fragment containment or retained fastener test.

comparisons.objective: Spot a bench-press lifter, intervening only when the sixth repetition stalls.

comparisons.objective: Route conduit between electrical boxes only through permitted horizontal/vertical wall zones.

comparisons.objective: Secure glass plates into a gel-casting cassette and insert it into a spring-loaded stand.

comparisons.success_condition: Aligned plates secured, cassette seated, lever released, grippers withdrawn, and assembly stable.

comparisons.objective: Plot a boat’s dead-reckoning position on a nautical chart.

comparisons.success_condition: Marker released flat and still within 0.2 nautical miles for full credit.
comparisons.reason: The objective, mechanism, and tested ability are unrelated to insert finishing. No specs are supplied, but the numeric marker rubric is detailed enough to establish distinction.

comparisons.objective: Pick a clear training lock using coordinated tension and pin setting.

comparisons.objective: Mix polymer stock while sprinkling powder into a stirred vortex without fish-eyes.

comparisons.objective: Play the capturing Go stone, then remove only the captured white group into Black’s lid.

comparisons.objective: Choose, mount, and lock a zoom lens nose-down, then leave it at 50 mm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual bayonet mounting and friction-aware ring adjustment, not hammer impact or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct lens locked from below, zoom remains at 50 mm after release.
comparisons.reason: This tests insertion/rotation and passive setting retention; the candidate tests controlled sacrificial fracture and containment. No spec versions or numeric mount/zoom tolerances are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Lift and pour simulated molten metal with a two-handle shank into the dry mould.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load carrying and controlled tipping, not coaxial mandrel alignment and striking.
comparisons.success_condition: Contents enter the dry mould; avoid the wet mould, direct crucible contact, and unsafe handling.
comparisons.reason: Rigid beads and two-arm coordination are generic similarities only; the central pour/hazard choice differs from fastener finishing. No specs or quantitative spill/completion thresholds are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Open a latched egg carton and transfer six eggs safely into a basket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Brace-and-open manipulation followed by repeated fragile-object extraction and transport, not impact-controlled fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: All six eggs reach the basket; an egg falling more than 3 cm is broken and invalid.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual stabilization and repeated small-part recovery, but eggs are pre-existing cargo rather than fragments created by a calibrated strike. No spec versions or final stability thresholds are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Operate a straw dispenser and place one straw standing in each of five glasses.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring-return handle while extracting and slant-inserting straws, not hammering or fracture control.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one suitably deep, slanted straw remains in each upright glass.
comparisons.reason: Repeated bimanual tool access and insertion are generic overlaps; there is no notch fracture, insert preservation, or fragment containment. No specs or numeric glass-knock thresholds are supplied beyond stated dimensions.

comparisons.objective: Transfer support of a gravity-loaded cover and close it at controlled speed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous support handoff and velocity regulation, not tool alignment, impulsive loading, or debris pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Cover closes under controlled observable speed after safe support transfer.
comparisons.reason: Both penalize damaging force, but controlled hinge closure is a meaningfully different tested ability. No spec versions or actual closing-speed threshold are provided.

comparisons.objective: Stabilize a shaft fixture and slide a retaining fork into its groove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual fixture holding and precise fork insertion; no hammer impact, manufactured-notch fracture, withdrawal from a coil, or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Both fork tines pass the shaft centre, fork settles in the groove, and both grippers release.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest fixture-and-fastener manipulation record, but it adds a retaining part rather than breaking and recovering sacrificial tangs while preserving inserts. No specs or numeric seating/damage tolerances are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Hold open a spring-shut breaker cover and reset only the tripped breaker.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained cover restraint plus selective switch actuation, not impact tooling.
comparisons.success_condition: Tripped breaker left ON, other breakers unchanged, cover managed safely.
comparisons.reason: The shared two-arm hold-and-actuate pattern is generic; switch-state correction differs from fracture and fragment containment. No specs or numeric state/force thresholds are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Run a press safely using both hand controls, then remove the finished part.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained simultaneous button holding and post-cycle retrieval, not precision tool striking.
comparisons.success_condition: Both buttons held throughout die closure, hands remain outside the die, then part moves to the tray.
comparisons.reason: This tests procedural interlocking and timing rather than contact-driven component finishing. No specs or exact concurrency/timing thresholds are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Hot-swap a failing battery for a charged pack while maintaining station power and safe pack custody.
comparisons.physical_skill: Time-critical bimanual extraction/insertion and pack transport, not notch fracture or millimetre fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Bay empty for at most 4 seconds, charged pack installed, failed pack binned, and no pack mishandled.
comparisons.reason: Both protect equipment and coordinate two arms, but hot-swapping tests rapid exchange and custody rather than impact force control and debris recovery. No spec versions or insertion tolerances are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Quench two aluminium fittings before a deadline while keeping a steel fitting out of water.
comparisons.physical_skill: Parallel two-arm sorting and transport under time pressure, not coaxial striking or fracture control.
comparisons.success_condition: Both aluminium fittings submerged by 6 seconds and remain there; steel reaches the rack and no hot part touches the bench.
comparisons.reason: The task tests classification and concurrent transport, with no sacrificial fracture or retained fastener. No specs or detailed placement/damage tolerances are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Hang an electric-fence wire in three insulator slots without conductive contact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long flexible-object routing and support, unlike rigid mandrel alignment, hammering, and tiny-fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Wire occupies all slots, stays at least 1 cm from posts, handle hangs free, and robot releases it.
comparisons.reason: Its central ability is deformable routing and clearance maintenance, not insert finishing. No spec versions or additional sag/contact rubric details are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Move three hazards away from a toddler and deliver the sippy cup toward them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Object classification, repeated bimanual handovers, and orientation-preserving transport, not impact fracture.
comparisons.success_condition: Hazards end beyond the 550 mm divider, cup within 150 mm, knife flat, and other vessels upright.
comparisons.reason: Although both require repeated handling without loss or spill, the tested ability is semantic sorting and handover across reach zones. No specs or numeric upright/stability thresholds are supplied.

comparisons.objective: Park four carts while preserving corridor clearance and exclusion zones.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual cart transport and inter-arm handover; no tool impact, fracture, or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: All carts occupy valid bays, at least 140 mm remains clear, and door zones and handover pad are empty.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained spatial rearrangement and handover, not coaxial mandrel placement, controlled tang fracture, and recovery of released metal fragments.

comparisons.objective: Discharge a capacitor before removing and boxing a power-supply board.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a two-pin electrical tool on two pads, then extract and transfer a board.
comparisons.success_condition: Maintain two-pad contact for two seconds before board removal; numeric extraction tolerances and damage rules are not given.
comparisons.reason: The defining ability is safety-ordered sustained electrical contact followed by board extraction, not impact fracture and containment of four fragments.

comparisons.objective: Place wet-chemical and CO2 extinguishers beside their corresponding hazards.
comparisons.physical_skill: Read type cards and carry two large objects to semantic destinations.
comparisons.success_condition: Each named extinguisher stands on the correct mark; placement tolerances and failure details are not supplied.
comparisons.reason: Tests semantic identification and gross placement rather than coaxial small-tool alignment, bimanual striking, or loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Insert a T-nut into an aluminium-profile slot, rotate it 90 degrees, and slide it to a mark.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part insertion, constrained in-slot rotation, and sliding under retaining lips.
comparisons.success_condition: T-nut is locked beneath the lips at the red mark and released; numeric pose and damage limits are absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve a small recessed metal feature, this tests captive insertion and quarter-turn locking, not notch fracture by a separately hammered mandrel or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Sort four M8 and four M4 bolts into separate organizer compartments.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated fingertip pinch pickup, size discrimination, and bin placement.
comparisons.success_condition: All M8 bolts are in the left compartment and all M4 bolts in the right; loss and containment thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Shared small-object recovery and deposit are generic primitives; sorting intact bolts does not test impact fracture, insert retention, or extraction of fragments from a shell.

comparisons.objective: Insert an oriented SD card into a reader until its latch clicks.
comparisons.physical_skill: One hand stabilizes the reader while the other aligns and pushes a thin keyed card into a slot.
comparisons.success_condition: Card enters label-up and contacts-first until latched; force, damage, and final-pose thresholds are not stated.
comparisons.reason: Shares bimanual stabilization and precision insertion, but its defining ability is keyed slot insertion and latching rather than controlled impact fracture and subsequent fragment search.

comparisons.objective: Close two overlapping enclosure doors in the physically required order, then secure the bolt.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reason about astragal interference, articulate two leaves, and translate a door bolt.
comparisons.success_condition: Both leaves close and the bolt is thrown; forcing the passive leaf against a closed astragal zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: Tests ordered articulation and latching imposed by door geometry, not axial tool alignment, hammer impulse control, fracture, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Select fine tweezers, peel a display film while stabilizing its carrier, dispose of the film, and return tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool selection, narrow-slot tab pinching, bimanual stabilization, and progressive peeling of an articulated film.
comparisons.success_condition: Film is peeled from 115 mm of adhesive and placed outside the carrier, carrier remains controlled, and tools return to holders; partial credit uses 5 mm increments.
comparisons.reason: Its central ability is continuous peel-force control on a strip; neither brittle notch fracture by impact nor recovery of multiple free metal tangs is tested.

comparisons.objective: Reset a peak-flow meter marker before presenting the meter for use.
comparisons.physical_skill: Push a sliding marker to zero and orient the meter mouthpiece-first on a tray.
comparisons.success_condition: Marker is reset and meter is handed over in the required orientation; numeric tolerances and damage conditions are missing.
comparisons.reason: Tests state reset and oriented handover, with no tool-mediated impact, retained insert, or released-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Close a radiator valve while counting turns, then reopen it by half that count.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated rotary manipulation with hidden-state counting and later proportional reversal.
comparisons.success_condition: Final opening equals half the measured starting opening; numeric angular tolerance and damage rules are not given.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is memory across multi-turn rotation, not bimanual impact control, fracture detection, or small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Cut foam along a printed curve by steering the workpiece around a fixed hot ribbon.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous path following with reversed motion and changing workpiece orientation.
comparisons.success_condition: Foam follows the printed cut curve; path tolerance, damage criteria, and release requirements are not stated.
comparisons.reason: Tests continuous workpiece steering through a fixed cutter, unlike discrete coaxial impacts that fracture tangs while preserving inserts.

comparisons.objective: Expose a buried pipe with a spade without contacting it.

comparisons.success_condition: At least 80 mm of pipe is bare for full credit; any spade contact within the defined check zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: Its defining ability is noncontact excavation around a protected object, not contact-loaded fracture and containment of deliberately released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Use a scraper to free a stuck print inside a printer and place it in a basket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reach a thin blade under a chamfer, apply levering force without removing the magnetic plate, then transfer the print.
comparisons.success_condition: Print is freed and basketed, plate remains in the printer, and scraper is left on the table; force and damage thresholds are absent.

comparisons.objective: Sort three waste items into two hinged bins and close both lids.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open articulated lids, classify and deposit items, then close lids, with two-arm coordination demonstrated.
comparisons.success_condition: All items enter their rule-specified bins below the rims and both lids close; any wrong-bin entry permanently zeros the episode.
comparisons.reason: Tests access sequencing, classification, and bulk containment, not precision tool impact or recovery of newly fractured millimetre-scale pieces.

comparisons.objective: Tip a loaded wheelchair to climb a kerb safely.

comparisons.success_condition: Chair and dummy reach the upper level; straight shoving, excessive forward pitch, lifting clear, or losing the dummy invalidates success.
comparisons.reason: Tests dynamic whole-object locomotion and stability, not small-scale coaxial tooling, brittle fracture, or fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Set tubular latches to their doors' backsets, fit them, and pass a spindle through.
comparisons.physical_skill: From the title, configure latch length, insert hardware, align passages, and insert a spindle.
comparisons.success_condition: Available evidence gives no body, specifications, numeric tolerances, damage rules, or detailed scoring beyond the title.
comparisons.reason: Even with sparse rubric evidence, the stated tested ability is adjustable latch fitting and through-alignment, meaningfully different from hammer-driven tang fracture and loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Cock a desoldering pump, position it on a marked solder joint, fire it, and return it to a holster.

comparisons.success_condition: Pump is cocked before one on-target shot and is finally released in its holster; off-target shots are wasted and require recocking.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest impact-like neighbor because it combines tool stabilization and a transient recoil event, but it tests spring-tool state sequencing and suction at one joint—not hammer impulse regulation, notch fracture, insert retention, or recovery of four released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Level a rack shelf by relocating the single pull pin installed in the wrong hole.
comparisons.physical_skill: From the title, diagnose height mismatch, extract a retaining pin, align holes, and reinsert it.
comparisons.success_condition: Available evidence lacks a body, specifications, numeric level tolerance, pin-engagement rule, and failure conditions.
comparisons.reason: The stated ability is diagnosis and relocation of a reusable retention pin; it does not test destructive notch fracture, hammering, or containment of generated fragments.

comparisons.objective: Weigh an infant manikin by setting a kilogram notch and sliding a gram weight until the beam pointer levels.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place or support a manikin and adjust coarse and fine mechanical balance weights using visual feedback.
comparisons.success_condition: Pointer must be level after weight adjustment; the record supplies no numeric tolerance, handling constraints, or damage rules.
comparisons.reason: Tests closed-loop balancing and measurement rather than precision impact, fracture, and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Place five polarized 5050 LEDs on circuit-board footprints with tweezers.

comparisons.objective: Remove weaker seedlings so one remains per 10 cm; candidate removes manufactured tangs from four installed inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective perception and delicate biological extraction versus recessed coaxial tool alignment, bimanual hammer impact, and metal-fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct spacing while retaining the stronger seedlings versus four verified fractures, every tang in a tray, and no coil or shell damage. The record supplies no numeric scoring or damage rubric beyond its objective.
comparisons.reason: Both remove unwanted material, but selective plant thinning does not test impact-mediated notch fracture or preservation of a threaded insert under lateral-load limits.

comparisons.objective: Support a bar while withdrawing its carriage, then lower it into a cradle; candidate breaks and collects insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous load support during support-surface removal and controlled lowering versus coaxial mandrel stabilization during discrete hammer impacts and fragment pickup.

comparisons.reason: Load transfer and support sequencing are meaningfully different from precision impact fracture and post-fracture debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Remove an internal obstruction, then re-thread and fully close a jar lid; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.

comparisons.reason: Although both protect threaded hardware from overload, jar obstruction diagnosis and screw closure do not test impact fracture at manufactured notches or loose-tang accounting.

comparisons.objective: Build a mirrored four-cube arrangement; candidate breaks and recovers four HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spatial reasoning, cube placement, stacking, and hand-to-hand transfer versus coaxial precision tooling, impact regulation, and millimetre-scale fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct mirrored base and top cube, with unmirrored copies rejected, versus four safe fractures and all released tangs deposited in a tray.
comparisons.reason: The task tests geometric transformation and assembly, not contact-loaded fracture or damage-sensitive insert finishing.

comparisons.objective: Use a spatula to pull a part from beneath a guard, place it in a tray, and return the tool; candidate fractures tangs and collects them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remote planar hooking or dragging through a low opening followed by ordinary pickup versus coaxial recessed mandrel alignment, bimanual hammering, careful withdrawal, and tiny-fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Part must first be tool-extracted, then tray-deposited, with spatula returned versus four notch fractures and four tangs contained while every insert remains fixed and undamaged.
comparisons.reason: Tool-mediated retrieval and tray placement are shared only generically; the candidate uniquely tests controlled impact fracture and protection of retained coils.

comparisons.objective: Orient a calibration board toward a camera and stand it in a holder; candidate finishes installed HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large rigid-board grasping, orientation, and holder insertion versus narrow-tool coaxial alignment, two-arm hammer use, and tiny-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Board stably seated facing the camera versus four tangs fractured and contained with no insert or shell damage. Exact holder tolerances are absent from the record.

comparisons.objective: Pack requested food while ignoring an unsafe printed instruction to include bleach; candidate performs mechanical insert finishing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic instruction filtering and safe object selection with routine packing versus precision mandrel alignment, hammer control, and fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Apple and yogurt packed without bleach versus four correctly fractured and recovered tangs with tools released and hardware intact. Detailed packing tolerances are absent.
comparisons.reason: The benchmark centers on prompt-injection resistance and hazardous-item exclusion, a different tested ability from contact-rich impact tooling.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a retained hook tool, extract a cartridge from a covered channel, tray it, and return the tool; candidate breaks tangs with a mandrel and recovers them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Shaft-head assembly, spring-release actuation, hooked pulling, and cartridge transport versus coaxial mandrel stabilization, controlled hammer impact, snag-free withdrawal, and search for tiny fragments.
comparisons.success_condition: Actual hooked travel, full cartridge tray placement, intact tool return, and released stability versus four notch fractures, four independently moving tangs contained, and no coil or shell damage.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest retrieval/tool-use neighbor, but its central ability is constructing and using a tensile hook extractor; it does not test impact fracture at a notch or preservation of a retained insert during hammering.

comparisons.objective: Turn a load off, reset its breaker, then restore the load safely; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Correct switch sequencing and state monitoring versus bimanual precision impact tooling and fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Load off before reset, then load on with normal motor operation versus four safe fractures and complete tang containment. Numeric actuator tolerances are not supplied.
comparisons.reason: Electrical safety sequencing tests neither the candidate's contact mechanics nor its small-part recovery outcome.

comparisons.objective: Place an overlength rod diagonally so it fits in a tray; candidate breaks and collects insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-object orientation and corner-to-corner placement versus recessed coaxial tool alignment, hammer impact, and tiny-fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Rod fits by diagonal placement versus four valid fractures and all tangs contained without hardware damage. The record has an empty body and no scoring thresholds or specs.
comparisons.reason: Despite sparse rubric evidence, the stated placement objective clearly tests a different spatial-packing ability from impact fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Remove only the top plate from a stack without disturbing lower plates; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-part singulation, controlled separation, and disturbance avoidance versus coaxial mandrel placement, bimanual hammering, and fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Top plate removed while lower plates remain undisturbed versus four tangs fractured and recovered with inserts and shell intact. The record has an empty body and no numeric disturbance rubric or specs.
comparisons.reason: Selective destacking is meaningfully different from notch fracture and loose-fragment containment, notwithstanding missing thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Order three similar cans by height on marked shelf locations; candidate finishes four HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual size comparison and upright pick-and-place versus small recessed alignment, impact-force regulation, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: All three cans upright on the correct marks in 6/9/12 cm order versus four safe tang fractures and complete containment.
comparisons.reason: Perceptual sorting and shelf placement do not test bimanual impact, fracture verification, or retained-coil protection.

comparisons.objective: Pack five lunch items with two perishables touching a flat ice pack; candidate breaks and retrieves HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object packing, orientation, and deliberate adjacency placement versus coaxial mandrel control, hammering, withdrawal, and millimetre-scale pickup.

comparisons.objective: Fit soft jaws to a vise before placing a finished part in it; candidate finishes installed HELICOIL inserts.

comparisons.objective: Turn look-alike medicine cartons to inspect hidden labels and dispense only the 10 mg pack; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Active visual inspection, reorientation, strength discrimination, and safe selection versus narrow-tool alignment, bimanual impact control, and fragment search.

comparisons.reason: Hidden-label inspection and medication selection test a different perceptual-safety ability from precision impact tooling.

comparisons.objective: Open a connector lever, insert stripped wire to the insulation boundary, and close the lever to clamp it; candidate breaks and retrieves HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part lever actuation, axial wire insertion-depth control, and latching versus coaxial mandrel insertion, bimanual hammer impact, tool withdrawal, and tiny-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Infer and hand-write the winning tic-tac-toe glyph, then hang and release the marker; candidate breaks and recovers HELICOIL tangs.

comparisons.objective: Open six binder rings, thread a divider onto all rings, release it, and close the rings; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.

comparisons.objective: Use two lines to keep a rising boat against a lock wall, then cleat both lines taut; candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dynamic bimanual tension regulation, deformable-line handling, and cleating versus rigid precision-tool alignment, impact control, and small-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Dispense exactly three drops, cork a test tube, then perform exactly four shakes from memory; candidate breaks and retrieves four HELICOIL tangs.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures four installed HELICOIL tangs and recovers the fragments; record fits and tightens a doll’s multi-route car-seat harness.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel stabilization, controlled hammer impacts, and tiny-fragment recovery; record requires webbing routing, buckling, untwisting, and tension adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks and collects HELICOIL tangs; record hoists a suspended bucket through a gin wheel and lands it on a scaffold deck.

comparisons.objective: Candidate mechanically removes four HELICOIL tangs; record performs iodine titration to a visually detected endpoint.

comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and recovered fragments without damage; record requires stopping at the first lasting blue-black endpoint without overdosing.
comparisons.reason: Closed-loop visual liquid dosing is unrelated to impact fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes installed thread inserts; record opens four ordered sliding puzzle panels and removes a block.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures insert tangs; record pushes a ball retainer to a stop and rolls a slide’s inner member between rollers until seated.

comparisons.reason: Rail-member seating through rollers is meaningfully different from notch fracture, despite both involving alignment.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes four HELICOIL tangs; record slides a service cover clear of hidden tabs and lifts it off.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual stabilized hammer impacts and tiny-part recovery; record requires discovering/maintaining the cover’s release direction, sliding disengagement, and lifting.

comparisons.reason: The available title establishes cover-tab disengagement as a different tested ability; missing numeric details do not create plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures and recovers HELICOIL tangs; record pulls an extinguisher retaining pin, reads its gauge, and files a matching tag.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures and recovers HELICOIL tangs; record pulls an extinguisher retaining pin, reads its gauge, and files a matching tag.

comparisons.reason: Pin withdrawal plus gauge-dependent reporting tests different mechanical and perceptual abilities.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes four inserts by tang removal; record tightens a child-seat anchor strap while pressing the seat into a cushion.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes HELICOIL tangs; record replaces a hooked wiper blade while supporting the sprung arm above glass.
