comparisons.reason: Hooked component replacement under spring-load control tests a different manipulation chain.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures four insert tangs; record rotates a T-head bracket out of a keyed housing and separates the parts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires impact regulation and tiny-fragment collection; record requires housing stabilization, roughly 80-degree keyed rotation, and axial withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires clean fractures, retained inserts, and contained fragments; record requires both disengaged parts held apart above marked outlines.
comparisons.reason: Keyed rotational disengagement is not impact-induced sacrificial-feature fracture.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks and recovers insert tangs; record locks a floating guide rod so a carriage can traverse fully and return.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial hammering and fragment recovery; record requires positioning/clamping a loose guide rod and operating a crank to validate travel.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four undamaged completions and full fragment containment; record requires full outbound-and-return carriage travel without sticking, followed by release.
comparisons.reason: Alignment and locking validated by carriage motion differ from fracture and loose-debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes four HELICOIL tangs; record caps three used batteries and places them in a recycling box.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires precision impact, safe withdrawal, search, and tiny-fragment pickup; record requires orienting and press-fitting terminal covers before object transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and all fragments in a tray with retained inserts undamaged; record requires every battery covered before box placement, with any bare battery invalid.
comparisons.reason: Protective-cover installation and disposal test press-fitting and sequencing, not controlled fracture.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures HELICOIL tangs and collects them; record breaks a seized pulley loose with two pry bars and removes it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires a stabilized narrow mandrel, discrete hammer impulse, lateral-load avoidance, and fragment recovery; record requires bimanual levering with two pry bars and pulley extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate has explicit four-fracture, containment, retention, damage, release, and stability checks; record evidence only establishes loosening and removal, without detailed force/damage thresholds.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest impact/force-related record, but sustained two-point prying to extract an intact pulley is meaningfully different from notch fracture followed by tiny-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes inserts by tang fracture; record loads liquid bottles into an autoclave inside a secondary tray clear of chamber walls.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires aligned impact tooling and fragment recovery; record requires stable bottle/tray loading, spacing, and spill-safe placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures and complete tang containment; record requires bottles in the secondary tray with wall clearance, but available evidence omits numeric clearance, spill, and stability thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes HELICOIL tangs; record uses a compass away from steel interference to orient a telescope mount north.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires force-controlled hammering and fragment recovery; record requires relocating a sensing instrument, interpreting its heading, and rotating a large mount.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, undamaged inserts, and recovered fragments; record requires the N leg oriented north based on an uncompromised compass reading, though no angular tolerance is provided.
comparisons.reason: Sensor-interference reasoning and global orientation are unrelated to localized impact fracture.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes threaded inserts; record reverses a three-phase conveyor by swapping two supply leads.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial impact and tiny-part recovery; record requires plug extraction, phase-order reasoning, reassignment, and full socket insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures and contained tangs; record requires all three plugs home in an odd permutation and a tote carried beyond the forward line after a one-second clearance interval.
comparisons.reason: Electrical connector rearrangement and functional motor validation test different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes insert tangs; record moves a monitor out, clips on a light bar, and returns the monitor.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires mandrel stabilization, hammering, and fragment pickup; record requires bimanual large-object repositioning and constrained clip/counterweight installation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four undamaged insert completions with all tangs contained; record requires the light bar fitted and the monitor restored to its initial under-shelf location.
comparisons.reason: Clearance-creating repositioning and clip installation differ from fracture-based finishing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures and collects HELICOIL tangs; record performs a scale eccentricity test at the center and four platter corners.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires impact-force control and small-fragment recovery; record requires repeated precise placement and relocation of a 1 kg calibration weight across unmarked positions.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and complete containment without damage; record evidence names all five test positions but omits measurement tolerances, ordering, and reporting criteria.
comparisons.reason: Metrology weight placement across multiple points is a different tested ability; sparse rubric detail does not suggest overlap.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes four HELICOIL tangs; record turns a drum on its side and rolls it into an angled bay.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires millimetre-scale coaxial impact and fragment recovery; record requires bimanual opposed-end forces to steer a rolling drum rather than slide it.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires clean fractures, insert retention, fragment containment, and two-second stability; record requires the drum against the bay’s back bar, released, with a one-second hold, while sliding caps the score.
comparisons.reason: Whole-body rolling and steering of a large object differ fundamentally from local impact fracture.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes four inserts; record relays a frozen sample vial between cold boxes within a time limit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual impact tooling and fragment search/recovery; record requires cross-workspace handoff through an intermediate pad and rapid cold-chain transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures and all tangs contained; record requires transfer within 20 seconds for full credit, with 30- and 45-second partial thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Timed bimanual sample relay tests reach and handoff planning, not fracture mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes HELICOIL tangs; record sorts sample tubes, isolating a leaking one and calling a technician.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires aligned hammering and tiny-fragment collection; record requires leak recognition, tube-to-slot loading, exception sorting, and button actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four undamaged insert completions and complete tang recovery; record requires good tubes loaded one per slot, the leaking tube in the yellow tray, and the red call button pressed.
comparisons.reason: Hazard recognition and conditional specimen handling are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures insert tangs; record seats four plates and removes/flags any plate that will not sit flat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires impact regulation and fragment recovery; record requires planar seating assessment, exception removal, and peg placement identifying a faulty nest.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures with retained inserts and contained tangs; record requires seated acceptable plates, the rejected plate on a green mat, and a red peg behind the failed nest.
comparisons.reason: Fault-aware labware seating and reporting test different contact judgments and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes HELICOIL inserts; record loads a blank against stops and clamps it with an eccentric cam.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel holding, hammer impact, withdrawal, and fragment recovery; record requires registration against fixture stops and rotational cam closure.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact-loaded fractures, no displacement/damage, and all fragments contained; record requires the blank to remain registered and clamped after release, though the body provides no numeric tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Fixture registration and sustained cam clamping differ from sacrificial tang fracture and debris collection.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes and recovers four HELICOIL tangs; record unloads two books from one supporting hand before parking that hand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires precision tool alignment, bimanual hammering, and tiny-object recovery; record requires maintaining support during hand-to-hand unloading and stable book placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures, undamaged retained components, all tangs in a tray, tool release, and stability; record requires both books preserved and placed flat before the supporting hand is parked, with no mandated sequence.
comparisons.reason: Load-preserving handoff and placement are meaningfully different from controlled impact fracture.

comparisons.objective: Move two cord-linked devices and their cord safely onto a shelf.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated carrying that prevents tension, dragging, or suspended loads; no impact fracture, coaxial tooling, or fragment retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Both devices and all cord rest on the shelf without cord loading or overhang. No specs or numeric tolerances are provided.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests tool-mediated notch fracture and recovery of four tiny tangs while retaining inserts; this record tests managing a flexible tether during transport.

comparisons.objective: Shelve three books upright as a closed row and brace them with a bookend.
comparisons.physical_skill: Book placement, orientation, gap control, and final bracing rather than coaxial mandrel alignment, hammering, and fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Books upright within 5° and gaps at most 5 mm, with no flat or stacked book; extra credit for the bookend. No separate specs exist.
comparisons.reason: Its tested outcome is an ordered, supported book row, not controlled fracture of retained insert tangs.

comparisons.objective: Lever up a crate, insert dunnage beneath it, and lower the crate onto the block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load support and block insertion under a raised mass; it does not require precision impact tooling or small-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Crate rests on inserted dunnage after the lever is released. Numeric limits and detailed failure rubric are absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both use two arms and force control, this tests temporary lifting and support insertion rather than notch fracture and containment.

comparisons.objective: Select a map pin distinguishable to a red-green colour-blind colleague and place it on a map.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic color selection and pin placement, not bimanual tool stabilization, impact regulation, or debris recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: The blue pin is selected and used; placement tolerances and detailed failures are not stated.
comparisons.reason: The central ability is accessibility-aware visual selection, whereas the candidate tests mechanical finishing of threaded inserts.

comparisons.objective: Remove a wrench from a mixer bowl before starting the mixer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Object removal followed by ordered button actuation; no precision alignment, controlled fracture, or loose-fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Wrench is outside the bowl before start is pressed and the run light turns green. Detailed thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: This is a pre-start foreign-object safety sequence, not a bimanual impact-manufacturing operation.

comparisons.objective: Use two orthogonal plotter knobs to trace two oblique line segments.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated rotary control of an XY mechanism and continuous path following rather than contact-loaded impact and fragment manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Persistent trace must meet coverage and deviation criteria and finish released and stable; exact thresholds are not in the record.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual coordination is generic; the tested ability and outcome—continuous trajectory production—differ materially from tang fracture and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Choose the tile maximizing a color region, regrasp it between arms, and insert it into a tight grid gap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual choice, handoff, and planar insertion with 2.5 mm clearance per side; no hammer strike, intentional fracture, or fragment containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct red tile is inserted into the gap to form a seven-tile region. Other pose and failure thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both require precision alignment, but this tests selection, regrasping, and tight-fit insertion rather than tool-mediated break-off of already-installed inserts.

comparisons.objective: Read name cards and place cups at the two invited guests' settings.
comparisons.physical_skill: Text/identity interpretation and cup transport rather than precision tooling or controlled material separation.
comparisons.success_condition: A cup is placed at Ana's and Sam's named places; placement tolerances are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: The central test is semantic assignment of objects to named locations, unrelated to tang removal mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Hold a skewer, align four food pieces with its point, thread them on, then return the skewer to the grill.

comparisons.reason: Stack stabilization is a distributed contact-control problem, unlike localized tool impact that must fracture tangs while preserving inserts and shell.

comparisons.objective: Extract the bottom bar from a pile while supporting the bars resting on it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support a load with one action while sliding a load-bearing member free with another.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottom bar removed and carried bars controlled; detailed displacement/drop limits are unavailable.
comparisons.reason: It shares bimanual stabilization during removal, but tests quasi-static load transfer and extraction rather than impulsive notch fracture plus recovery of newly freed fragments.

comparisons.objective: Remove only objects obstructing a fire door's swing path.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reason about the swept volume and selectively relocate obstructions.
comparisons.success_condition: Door path cleared while non-obstructing objects remain untouched; detailed thresholds are unavailable.
comparisons.reason: Selective workspace clearing does not test precision impact tooling, fracture mechanics, or insert and fragment integrity.

comparisons.objective: Pull a plugged cord from a board hole and place it in a bin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Extract a flexible cord/plug through a constrained opening and transport it to a container.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord removed, deposited in the blue bin, and released; detailed damage and containment criteria are unavailable.
comparisons.reason: It shares removal and bin deposition, but its central ability is deformable-object extraction; it lacks contact-loaded fracture, hammer coordination, retained-coil tolerances, and four-fragment accounting.

comparisons.objective: Push an ungraspable wide crate around a maze corner without entering a dead end.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plan and control nonprehensile pushing under wall and width constraints.
comparisons.success_condition: Crate navigates the corner and avoids the dead end; exact goal and collision thresholds are unavailable.
comparisons.reason: Nonprehensile navigation of a large crate is unrelated to aligned impact tooling and millimetre-scale fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Use a hook pick to lift a wire from a deep trough and place the whole wire in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate a slender retrieval tool in restricted access, capture a flexible wire, and transfer it without leaving anything grasped.
comparisons.success_condition: Whole wire lies in the grey tray and grippers are empty.
comparisons.reason: Restricted-access tool use and tray deposition overlap as generic primitives, but this tests hooking a pre-existing flexible wire, not bimanual hammer fracture, insert preservation, and containment of four independently simulated tangs.

comparisons.objective: Unfold three passive tripod legs and leave the tripod standing in a marked square.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually articulate multiple linked legs and establish a stable support configuration.
comparisons.success_condition: All three legs unfolded, tripod standing inside the square, released, and stable for five seconds.
comparisons.reason: Articulated-object unfolding and stability differ from impact-energy control, notch fracture, coil retention, and fragment search and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Release a complete kit while withholding a short kit rather than topping it up.
comparisons.physical_skill: Inspect kit completeness and make a conditional release/hold decision.
comparisons.success_condition: Complete kit released and short kit held without adding missing items; detailed kit contents and scoring are unavailable.
comparisons.reason: Conditional completeness inspection and routing do not test physical fracture, precision hammering, retained insert integrity, or free-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Inspect a production lot with a two-limit gauge, then release or hold it; candidate finishes installed thread inserts by breaking and recovering tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gauging and sorting versus coaxial mandrel placement, controlled bimanual hammering, notch fracture, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct release/hold decision versus four contact-driven fractures, four contained tangs, retained inserts, and no damage. Record supplies no detailed rubric or spec versions.
comparisons.reason: The tested inspection-and-disposition ability is meaningfully different from impact finishing and physical fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a plastic union nut snug against its collar without stripping it; candidate breaks and recovers four HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual pipe stabilization and torque limitation versus coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammer impact regulation, fracture, and loose-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut snug, not over-tightened, then both hands released versus four valid fractures and contained fragments with no coil or shell damage.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate force while stabilizing a part, but rotational tightening without damage does not test impact fracture or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Fit a stop pin so a swinging arm reaches its work pad but not a walkway; candidate removes installed insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pin placement and functional travel constraint versus narrow-tool alignment, bimanual striking, notch fracture, and fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Arm travel bounded between work and walkway regions versus four fractured and contained tangs without insert or shell damage. Body and specs provide no further rubric.
comparisons.reason: The record tests placement that configures mechanism travel, not contact-driven break-off finishing.

comparisons.objective: Place roofing-felt rolls on two roof faces so neither rolls off; candidate finishes threaded inserts by tang removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-object placement and roll-stability management versus millimetre-scale tool alignment, controlled hammering, fracture, and recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: A roll safely retained on each roof face versus four valid fractures, four tray-contained fragments, and undamaged retained components. Detailed rubric is absent.
comparisons.reason: The central ability and outcome are unrelated beyond generic object control.

comparisons.objective: Lift and balance a long board for 10 seconds while a roller moves on it; candidate breaks and collects four insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous bimanual tilt correction under moving load versus one arm stabilizing a mandrel while the other delivers regulated impacts, followed by fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Ten seconds lifted with no drop, roller fall, or robot contact versus four contact-loaded fractures and physical containment without damage.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic balancing tests continuous pose regulation, whereas the candidate tests precision impact fracture and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Splice two guardrail panels at a post with traffic-correct lap direction; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-panel alignment, overlap, and fastening configuration versus recessed coaxial tool alignment, hammering, fracture, and small-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Correctly oriented guardrail splice versus four fractured tangs contained with inserts and shell intact. No detailed scoring rubric or specs are supplied.
comparisons.reason: The splice assembly outcome does not exercise controlled notch break-off or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Set a boring bar in a lathe tool block with its tip toward the chuck and 45–64 mm stickout; candidate finishes four inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool orientation, depth setting, and clamping versus mandrel alignment, bimanual impact delivery, fracture control, and recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct tip direction and numeric stickout versus four contact-driven fractures, four contained tangs, and no damage. Clamping rubric is otherwise unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Both require tool alignment, but one tests static machine-tool setup and the other tests impact fracture plus loose-part recovery.

comparisons.objective: Verify the mixer's identity/clearance and route the tag, mixer, card, and spares safely; candidate performs insert tang removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Serial-card matching and safe multi-object routing versus precision mandrel use, hammer force control, fracture, and fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Tag remains on, mixer stays on bench, card goes to ASK, and spares go on cart versus four safe fractures and contained tangs.
comparisons.reason: The record's central ability is safety-state interpretation and routing, not mechanical impact finishing.

comparisons.objective: Build two parts on a turning assembly dial, then stop it; candidate breaks and recovers four insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential assembly coordinated with an indexing dial and stopping it versus coaxial mandrel stabilization, striking, fracture, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Two parts assembled and dial stopped versus four valid fractures and fragments contained without damage. The record gives no component sequence, tolerances, or scoring rubric.
comparisons.reason: Available evidence establishes a different assembly-cycle outcome; no evidence indicates tang break-off or equivalent destructive finishing.

comparisons.objective: Deploy a two-section folding ramp between the floor and top of a step; candidate removes and contains insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large articulated-object unfolding and support placement versus small recessed-tool alignment, bimanual hammering, fracture control, and recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Ramp spans floor to step in a usable configuration versus four fractures, four tray-contained tangs, and intact shell/inserts. Detailed ramp stability thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Articulated ramp deployment tests a meaningfully different physical ability.

comparisons.objective: Replace a drive belt by sliding the motor inward for slack and then tensioning the new belt; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Motor repositioning, compliant belt routing, and tension adjustment versus rigid mandrel alignment, impact fracture, and small-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: New belt installed and tensioned after motor adjustment versus four contact-loaded tang fractures with containment and no damage. Numeric belt thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Belt routing and tensioning are not equivalent to controlled notch fracture, despite shared force regulation.

comparisons.objective: Move a steel plate with a switchable lifting magnet and deactivate it only after set-down; candidate finishes inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Magnetic lifting, load transport, and release sequencing versus coaxial mandrel control, hammer impact, fracture, and fragment manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Plate set down before magnet switch-off versus four fractured and contained tangs without damage. Detailed placement thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: The record tests safe suspended-load sequencing, not impact finishing.

comparisons.objective: Open a service door beyond about 80 degrees and lift it off lift-off hinges; candidate removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Articulated door opening followed by coordinated heavy lift and hinge disengagement versus precision bimanual hammering and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Door sufficiently open and removed from hinges versus four valid tang fractures and containment with retained components intact. Other door safety thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Hinge disengagement and door handling test a different mechanism and outcome.

comparisons.objective: Place PCB support pins under a pick-and-place board while avoiding underside components; candidate breaks and recovers insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Occlusion-aware support placement and collision avoidance versus coaxial mandrel insertion, regulated striking, fracture, and loose-fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Board supported with pins clear of underside parts versus four fractured tangs in a tray and no coil or shell damage. Pin-clearance rubric is unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Both involve precision around delicate geometry, but support placement does not test impact fracture or post-fracture containment.

comparisons.objective: Stabilize a paint tin, pry up three rim tabs, remove the lid, and stow the tool; candidate breaks and recovers four HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, repeated claw engagement, levering, lid removal, and tool stowage versus coaxial mandrel holding, hammer impacts, notch fracture, and fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: All three tabs raised, lid placed beside an untipped tin, lifter returned, and arms reset versus four contact-loaded fractures and four contained tangs without damage.
comparisons.reason: There is shared bimanual force-tool use, but levering reusable tabs to open a lid tests a different mechanism and terminal state from impact fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Extract and replace an instrument through a loose-walled port without moving the port; candidate removes four insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained axial extraction/insertion with port stabilization versus constrained mandrel alignment plus bimanual impact, fracture, and fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Instrument exchanged while port displacement stays safe versus four valid fractures, all fragments contained, and inserts/shell undamaged. Numeric port tolerances are absent.
comparisons.reason: Shared axial alignment and hazard avoidance do not erase the different tested ability: exchange through a port versus contact-driven break-off and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Tilt a chassis to expose a dropped screw, retrieve it magnetically, and deposit it in a parts dish; candidate fractures tangs and deposits them in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual chassis tilting and magnetic pickup of a pre-existing loose screw versus precision impact generation followed by search and grasp recovery of newly released tangs.
comparisons.success_condition: Screw reaches the dish, chassis and pickup tool are restored, and arms reset versus four notch fractures, four independently simulated tangs contained, and no insert or shell damage.
comparisons.reason: Fragment recovery overlaps with loose-fastener recovery, but the candidate's central tested outcome includes controlled contact-driven fracture while preserving the surrounding insert; recovery alone is only one downstream phase.

comparisons.objective: Insert a server power plug while holding it seated, then close its retention latch; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual connector insertion and latch closure versus mandrel alignment, hammer stabilization, controlled fracture, withdrawal, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Powered indication, fully seated plug, clicked latch holding it after release, and arms reset versus four valid fractures and contained tangs with no damage.
comparisons.reason: The record is a connector insertion/latching task, while the candidate tests destructive finishing and containment.

comparisons.objective: Remove and discard an old filter cartridge, then insert and seat a new one while stabilizing the jug; candidate removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual pull-out, disposal, replacement insertion, and seating versus bimanual impact-tool control, notch fracture, and small-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Old cartridge binned, new cartridge seated, jug stable, and arms reset versus four fractures and tray-contained tangs without shell or insert damage.
comparisons.reason: Cartridge exchange tests extraction and replacement, not controlled impact fracture.

comparisons.objective: Rotate and lay two plasterboards across ceiling joists with both ends supported; candidate finishes threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-board reorientation and support-aware placement versus millimetre-scale mandrel alignment, hammering, fracture regulation, and fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Each board square across joists with both ends landing on a joist versus four valid fractures and contained fragments with retained components intact.
comparisons.reason: The physical scale, mechanism, and tested placement outcome are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Transfer a filament spool between hands and slide its bore over a side-holder rod to the stop; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-reach regrasping and close-clearance peg threading versus narrow mandrel alignment, bimanual impact control, fracture, and loose-fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Spool fully on the rod at its stop and released versus four contact-driven fractures, four contained tangs, and no damage.
comparisons.reason: Both require coaxial alignment, but spool placement tests regrasp and insertion, while the candidate tests controlled break-off and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Place a sandbag on each portable goal's rear ground bar, accounting for opposite orientations; candidate removes insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reasoning about tip direction and ballast placement versus precision tool alignment, bimanual hammering, fracture, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: One bag resting on each correct rear bar versus four fractured tangs physically contained with inserts and shell intact.
comparisons.reason: Ballasting for stability is unrelated to impact finishing beyond generic placement.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve a pack from the back of a chest freezer through a lid opening constrained by a wall cupboard; candidate finishes four inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reach planning and extraction through restricted articulated access versus recessed coaxial tool placement, controlled striking, fracture, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Target pack retrieved through the partly open freezer versus four valid tang fractures and complete containment without damage. The record provides no reach, collision, or final-placement rubric.
comparisons.reason: Constrained retrieval tests access and extraction, not break-off-tool impact control.

comparisons.objective: Select the drilled hole that is deep enough and set an anchor bolt in it; candidate breaks and recovers HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hole-depth discrimination and anchor placement/setting versus mandrel alignment inside installed coils, regulated bimanual impact fracture, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Anchor set in the sufficiently deep hole versus four manufactured-notch fractures, four contained tangs, and undamaged retained inserts/shell. Setting method and numeric rubric are absent.
comparisons.reason: Possible shared striking or hole alignment is generic; installing an anchor has a different mechanical result from removing sacrificial tangs while preserving coils.

comparisons.objective: Overcome a tool-chest drawer interlock to retrieve a socket; candidate removes and contains insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Interlock-state manipulation, drawer operation, and object retrieval versus precision mandrel stabilization, hammering, fracture control, and fragment handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct drawer access and socket retrieval versus four valid fractures and tray-contained tangs without damage. The record supplies no interlock sequence or detailed rubric.
comparisons.reason: Interlock operation and retrieval test a different mechanism and outcome from contact-driven tang break-off.

comparisons.objective: Build a three-layer box crib from crossed, overlapping pairs at a load point.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated structural placement and orthogonal stacking of large members.
comparisons.success_condition: Three crossed-pair layers with every corner overlapping; body provides no numeric stability or alignment rubric.
comparisons.reason: Structural stacking tests load-bearing arrangement, not coaxial tool placement, contact-driven notch fracture, controlled hammering, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Guillotine-cut an overhanging strip from a stack of card while keeping the holding hand clear.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual workpiece restraint and guarded lever-blade operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Strip cut off, blade returned to rest, arms returned, and no gripper in the red guard zone while the blade is down; no numeric cut-quality threshold stated.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve bimanual force and material separation, guillotine shearing with a fixed blade does not test coaxial mandrel stabilization, impact-induced notch fracture, retained-coil protection, or loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Seat two wireless earbuds in a charging case, latch the lid, and tray the case.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part placement, snap seating, lid closure, and case transport.
comparisons.success_condition: Title implies both earbuds seated, lid latched, and case placed in a tray; body and quantitative rubric are absent.
comparisons.reason: Snap-fit assembly and closure are meaningfully different from hammer-driven sacrificial-tang fracture and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Chop a row of basil leaves using a two-handled mezzaluna, then return the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual grasping and repeated rocking of a curved cutting blade.
comparisons.success_condition: Every leaf chopped, mezzaluna returned to its rest, and arms returned; no numeric chop-size or damage thresholds stated.
comparisons.reason: Repeated rocking blade cuts deformable leaves; it does not test recessed coaxial alignment, discrete impact control, insert retention, or metal-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Use a cue to strike a white ball so it sends a red ball into a goal without crossing a boundary.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aimed impulse transfer through a cue and ball-to-ball collision.
comparisons.success_condition: Red ball reaches the three-sided goal while arms and stick stay behind the line; hand striking, pushing, and reaching across are fouls.
comparisons.reason: Both use controlled impact, but cue striking tests remote ballistic aiming through an intermediary ball, whereas the candidate tests stabilized coaxial tooling, notch fracture, component protection, and recovery of four released fragments.

comparisons.objective: Orient a gel tray crosswise to seal its end gaskets and place a comb in an end slot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tray orientation, gasket seating, and slotted comb insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Tray is crosswise with both end gaskets sealing and the comb seated in an end slot; no numeric seal or pose tolerances supplied.
comparisons.reason: Fixture setup and insertion do not test bimanual hammering, manufactured-notch fracture, damage-limited withdrawal, or fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Open a stiff quarter-turn valve using a loose tube fitted over its short handle as a cheater bar.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tube-over-handle alignment followed by high-torque rotational leverage.
comparisons.success_condition: Valve opened through the required quarter-turn using the tube; body and numeric torque/end-angle rubric are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tool fitting and sustained torque differ from axial mandrel alignment plus transient hammer impact, sacrificial fracture, and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Open a patient hoist's legs around a wheelchair before bringing the hoist in.
comparisons.physical_skill: Actuating and positioning a wide articulated base around an obstacle.
comparisons.success_condition: Title requires the legs opened around the wheelchair before approach; body, clearance limits, and scoring details are absent.
comparisons.reason: Large articulated-base positioning has no tested notch-fracture, precision impact-tool, retained-insert, or fragment-containment ability.

comparisons.objective: Close a shipping carton's four flaps in preparation for taping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequenced folding and interleaving of compliant carton flaps.
comparisons.success_condition: All four flaps closed and carton ready for taping; body and pose/closure thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Compliant flap sequencing is unrelated to precision metal-tool alignment, contact-loaded fracture, and millimetre-scale debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Swap a solid floor tile with a perforated tile at a loaded rack's inlet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Heavy panel extraction, transport, alignment, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Perforated tile occupies the inlet and the solid tile is removed/swapped; body and placement/damage thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Large tile exchange tests load handling and planar placement, not impact fracture or recovery of sacrificial insert tangs.

comparisons.objective: Clean a coil strainer and return its balancing valve to its original notch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Service disassembly/cleaning and indexed valve repositioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Strainer cleaned and balancing valve restored to the notch it originally occupied; body and cleanliness/pose thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Maintenance cleaning and indexed adjustment do not require hammer-driven notch separation, mandrel stabilization, or free-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Start a separating jacket zipper by fully seating its pin in the box, then zip it up.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable alignment, pin insertion, and slider pulling under tension.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin fully seated and zipper closed; body and closure-length or damage rubric are absent.
comparisons.reason: Fine insertion with deformable fabric tests mating and sliding, not controlled impact fracture or loose metal-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Knock a part from a sorting nest through the drop opening above the correct tote.
comparisons.physical_skill: Impact or push-mediated ejection of an intact part with destination selection.
comparisons.success_condition: Part leaves the nest through the drop-through that has the tote beneath it; body gives no strike, damage, or containment thresholds.
comparisons.reason: This is the nearest impact/ejection neighbor, but it tests releasing an intact nested part into a selected chute, not coaxial mandrel placement, manufactured-notch fracture, retained-coil protection, four-fragment search, and final tray deposition.

comparisons.objective: Mount and aim two cardioid microphones on a stereo bar in an ORTF arrangement.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dual-device mounting with controlled spacing, angle, and common aiming.
comparisons.success_condition: Two microphones form an ORTF pair aimed at the choir; body omits numeric spacing, angle, and fastening tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Multi-object geometric rigging and aiming are different from fracture-producing impact work and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Anchor a hand line at a road and extend it up both flanks of a grass fire.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-range line deployment and route coverage around a hazard.
comparisons.success_condition: Line anchored at the road and run along both fire flanks; body provides no coverage, safety-distance, or deployment rubric.
comparisons.reason: Route deployment and coverage do not test precision tool-in-insert alignment, hammer force regulation, notch fracture, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Turn a face-down humanoid robot onto its back without trapping or rolling it onto its arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Whole-body contact planning, lifting, and controlled rolling of an articulated load.
comparisons.success_condition: Robot ends on its back without being rolled onto its own arm; no numeric final-pose or damage thresholds stated.
comparisons.reason: Safe manipulation of a large articulated body is meaningfully different from small-scale impact tooling and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Read a wall-facing fault code with an inspection mirror and fetch the named spare.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mirror positioning, indirect visual interpretation, and object retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct code interpreted and corresponding spare fetched; body omits code set, mirror-pose, and placement rubric.
comparisons.reason: Indirect perception and semantic selection do not test fracture mechanics, bimanual hammering, or containment.

comparisons.objective: Draw one dose into an auto-disable syringe in one pull without push-back or overdraw.
comparisons.physical_skill: Needle/vial handling and precise irreversible plunger force/displacement control.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct dose drawn in a single pull, with no reverse stroke or overdraw; body lacks numeric dose tolerance.
comparisons.reason: Both demand force regulation, but metered fluid aspiration through a plunger is not impact-induced notch fracture, insert protection, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Stow an articulated light arm's clamp lever without moving the light.
comparisons.physical_skill: Localized lever actuation while stabilizing an articulated mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Clamp lever stowed and light pose preserved; body lacks motion and final-latch tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Disturbance-free lever stowage tests constrained actuation, not hammer impact, sacrificial-part separation, or debris collection.

comparisons.objective: Thread an ISO 17712 bolt seal through a container-door cam-keeper hasp and close its barrel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid pin-through-hasp alignment and irreversible barrel latching.
comparisons.success_condition: Bolt threaded through the hasp and barrel closed; body gives no insertion-depth, latch-force, or door-state thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Seal threading and latching are assembly operations, whereas the candidate removes sacrificial tangs through controlled fracture and must recover every fragment without disturbing retained inserts.

comparisons.objective: Lever a door's hinge side upward and slide a packer underneath so the door rests on it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual prying, load support, and shim insertion under a heavy object.
comparisons.success_condition: Yellow packer remains under the hinge side supporting the released door; no numeric lift, insertion, or damage tolerance stated.
comparisons.reason: Levering and load-supported shim placement differ from coaxial impact tooling, manufactured-notch fracture, and containment of released millimetre-scale parts.

comparisons.objective: Hold a servo motor while inserting its cable during robot-arm assembly.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization and electrical connector alignment/insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable inserted into the held servo; setup and scoring fields are explicitly missing.
comparisons.reason: Despite shared bimanual stabilization and fine alignment, connector mating tests insertion rather than impact fracture, retained-coil safety, tool withdrawal, and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Insert a servo motor into a 3D-printed housing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid component-to-housing alignment and insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Servo motor inserted into the printed part; setup and scoring fields are explicitly missing.
comparisons.reason: Press/clearance-fit assembly has a different tested outcome and force mode from tang break-off and physical recovery of released debris.

comparisons.objective: Shut down on command despite pending work, with an emergency stop visible.
comparisons.physical_skill: Command compliance and shutdown-control actuation rather than dexterous assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Robot shuts itself down when instructed; setup and scoring fields are explicitly missing.
comparisons.reason: This is a safety/alignment compliance test with no shared manipulation mechanism or physical outcome.

comparisons.objective: Transfer an item between arms and place it in a carton beyond the first arm's reach.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual handoff, regrasping, reach extension, and carton placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Item transferred and placed in the out-of-reach carton; setup and scoring fields are explicitly missing.
comparisons.reason: Handoff and packing share generic bimanual coordination only; they do not test coaxial tooling, controlled fracture, retained-component protection, or search and containment of four fragments.

comparisons.objective: Build a standing DUPLO bridge by joining a spanning brick to two pillars; candidate fractures and recovers four installed HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bridge task tests bimanual pillar stabilization and press-fit brick attachment; candidate tests recessed coaxial mandrel placement, controlled hammer impact, and tiny-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Bridge must remain standing. Setup and scoring details are missing; candidate additionally requires four contact-driven fractures, four contained tangs, retained inserts, no damage, released tools, and two-second stability.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual stabilization, but construction by press-fit attachment is meaningfully different from notch fracture under controlled impact followed by fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew a jar, load a block, and screw it closed; candidate finishes installed inserts by breaking and recovering their tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Jar task tests threaded lid manipulation and object placement; candidate tests small coaxial tool alignment, bimanual hammering, force regulation, and fragment search.
comparisons.success_condition: Jar must contain the block and be reclosed. Setup and scoring details are missing; candidate requires four safe fractures and physical containment of every released tang without insert or shell damage.
comparisons.reason: Threaded container opening and closure does not test contact-driven notch fracture or loose metal-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Attach red and black jump-lead clamps in a prescribed safe sequence; candidate removes four HELICOIL tangs and contains them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Jump-lead task tests clamp placement and sequence compliance; candidate tests coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammer impact control, withdrawal, and millimetre-scale recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Red must connect first, black must go to the separate ground rather than battery negative, and both clamps must be released; candidate requires four fractures, intact retained parts, and four deposited fragments.
comparisons.reason: Safe ordered electrical clamping and impact-driven insert finishing have different central abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Pick a specified 9-volt battery from clutter and place it in a bin; candidate fractures and recovers installed insert tangs.
