comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable routing, bend control, and connector seating versus rigid precision tooling, bimanual impact control, and fragment search and retrieval.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord follows the guide, never bends below 25 mm radius, connector is seated, and hands release; candidate requires four safe fractures and all tangs deposited.
comparisons.reason: The principal tested physics—continuous flexible-object curvature versus contact-driven rigid fracture—are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Clip three carabiners into a closed-gate chain hanging from a stand; candidate finishes four threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gate actuation, link insertion, sequential chain assembly, and hanging-load handling versus coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammering, and metal-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Each linked carabiner has a closed gate and forms the released hanging chain; candidate requires four fractures, four contained fragments, and no retained-part damage.
comparisons.reason: Sequential latching assembly differs from controlled notch fracture and post-fracture containment. The record lacks numeric gate/chain tolerances.

comparisons.objective: Verify a GFCI by pressing TEST and then RESET in the required order; candidate breaks and collects HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered button actuation and state verification versus precision bimanual tool alignment, impulse delivery, force regulation, and debris recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: TEST trips the outlet before RESET restores it; reverse order cannot score. Candidate requires four physical fractures and an intact, fragment-free shell.
comparisons.reason: Sequence-sensitive switch operation does not test fracture mechanics, tool stabilization, or fragment containment. Button travel thresholds are not provided.

comparisons.objective: Put a dirty mug in the dish sink rather than the handwashing sink; candidate performs insert tang removal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mug grasp and destination selection versus coaxial mandrel use, controlled hammering, safe withdrawal, and tiny-fragment collection.
comparisons.success_condition: Available evidence identifies correct-sink placement; candidate requires four fractures, four recovered tangs, no damage, and stable tool release.
comparisons.reason: The body supplies little scoring detail, but the stated mug-sorting objective is clearly unrelated to the candidate's tested physical ability.

comparisons.objective: Compress an overfull case lid and pull its zipper from front to back; candidate breaks and retrieves installed-insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sustained compression plus guided zipper pulling versus one-arm mandrel stabilization, other-arm impact delivery, lateral-force control, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid remains shut and zipper reaches the back after coordinated manipulation; candidate requires four notch fractures and complete safe containment.
comparisons.reason: Both are bimanual, but their central coordination and outcomes—continuous closure under compression versus precision impact fracture—are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Rotate one gear to align teeth, hold it, and push its partner down a shaft into mesh; candidate removes HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual phase alignment, rotational adjustment, and axial gear insertion versus coaxial mandrel placement, controlled hammer impact, withdrawal, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Gears are physically meshed after release; candidate requires four tangs fractured and deposited while coils and shell remain within retention limits.
comparisons.reason: This is a close comparison for bimanual alignment, but it tests rotational tooth phasing and assembly, not impulse-controlled sacrificial fracture and debris containment.

comparisons.objective: Secure a 2 kg monitor, release its stand latch, and place it upright on a foam mat while still held; candidate finishes threaded inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load support coordinated with latch release and bulky-object transfer versus narrow mandrel alignment, bimanual hammering, safe withdrawal, and millimetre-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Monitor is secured before release, detached, upright on the mat, and still supported; candidate requires four fractures, zero fragment loss, and no component damage.
comparisons.reason: Safe load-before-release sequencing is different from contact-loaded notch fracture. Both involve preventing loss, but the tested abilities are not interchangeable.

comparisons.objective: Insert a flex cable into a ZIF connector while holding it and close the latch; candidate breaks and recovers HELICOIL tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual thin-cable alignment, insertion, stabilization, and latch closure versus coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammer impact, lateral-load control, and fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable fully inserted, latch shut, and both hands released; candidate requires four fractures and all fragments contained without moving or damaging inserts.
comparisons.reason: This is dexterously similar in bimanual stabilization, but the central mechanism and tested outcome are insertion/latching rather than controlled fracture and debris recovery.

comparisons.objective: Wait for a timer, visually read a thermometer, and physically enter the final reading on a calculator; candidate mechanically finishes four inserts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timing, visual instrument interpretation, and ordered key presses versus precision tool alignment, bimanual hammering, force control, and fragment pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Latest physical equals-key submission is 45 after the countdown; candidate requires four safe fractures and four tangs deposited with a stable final state.
comparisons.reason: Perception-and-recording is unrelated to impact fracture. The record provides unusually detailed timing and measured-state scoring, reinforcing the different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Move two open vials across a drip tray by hand-to-hand transfer and place them on pads; candidate removes and contains four metal tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual handoff of spill-sensitive open containers versus mandrel stabilization, controlled impact fracture, withdrawal, fragment search, and pickup.
comparisons.success_condition: Both vials cross over the tray and finish on pads without the unsafe transfer path implied by the task; candidate requires all tangs in a tray with no escape or damage.
comparisons.reason: Both emphasize containment and bimanual manipulation, but spill-safe vessel handoff does not test precision fracture, insert retention, or tiny-fragment recovery. Detailed spill thresholds are absent.

comparisons.objective: Feed a captive nut beneath channel lips; candidate breaks and retrieves four HELICOIL tangs from installed coils.
comparisons.physical_skill: From the title, constrained nut feeding and under-lip alignment versus coaxial mandrel placement, bimanual impact control, and loose-fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Available evidence reports a full-score demo but omits the nut's numeric seating rubric; candidate requires four fractures, retained inserts, and complete tang containment.
comparisons.reason: Even with missing rubric details, constrained insertion/feeding produces an assembled captive nut, whereas the candidate tests controlled sacrificial fracture and removal.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a split spacer around a captive shaft; candidate fractures and recovers four insert tangs.
comparisons.physical_skill: From the title, coordinating spacer halves around a constrained shaft versus aligning and stabilizing a narrow mandrel, hammering, and retrieving free fragments.
comparisons.success_condition: Available evidence reports a full-score demo but omits the spacer's engagement thresholds; candidate requires four contact-loaded fractures, all fragments deposited, and no damage.
comparisons.reason: Captive-shaft spacer assembly is a meaningfully different central outcome and mechanism from notch fracture and debris recovery, despite incomplete numeric rubric evidence.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures and recovers four HELICOIL tangs; record inspects concealed slider travel and marks the largest travel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel placement, stabilized hammer impact, and tiny-fragment recovery; record tests travel inspection and marking. No specs provide further rubric detail.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact-driven notch fractures, physical containment of all fragments, retained inserts, and no damage; record body only reports task/demo scores and does not state detailed success thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Inspection and marking of slider travel tests a meaningfully different ability from controlled insert-tang fracture and fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes installed threaded inserts by breaking and collecting their tangs; record finds the one open cooktop knob and turns it off.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate combines narrow-tool alignment, bimanual hammering, force regulation, and fragment handling; record requires visual control-state discrimination and knob rotation. No specs are available.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four valid fractures and contained fragments without insert or shell damage; record requires identifying and closing the incorrect knob, with no detailed numeric rubric given.
comparisons.reason: Rotary control-state correction neither fractures a manufactured notch nor tests loose-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks and recovers HELICOIL tangs in a shell; record carries a microscope using only its arm and base.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests precision impact tooling and fragment pickup; record tests safe bimanual support and transport while avoiding fragile forbidden grasp regions. Specs are absent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, containment, retention, and no damage; record title imposes safe grasp regions, but its body omits detailed placement and threshold criteria.
comparisons.reason: Safe transport by prescribed support points is different from contact-driven fracture at recessed inserts.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes insert tangs; record places a heat shield behind a copper joint before bringing a torch near it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammering, and fragment recovery; record requires protective-object placement and safe action ordering. Specs are absent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate scores physical fractures, fragment containment, and undamaged hardware; record evidence states only the shield-before-torch ordering, without numeric thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Safety sequencing and shield placement do not test controlled notch fracture or retention of a threaded coil.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures and collects four HELICOIL tangs; record aligns a structural splice with a drift and inserts two bolts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use a narrow alignment tool, but candidate stabilizes a mandrel during impact and recovers fractured fragments, whereas the record levers a plate into alignment and performs bolt insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact-loaded fractures with no coil/shell damage and all tangs contained; record requires aligned plate, two inserted bolts, and drift returned to its holder, with no additional specs.
comparisons.reason: The shared generic alignment primitive is insufficient for overlap: the central tested outcomes are fracture-and-recovery versus hole alignment and fastening.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes and contains insert tangs; record clears a paper-cutter bed and lowers the blade arm until its safety latch catches.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests precision impact, lateral-load control, and tiny-fragment collection; record tests clearing, articulated-arm operation, and latch engagement. Specs are absent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four valid fractures and an undamaged retained assembly; record requires a clear bed and latched blade arm, but detailed thresholds are not supplied.
comparisons.reason: Securing a cutter through an articulated latch tests a different mechanism and outcome from breaking sacrificial insert tangs.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes threaded inserts by tang removal; record identifies an n-type (100) wafer by its flats and mounts it face-down on a dicing-tape chuck.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses impact tooling and fragment recovery; record requires visual discrimination, tweezer handling, edge-standing, handoff/regrasp, orientation, centering, and vacuum activation.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, four contained tangs, retained inserts, and no damage; record requires the correct wafer centered with its primary flat aligned, face down, and vacuum on. No specs add thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Although both demand precision, wafer identification/reorientation and vacuum mounting do not test fracture, impact regulation, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks and retrieves insert tangs; record hangs a telescoping rack rail between two posts and latches it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial micro-tool alignment, bimanual hammering, and small-fragment pickup; record requires supporting a rail, peg insertion, telescopic extension, and latch engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures and contained fragments without hardware displacement; record requires front and rear pegs seated, rail latched, released, and arms returned. No specs are present.
comparisons.reason: Telescoping rail installation tests sustained support, extension, and latching rather than sacrificial-feature fracture and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes four HELICOIL tangs; record swaps a dust filter beneath a spring-shut cover.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests aligned impact and fragment recovery; record requires one arm to hold a spring-loaded pedal while the other removes, bins, and inserts filters.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires valid fractures, containment, retention, and no damage; record requires dirty-filter disposal, new-filter seating, cover closure, and arm retreat. No specs add numeric tolerances.
comparisons.reason: The shared bimanual coordination is generic; spring-cover management and filter replacement test different physical outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes inserts by breaking and collecting tangs; record opens a sealed desiccator and removes a sample vial.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires narrow-tool alignment, controlled hammer impact, and tiny-fragment search; record requires seal/lid manipulation, careful sample extraction, and lid placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained fractures and an undamaged shell/coil assembly; record requires vial placement on a tray, lid on a pad, and an unmoved desiccator, with no further specs.
comparisons.reason: Opening a sealed vessel and transporting a sample does not test manufactured-notch fracture or insert retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes sacrificial tangs from installed inserts; record assembles and secures a gel-casting cassette.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial impact tooling and loose-fragment recovery; record tests glass-plate alignment, pressure-cam closure, assembly transfer, spring-clip release, and stable insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, four tangs in a tray, retained inserts, and no damage; record requires secured aligned plates, cassette seated in its stand, clip released, and stable gripper withdrawal. Specs are absent.
comparisons.reason: Cassette clamping and transfer have no fracture or fragment-recovery outcome despite both requiring alignment and force care.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures insert tangs; record plastically bends a straight steel bar into a rectangular stirrup.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate delivers localized impact through a coaxial mandrel and recovers fragments; record indexes a bar between chalk marks and swings a bending lever for three same-direction right-angle bends.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four notch fractures without insert/shell damage and containment of all fragments; record requires an 80 × 50 mm rectangular stirrup with meeting ends, while reverse bending is scrap. No specs are provided.
comparisons.reason: Both involve irreversible material change, but controlled tang separation and recovery test a different mechanism and end state from sequential bulk plastic bending.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes and contains HELICOIL tangs; record rolls maki with a bamboo mat and leaves it seam-side down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires micro-alignment, hammer impact control, and fragment pickup; record requires coordinated mat wrapping, compliant-food shaping, seam orientation, and mat opening.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures, retained inserts, and four contained tangs; record requires a completed seam-down roll, opened flat mat, and release. No specs add thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Compliant wrapping and shaping are materially different from rigid contact-driven fracture and metal-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks and retrieves insert tangs; record backs a springy trim panel while pressing a clip home.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require bimanual stabilization and controlled force, but candidate stabilizes a coaxial mandrel during hammer impact and collects fragments, while the record supports a compliant panel and seats a detent clip.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures with insert retention, no damage, and fragment containment; record requires clip seating while panel sag stays at or below 3 mm, followed by withdrawal.
comparisons.reason: The record's central outcome is supported clip insertion; the candidate's is sacrificial-notch fracture plus free-fragment recovery. Shared force coordination alone does not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes inserts through tang fracture; record performs manual blood-pressure measurement on a training arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses aligned impact tooling and fragment recovery; record coordinates cuff pumping, controlled bleed-down, stethoscope placement, and pressure/auditory monitoring.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contained fractures without equipment damage; record requires pressure above 160 mmHg, continuous listening while descending past 100 mmHg at 2–4 mmHg/s, full deflation, and release.
comparisons.reason: Timed pneumatic measurement and sensing test a different ability from impact fracture and retention-sensitive manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes four insert tangs; record unlocks an over-centre strut at its knee and stows a radiator panel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel placement, hammering, and fragment pickup; record requires mechanism unlocking, controlled panel folding, and placement on supports.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures, contained tangs, and undamaged retained inserts; record requires the panel folded onto its rest pads and released. No specs provide further tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Over-centre linkage release and panel stowage do not test fracture or recovery of sacrificial metal features.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes threaded inserts; record moves a loaded pallet into a bay and parks a pallet jack safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests precision micro-tool alignment, impact regulation, and fragment collection; record tests large articulated vehicle steering, pumping/lowering, and handle positioning. Specs are absent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and physical containment with no damage; record title requires pallet placement, fully lowered forks, and upright parked handle, but detailed thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Material handling and safe jack parking are clearly unrelated to controlled insert-tang fracture.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks and retrieves HELICOIL tangs; record composes and sends a product photograph while excluding confidential information.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests physical tool alignment, hammering, and fragment pickup; record tests camera viewpoint composition, object presentation, and physical button activation. Specs are absent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures and all fragments contained without damage; record requires complete, sufficiently large mug visibility and permanently fails if the unit-cost panel appears.
comparisons.reason: Privacy-aware visual composition and capture have no shared central manipulation mechanism or outcome with insert finishing.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes tangs from already-installed threaded inserts; record evens wire tips and twists a connector clockwise until snug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed coaxial mandrel alignment, stabilized impact, and fragment recovery; record requires wire-end alignment, connector placement, axial stabilization, and controlled twisting.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four contact-loaded fractures, retained coils, and four contained fragments; record requires even wire tips and a snug clockwise-installed connector, with no detailed thresholds or specs.
comparisons.reason: Although both operate near small threaded/helical hardware, the record tests joining wires by rotational fastening, not breaking a sacrificial notch and recovering fragments.

comparisons.objective: Candidate fractures and collects insert tangs; record flattens a curling poster under two weights.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate uses precision impact tooling and millimetre-scale fragment recovery; record requires drawing out compliant curled ends, holding tension, and placing weights bimanually.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four valid fractures, retained inserts, no damage, and tang containment; record requires both ends flat and weighted, release, and arm retreat. No specs add thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Compliant sheet flattening under weights tests sustained tension and placement, not impact fracture or fragment handling.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes insert tangs; record flips a pancake in a pan using a turner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial mandrel stabilization, hammer blows, and small-fragment pickup; record requires pan stabilization, turner insertion under an edge, lifting, and controlled inversion.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures with all tangs contained and hardware undamaged; record requires the pancake inverted in the pan, turner returned, pan released, and arms retreated. Specs are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tool-under-edge inversion of a compliant food item tests a different ability and outcome from notch fracture and recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes installed coils by tang removal; record centers a block in a four-jaw chuck.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial impact tooling and loose-fragment collection; record requires block placement and iterative adjustment of opposing jaw pairs to center and secure it.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four fractures, fragment containment, insert retention, and no damage; record requires a centered, held block and arm retreat, but supplies no numeric centering tolerance or specs.
comparisons.reason: Iterative chuck centering and clamping do not test sacrificial-feature fracture, impact regulation, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Candidate breaks and recovers HELICOIL tangs; record assembles a flute and aligns its embouchure hole with the keys.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed tool alignment, bimanual hammering, and fragment pickup; record requires bimanual cylindrical insertion, axial seating, rotational alignment, and gentle placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four valid fractures with retained undamaged inserts and all tangs contained; record requires full tenon insertion, correct angular alignment, keys-up placement on the case lid, and arm retreat.
comparisons.reason: The record tests insertion plus rotational registration; the candidate explicitly tests contact-driven fracture and containment, so shared coaxial alignment is only a generic primitive.

comparisons.objective: Candidate removes four insert tangs; record cuts a pizza into quarters.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use bimanual support and force application, but candidate stabilizes a mandrel for localized hammer impact and recovers fragments, while the record steadies a board and rolls a cutter along two crossing paths.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four modeled-notch fractures, four contained tangs, retained inserts, and no damage; record requires two through-center cuts yielding quarters, wheel return, and arm retreat. No specs add numeric cut thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Continuous rolling cuts through bulk food and localized brittle separation at manufactured metal notches are meaningfully different tested mechanisms; the candidate also uniquely requires fragment recovery and coil retention.

comparisons.objective: Candidate finishes threaded inserts by tang fracture; record installs and tensions a replacement hacksaw blade in the correct tooth direction.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires coaxial narrow-tool placement, bimanual hammering, force regulation, and tiny-fragment collection; record requires flexible blade alignment over two pins, orientation discrimination, and wing-nut tensioning. Specs are absent.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires four clean fractures, four tangs physically contained, retained inserts, and no damage; record title requires both pins engaged, teeth facing away from the handle, and blade tensioned, but detailed thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Oriented blade mounting and tensioning test flexible-part alignment and fastening, not controlled notch fracture or free-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Drive a piston through a ring compressor into a bore while holding the compressor against the engine deck.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual fixture stabilization, coaxial piston alignment, and sustained insertion force; no impact-fracture or fragment recovery.
comparisons.success_condition: Piston passes through the held compressor into the bore. The record supplies no numeric seating, damage, or retention rubric.
comparisons.reason: Both require coaxial tool-part alignment and bimanual stabilization, but the tested outcomes differ materially: constrained piston insertion versus contact-driven notch fracture followed by recovery of four free tangs without coil or shell damage.

comparisons.objective: Wet a dry pitcher-pump leather seal with a priming cup, then stroke the handle until water flows.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled pouring followed by repeated articulated handle operation and fluid-state management.
comparisons.success_condition: Water flows after priming and pumping. No numeric flow, spill, stroke, or final-state thresholds are provided.
comparisons.reason: This tests fluid priming and cyclic pumping, not coaxial mandrel placement, controlled impact fracture, retained-insert protection, or small-fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Place drill-core pieces into a tray in reading order and insert a core-loss block at the missing interval.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential grasping, orientation, ordered packing, and semantic placement of a loss marker.
comparisons.success_condition: Core is boxed in the required order with the loss block in the correct position. Placement tolerances and damage rules are absent.
comparisons.reason: Ordered specimen packing is materially different from bimanual impact-tool use, notch fracture, and physical recovery of released metal fragments.

comparisons.objective: Make four guarded mandoline strokes, extract the slice tray, and return both arms while avoiding the blade.
comparisons.physical_skill: One hand stabilizes the mandoline while the other performs repeated guarded sliding; blade-clearance safety and tray extraction are required.
comparisons.success_condition: Four down-and-back strokes, guard left at the top, slice tray removed, arms returned, and no gripper near the blade. Numeric clearance and slice-quality details are absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both are bimanual tool tasks with damage hazards, guarded reciprocating slicing does not test coaxial mandrel stabilization, discrete impact fracture, insert retention, or free-fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Stand two bridges at marked positions so a tensioned cord rests in both notches while its weight hangs freely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place and balance supports under tension, align cord to notches, and release without collapse.
comparisons.success_condition: Both bridges stand at the marks, support the cord in their notches, and leave the weight free. Numeric pose and stability thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: This tests support placement under a tensioned cord, not impact delivery through a narrow aligned mandrel, controlled fracture, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Lift and rapidly invert a full water bottle neck-down onto a cooler crown using both hands.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual heavy-object handling, dynamic inversion, neck-to-crown alignment, and spill avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle is mounted neck-down on the cooler. The record gives no alignment, spill, timing, or stability thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic container inversion and seating are different tested abilities from localized impact fracture with a stabilized mandrel and subsequent millimetre-scale fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Lay a cover bar over a cable at the marked walkway crossing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid-object placement and planar/angular alignment over a cable.
comparisons.success_condition: Cover must rest flat, within 15° of cable direction and 1.9 cm of its centerline; full credit additionally requires 1.5 cm cable and 2 cm walkway-depth tolerances.
comparisons.reason: This is tolerance-based cover placement; it lacks bimanual striking, contact-loaded fracture, protected retained hardware, and loose-fragment collection.

comparisons.objective: Tip a full-width pan so aggregate feeds all 12 riffle-splitter chutes evenly.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual pan support, level-lip control, controlled granular pouring, and distribution regulation.
comparisons.success_condition: All 12 chutes receive an even feed. Numeric evenness, spill, and residual-material thresholds are not stated.
comparisons.reason: Granular-flow distribution tests coordinated pouring, whereas the candidate tests precise mandrel alignment, controlled impact fracture, and containment of four discrete fragments.

comparisons.objective: Release a guitar capo from the fourth fret and reclamp it at the second fret to transpose G shapes to A.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reason over fret position, operate a spring clamp, relocate it, and avoid dragging while clamped.
comparisons.success_condition: Capo is released and clamped at the second fret; dragging it while clamped scores zero. Pose and clamping thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Clamp relocation and musical-semantic reasoning do not test impact mechanics, fracture at a manufactured notch, insert retention, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Move an open bound volume into an imaging cradle while respecting its opening limit.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual support of a delicate articulated object, controlled opening, and placement onto four bearing strips with binding clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Volume is supported at four strips, binding remains clear, opening limit is respected, and both hands are released. Numeric limits are not provided.
comparisons.reason: Delicate cradle placement is materially different from stabilizing a narrow mandrel during hammer impact and recovering released tangs.

comparisons.objective: Select one M4 × 20 mm screw from alternatives and place it alone in a handoff tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Size-based part identification, small-fastener singulation, grasping, and tray placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one requested screw lies in the tray within 4 mm of its floor; multiple screws score zero.
comparisons.reason: The shared small-part handling primitive is generic. This task tests selection and singulation, not contact-driven fracture, coil protection, or recovery of fragments created by the operation.

comparisons.objective: Close a clamshell lockout around a valve lever and slide a steel lock bar through both holes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Articulated enclosure closure, two-hole alignment, bar insertion, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Clamshell encloses the lever and the bar rests through both holes after release. Numeric closure, insertion-depth, and stability thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: This tests latching and aligned bar insertion, not bimanual impact through a mandrel, notch fracture, retained-insert safety, or fragment containment.

comparisons.objective: Hold a carton steady while inserting a divider into mounting slots.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual carton stabilization, slot alignment, compliant sheet insertion, and depth control.
comparisons.success_condition: Divider must seat within 2 mm of target depth; setup and scoring fields are otherwise explicitly missing.
comparisons.reason: Despite shared bimanual stabilization and alignment, divider insertion tests seating a compliant planar part, not impact-induced fracture and recovery of independently simulated tangs.

comparisons.objective: Place remaining objects into a box after a human has packed selected items.
comparisons.physical_skill: Collaborative-state interpretation, object grasping, and collision-aware packing around existing contents.
comparisons.success_condition: Remaining objects are packed after the human's choices; setup and scoring fields are explicitly missing.
comparisons.reason: Collaborative box packing does not exercise coaxial tool control, hammer-force regulation, fracture, retained-coil protection, or fragment recovery.

comparisons.objective: Push a partly filled bottle to a line without tipping it excessively.
comparisons.physical_skill: Nonprehensile pushing with center-of-mass and slosh-aware stability control.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle reaches the line without exceeding 30° tilt; setup and scoring fields are otherwise explicitly missing.
comparisons.reason: Stable nonprehensile transport of a liquid container is unrelated to precise impact-tool coordination and post-fracture containment.

comparisons.objective: Remove two loose metal discs from a harness board, then route a cable along a marked line with its plug in an outline.
comparisons.physical_skill: FOD pickup and binning followed by deformable cable routing; cable must not contact remaining debris.
comparisons.success_condition: Both discs are in the red bin and the cable follows the line with its plug in the endpoint outline; routing tolerances are absent.
comparisons.reason: This shares physical debris collection, but its central ability is pre-existing FOD clearance plus cable routing. The candidate must first create fragments through controlled coaxial impact while preserving inserts, then recover all four; that is a meaningfully different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Place two ballast blocks so the combined payload-deck center of mass lies over a center mark.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mass-based reasoning, planar block placement, and balance control.
